text: About Adroit Backup Utility Top About Adroit Backup Utility How to Use this Adroit Backup Utility The Adroit Backup Utility makes it possible to create a complete backup of your Adroit installation. This should be used to protect your Adroit installation from corruption or possible accidental deletion and also provides an easy way for transferring an Adroit project or system to another computer. This consists of the following 4 sections, which can be enabled or disabled according to your needs: Adroit installation files : backs up the files required by the Adroit application. Adroit data files : backs up the files required by your Adroit projects, where multiple file locations can be specified. Event Logs : ONLY exports the application; security and system event logs files. These event log files CANNOT be restored but can be viewed. Adroit registry : backs up both the global Adroit registry settings and the Adroit registry settings specific to the current user. Once the back up has been appropriately configured, click the Backup now button to execute the back up. The Backup path , allows you to specify where these Adroit backups are to be stored . The Overwrite option determines if

n appropriately configured, click the Backup now button to execute the back up. The Backup path , allows you to specify where these Adroit backups are to be stored . The Overwrite option determines if previous backups are preserved or overwritten , affecting the structure of the saved backup directory . The Adroit Backup Utility makes use of profiles to store different backup configuration settings for later reuse and as these profiles can be executed from the command-line , Adroit backups are also able to be scheduled or run from a batch file. The Set defaults button can be used to save the configured backup settings as the Default profile settings, this is recommended if the current settings are to be frequently used. On exit the currently configured settings are saved to the currently selected profile . -->

About Adroit Database Files (Agent Storage) Top About Adroit Database Files (Agent Storage) The Agent Server is a collection or container of the supported agent types and stores and manages the instances of their created agents, by providing consistent mechanisms for creating and destroying agents and accessing the information contained within them. Each agent type is a Windows Dynamic Link Library (.DLL) file in the Adroit system folder, which is loaded when the Agent Server starts up, making its functionality available for use. The Adroit database (.WGP) file or load file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server. This includes every agent that has been added to the current project of this Agent Server, with the exception of the agents that are automatically created or dynamic agents like Proxy and Scan agents. Note: For this reason it essential that this Adroit database (.WGP) file is frequently backed up. For details, see Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files . About Adroit Projects Top About Adroit Projects A project in Adroit , is the default mechanism for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, if Agent Server A and Agent Server B have the SAME project name (and are in the same network domain), then Agent Server A is able to refer to agents within Agent Server B and vice verse. For further details of how Adroit projects work and their limitations and the other mechanisms that are provided to overcome these limitations, see Agent Server Connection Methods . Note: Proxy agents are automatically created when an Agent Server accesses an agent that exists in a remote Agent Server. This provides client applications with a transparent mechanism for accessing agents, so that a distributed agent database acts as a standalone database. In other words, even though a Classic UI connects to a single Agent Server, one or its mimics or pictures can display agents that exist on a remote Agent Server. All Agent Servers need to specify a project name whether they are standalone (a single Agent Server on one computer) or distributed (requiring more than one Agent Server)

ist on a remote Agent Server. All Agent Servers need to specify a project name whether they are standalone (a single Agent Server on one computer) or distributed (requiring more than one Agent Server). While it is essential that each Agent Server has a unique name, project names should only be the same for those Agent Server that are required to communicate to one another. Configure the required Project and Agent Server name in the Agent Server Configuration page of the Adroit Configuration utility. A number of other configuration requirements must be met before a distributed project can be created. For details, see Requirements for Distributed Agent Servers . Tip: According to the best practices the Adroit Software should always be separated from the configured project(s), for this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created. For details, see Best Practices . Note: It is important to create a backup procedure to guarantee disaster avoidance rather than just disaster recovery and also to provide an easy way for transferring an Adroit project or system to another computer. For details, see About Backup Procedures . -->

About Agent Data (Slots) Top About Agent Data (Slots) Each agent (instance of an agent type) maintains its own unique set of data and is referred to by its own unique agent name. For details, see About Agents or Naming Agents . Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, which are referred to as agent attributes. Most of these attributes are accessible to clients of the Agent Server as slots of the agent. Slots can therefore be defined as externally accessible attributes of an agent. For details, see Accessing Agent Slots . For instance, the Analog agent slot has a hiHi slot that allows a value to be assigned that represents the high-high alarm limit for an analog signal. There are clearly different types of data that need to be stored in an agent. For example, the name, is an ASCII string, whereas the hiHi limit, referred to above, is a floating point Real number value, and the state of a Digital is a Boolean TRUE/FALSE indication. This implies the concept of slot type , as well as agent type. For details, see Slot Types . An Adroit configuration is therefore made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. Each

, as well as agent type. For details, see Slot Types . An Adroit configuration is therefore made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. Each agent, in turn, contains externally accessible data attributes, or slots, whose type corresponds to one of the supported slot types. For details of the available slots for each agent type, see Agent Type Slot Reference . An agent's "state", at any instant in time, is defined as the collective values of all its data. Agents have both generic and type-specific data. For details, see Data Structure of an Agent . Note: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . -->

About Agent Servers Top About Agent Servers The Agent Server is the storage facility for all real time and historical data. The real time data resides within intelligent objects, known as agents, which exchange messages with other agents or picture objects either from their local host computer or from remote computer nodes elsewhere on the network. Historical data is written to disk where it is available for rapid retrieval and on-line analysis. Note: Redundancy can be provided by configuring the Agent Server as a cluster server, which is a set of two Agent Servers running a replicated database. For details, see About Active Clustering and Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . Agents are described as intelligent because they store live data as well as providing methods of manipulating that data. Agents can be both clients and servers at the same time, by operating on, and being operated upon, by other agents. For details, see About Agents . The interaction of the agents with each other as well as with the Classic User Interface and its picture objects, provides a powerful and dynamic monitoring and control capability which reflects the status of your process

agents with each other as well as with the Classic User Interface and its picture objects, provides a powerful and dynamic monitoring and control capability which reflects the status of your process in real-time. For further details, see What you can do in Adroit . Agents are classified by function into a number of agent types, which can be used to implement a wide variety of system related, as well as application-specific tasks. For details, see About Agent Types . Note: An instance of an agent type is usually referred to as an agent. The Agent Server is therefore a collection or container of the supported agent types and stores and manages the instances of their created agents, in an agent database (.WGP) file. For further details regarding the storage of agents, see About Adroit Database Files (Agent Storage) . Note: The Agent Server is the only component in Adroit that needs to be licensed. For details, see Adroit Licensing . Adroit OEMs, distributors, and even power end-users can create their own custom agent types programmatically by using the Adroit agent interface. However, it is also possible to use the Custom agent type and its associated Custom Agent Designer utility. F

create their own custom agent types programmatically by using the Adroit agent interface. However, it is also possible to use the Custom agent type and its associated Custom Agent Designer utility. For details, see How to Use the Custom Agent Designer . Due to the way in which Adroit has been designed, there are no theoretical limits to the number of different agents that can be contained within an Agent Server. In addition, multiple Agent Servers can be distributed across many physical computers, in a local or wide area network, by using the concept of a Project. For this reason, the total number of agents that can exist in an Adroit installation is effectively unlimited. For further details concerning Projects in Adroit , see About Adroit Projects . Furthermore, because 32 bit Windows supports multi-threaded applications, Adroit Agent Servers can concurrently interact with as many client workstations as may be required. This feature is facilitated by Adroit agent level locking which ensures orderly access to any instance of an agent. ensures orderly access to any instance of an agent. The Agent Server is typically configured by means of the Configurator dialog in the Classic UI or by means of the Project Explorer. For details, see Configuring the Agent Server or The Project Explorer . Adroit Agent Servers, provide two basic methods of accessing the data within agents: The first allows a user to get a data value from or put a data value into an agent. About Agent Types Top About Agent Types Adroit configurations are composed of intelligent, cooperating objects known as agents . For details, see About Agents . These agents are differentiated into different types to provide specific information storage and manipulation mechanisms, with their intended function determining their complexity. By default, these agent types are further separated into the following categories to better facilitate the selection of the required agent when designing your system, as follows: Basic : these agent types form the basic building blocks of a system and are used for gathering, handling and processing data to and from the physical external world. Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, MultiState, String, StringList, Timer Advanced : these agent types provide powerful SCADA and integration functionality that allow the Basic agents to be alarmed and logged to databases and provides various means of reporting and/or controlling their values. Accumulator, AgentGroup, Alarm, Alarm List, AlarmManagement, ARec, Command, DbAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Recipe, Scheduler, Script, Shift, Statistical MIS/MES : thes

MaxDemand, OEE, PID IT : these agent types facilitate the integration and management of SCADA and IT Audit, DumpConfig, ICMP, Perfmon, SNMPMgr System : these agent types are used internally to perform certain SCADA and other specific functions. Note: Instances of these Agents are created automatically and cannot be added manually by the user. Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan, SystemDataLog, SystemInformation Primitive : these agent types are primitive because they offer limited value and are limited in functionality when compared to the Basic agents, they are essentially single value containers. About Agents Top About Agents The Agent Server is the storage facility for all agents. For details, see About Agent Servers . Agents are called agents because, instead of only containing data, like simple database records, they also usually contain the ability to operate or act on their own data, driving its values and to read and write to other objects, and so influence them. This concept is very much in line with object-oriented thinking, and is primarily why we refer to Adroit as being "object-oriented". Note: When referring to a data value within an agent this is often referred to as a tag. For details, see Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values . Agents are classified by function into a number of agent types, which can be used to implement a wide variety of system related, as well as application-specific tasks. For details, see About Agent Types . For example, the Analog agent type is used to handle the signal conditioning and alarm checking requirements of a process variable, and the DataLog agent type is responsible for creating, maintaining, and accessing historical data logs. An agent is therefore, more correctly, an instance of an agent type, for example an inst

iable, and the DataLog agent type is responsible for creating, maintaining, and accessing historical data logs. An agent is therefore, more correctly, an instance of an agent type, for example an instance of the Analog agent type could be the TANKLEVEL Analog agent (assuming that this agent has been created by a user). Each of these agent types have well defined rules for interfacing with other agents ensuring that an extremely robust and versatile environment has been created to handle any real world situation. For this reason each Adroit agent can be dynamically configured to benefit from specific functions provided by other agent types, such as scanning ( Communicating Values ), alarming ( Alarming Values ) and logging ( Logging values ). The interaction of these agents with each other as well as with the Classic User Interface and its picture objects, provides a powerful and dynamic monitoring and control capability which reflects the status of your process in real-time. For each agent type, there may be zero, one or many agent instances. Each time you add an agent, you are creating a new agent instance, however, agent instances are simply referred to as agents. About Alarm Acknowledgement Top About Alarm Acknowledgement Acknowledgment is typically recommended for alarms or incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). that require some sort of reaction or attention from the operator. In other words, an alarm should be any event that an operator must understand, acknowledge and respond to – and not simply acknowledge and ignore. Therefore you should carefully consider, which incidents require acknowledgement and which do not. Adroit provides the following methods of acknowledging alarms: Global acknowledgement: This should be used when using a standalone Adroit installation or for those alarms that only one operator needs to be made aware of. By globally acknowledging an alarm from any computer in the network, this incident will be removed from ALL the lists in the system (provided, of course, that the alarm is no longer active). Local acknowledgement: This should be used when you have alarms that more that one operator needs to be aware of. Click for mor

in the system (provided, of course, that the alarm is no longer active). Local acknowledgement: This should be used when you have alarms that more that one operator needs to be aware of. Click for more details: In other words you have a distributed Adroit installation, with operators viewing the process from remote user interfaces. Local acknowledge refers to the action of acknowledging an alarm in an alarm list of an AlarmList agent. This removes the alarm from this alarm list, provided the alarm is no longer active. If the alarm is routed to other alarm lists (usually on other computers), locally acknowledging the alarm one alarm list will not clear the alarm from these other alarm lists. This method therefore requires that each operator locally (remotely) acknowledges the alarm, to remove it from their alarm list (once it is no longer active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. ). Note1: In the case of local alarm acknowledgement, you need to use the AlarmList agent to contain these incidents and NOT the Alarm agent. About Alarm Management Top About Alarm Management Alarm management is concerned with improving the QUALITY of the information within the alarming configuration. This information should be used to reduce the QUANTITY of nuisance alarms (red herrings) so that only the most important and relevant alarms are displayed for your process. In other words, alarm management can counteract inefficient alarming. Up to now SCADA installations have used numerous alarms, each of which usually have very little awareness of the other alarms in the system. So generally each incident generates a flood of alarms, which operators simply ignore because there are too many to deal with. According to the EEMUA 191 guidelines a document created by the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association ( EEMUA) of alarm management guidelines, developed by the users of alarm systems, and is the globally accepted and leading guide to good practice for alarm management. : An alarm is an incident that an operator must understand, acknowledge and respond to – not simply acknowledge and ignore. For further details, see Effective Alarm Characteristics . No process should have more than 6 such alarm occurrences an

must understand, acknowledge and respond to – not simply acknowledge and ignore. For further details, see Effective Alarm Characteristics . No process should have more than 6 such alarm occurrences an hour during normal operations. Under abnormal process conditions no more than 10 alarms per minute should occur. Your SCADA installation requires an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. In this case fewer alarms are more effective as the human mind can only focus on a few things at a time. About Alarm Management Top The Why and How of Alarm Management in Adroit Why is alarm management needed? In the past alarms were hardwired into the panels, which limited their number; now that alarms are software-driven, means that you can have an unlimited number of alarms. In an effort to keep the operators sufficiently informed, SCADA installations typically use lots of alarms, each of which usually have very little awareness of the other alarms in the system. This means that each incident can generate a flood of alarms, which causes operators to become overloaded and confused and as a result they may even start ignoring alarms! Therefore LESS alarms are MORE effective. Alarm management is concerned with improving the QUALITY of the information within the alarming configuration. This information should be used to reduce the QUANTITY of nuisance alarms (red herrings) so that only the most important and relevant alarms are displayed for your process. In other words alarm management counteracts inefficient alarming by allowing you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. The following procedure describes the recommen

unteracts inefficient alarming by allowing you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. The following procedure describes the recommended method of using the AlarmManagement agent to configure and record your active incidents so that you can analyse this information to improve your alarming configuration. What is an incident? In Adroit, Alarm agents can monitor other agents for preset conditions or states. So that when a monitored condition occurs in an agent its Alarm agent uses predefined reporting methods to alert the necessary people and/or applications. That is why Alarming in Adroit primarily involves the configuration of the following two things: The preset conditions or states of each agent that you need to alarm, known as alarm types, which each constitute a separate alarm or event. The alarm routes that specify which alarm destinations (reporting mechanisms) you need to use to communicate the generated alarms and events to the necessary personnel and/or applications. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). . An Alarm agent can use one or more alarm routes to specify which alarm destinations to send the active incidents of the agents that it is monitoring. About Alarm Types Top About Alarm Types An alarm type is simply the required condition or state of an agent that you need to alarm. This can also contain a list of slots of this agent, which are reported when the alarm occurs. In Adroit , each agent drives the following status bits: These status bits are divided into the following categories: Common Status Bits , which indicate their internal status (or integrity) and are common to all agents. For instance, these can indicate failures within the Adroit system itself. Specific Status Bits , which indicate the status of the values driven by or contained in the agent and are specific to each agent type. For instance, these can indicate plant upsets or process variable excursions. Each alarm type requires two of the following three components: specify which of these status bits must be simultaneously enabled or disabled and provide a descriptive name for the specified condition, this usually takes the form of a descriptive abbreviation. text: About Backup Procedures Top About Backup Procedures It is important to create a backup procedure to guarantee disaster avoidance rather than just disaster recovery and also to provide an easy way for transferring an Adroit project or system to another computer. Hence, this backup procedure should include all the files utilised during plant operation and include storage facilities as well as locations, since critical data should be stored in an alternative location, such as a drive or remote hard disk etc. For these reasons it is recommended to use the System Backup and Restore facility provided by the Adroit Config Editor utility to execute and manage such a backup procedure. For details, see System Backup and Restore. Note: This requires you to have installed SmartUI . The backup process generates a single compressed file in the specified location, which contains the date and time of its creation, which contains all the relevant registry settings and all the files and folders containing the user-configuration of the currently specified Configuration. When restoring, you can restore between x86 and x64 operating system architectures and across different operating system language se

ng the user-configuration of the currently specified Configuration. When restoring, you can restore between x86 and x64 operating system architectures and across different operating system language sets. However, any file paths within the agent database (.wgp) file are not currently converted and still need to be manually edited after restoring the project. This backup includes the following files and settings: Adroit data files . This will backup up the files required by your Adroit projects, where multiple file locations can be specified. WGP files, provide two features to assist with their regular backup. For details, see Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files . WARNING! These features are merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! Event Logs . This will ONLY export the application; security and system event logs files. These event log files CANNOT be restored but can be viewed by using the Event Viewer. Adroit registry. This will backup both the global Adroit registry settings and the Adroit registry settings specific to the current user. This will contain the Adroit confi

by using the Event Viewer. Adroit registry. This will backup both the global Adroit registry settings and the Adroit registry settings specific to the current user. This will contain the Adroit configuration, workspaces and Adroit protocol driver configuration settings. -->

About Filtering Prioritised Incidents Top About Filtering Prioritised Incidents One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance. Since some alarms are critical, whereas others are more informational in nature. Once you have prioritised your incidents, Adroit provides the following ways to filter your incidents, based on their priority: You can configure the priority level of each Alarm agent to discard any alarm that has a LOWER priority level. In this way you can to filter out the alarms of less important or less critical agents. WARNING! This method REMOVES the lower prioritised alarms so that they are NOT REPORTED. This method should ONLY be used during times of process upheaval or when alarm flooding occurs (this is indicative of a badly configured alarm configuration). To set the alarm priority filter of an Alarm Agent: Any incident that has a LOWER priority is DISCARDED by the Alarm agent and is as if this alarm did not exist at all. Edit the required Alarm agent. Select the General tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Specify the LOWEST incident priority level in the Priority Filter edit box of t

this alarm did not exist at all. Edit the required Alarm agent. Select the General tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Specify the LOWEST incident priority level in the Priority Filter edit box of the General dialog as follows: 0: lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 0, which means that ALL alarms are dealt with. Click the OK button. Note: The EventLogging agent can also EXCLUDE events from agents based on their configured Alarm Priority. You can let your Alarm agents process ALL the active incidents (their default setting) and then use the priorities of the incidents to filter out the unnecessary incidents. For instance the Alarm List Viewer windows are able to filter incidents by specifying the required range of priorities. For details, see Row Filtering Configuration for Alarm Windows. Note: Adroit also provides the Filter Group setting, which is specified in the header of each agent and is typically used to denote different plant areas, so that the alarms can be filtered per plant area. For details on how to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance, see Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities . -->

About Power Factor Top About Power Factor The importance of the power factor lies in the fact that electricity providers supply customers with volt-amperes, but bill them for watts. Power factors below 1.0 require an electricity provider to generate more than the minimum volt-amperes necessary to supply the real power (watts). Since this increases the electricity provider’s generation and transmission costs, they may charge additional costs to customers who have a power factor below some limit. In other words, most electric billing is done in kilowatt-hours, which is determined by the following equation: Kilowatt-hours = (Volts * Amperes) * power factor * run time If we assume that the run time, volts, and kilowatt-hours are constant, then as the power factor decreases the amperage must rise to compensate. The converse is also true, if the power factor is raised for a load, then the amperage is reduced. For this reason, by adjusting the power factor of a system to very near unity, you ONLY pay for the power that you use. A good power factor is considered to be greater than 0.85. To understand the power factor is more detail, it is necessary to know that the following three types of

ONLY pay for the power that you use. A good power factor is considered to be greater than 0.85. To understand the power factor is more detail, it is necessary to know that the following three types of power are used to describe energy flow in an alternating current (A.C.) electrical system: Real power is the actual power that is being used or the ability of the system to perform work and is measured in watts (kW). Apparent power is the power that the system seems to be using, being the product of the current and voltage of the circuit and is therefore measured in volt-amperes (kVA). Reactive power is ‘invisible’ or wattless power, in which energy stored in the load is returned to the source and is measured in kVAR, which stands for volt-amperes-reactive. The power factor of an alternating current (A.C.) electrical system is simply the ratio of the real power to the apparent power and is a number between 0 and 1. The following ‘power triangle’ describes the relationship between these three types of power: Therefore, from this power triangle the following can be seen: When there is no reactive power element, such as for a purely resistive load (i.e. heating elements, incandescent lig

ree types of power: Therefore, from this power triangle the following can be seen: When there is no reactive power element, such as for a purely resistive load (i.e. heating elements, incandescent lighting, etc.) then the actual and the apparent power are the same i.e. there is no reactive power and so the power factor is 1. When a reactive power element exists then the apparent power can be greater than the real power component, which decreases the power factor. This reactive power element can be generated by: Inductive loads such as transformers and motors (any type of wound coil) generate reactive power with current waveform lagging the voltage Capacitive loads such as capacitor banks or buried cable generate reactive power with current phase leading the voltage. It is often possible to adjust the power factor of a system to very near unity. This practice is known as power factor correction and is achieved by switching in or out banks of inductors or capacitors. For example the inductive effect of motor loads may be offset by locally connected capacitors and vice verse. For further details, see: Wikipedia, Power factor , http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_factor (as of May. 28,

About SNMP Top About SNMP The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a trouble-free network management tool that can monitor and manage of diverse range of devices on a computer network, such as routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. Any SNMP network management system requires the following components: A manager, which is responsible for managing and monitoring SNMP devices, by performing the required network management functions. Note: Any computer or terminal running a SNMP manager is known as a Network Management Station (the NMS). An agent (NOT to be confused with an Adroit Agent or tag-type), which is simply a piece of software running on a device that is required to be managed. This agent is responsible for retrieving and setting management data, known as managed objects, for its device. Note: Any device that does not have an agent is referred to as being unmanageable. These SNMP managed objects might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and so on, that directly relate to the current operation of the device in question. For details, see SNMP Managed Objects . -->

About the AlarmManagement Database Top About the AlarmManagement Database The OLE DB compatible database specified by an AlarmManagement agent is the repository of all the logged incidents. This database allows you to obtain reports and KPIs focused around delivering a clear set of information on which the operators can act. The AlarmManagement agent provides the View Data and View Graph dialogs to allow users to analyse the data contained in its database. However, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. For this reason, it is necessary to know the structure of the tables within the OLE DB database that the AlarmManagement agent populates. This database records all the incidents including the time of incident, time of acknowledgement and time the incident cleared. IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of th

anagement database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. Each incident is logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent, so that it is possible to unify your alarm management for your enterprise and have more than one AlarmManagement agent log incidents to the SAME database. In this case please ensure that your AlarmManagement agent are uniquely named. The two primary tables in this database are the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents and Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents tables, which store all the logged incidents. An important field in these tables is the IncidentID field, which uniquely identifies each incident in this database. So by querying an entry in this field you can find out ALL the information pertaining

important field in these tables is the IncidentID field, which uniquely identifies each incident in this database. So by querying an entry in this field you can find out ALL the information pertaining to a specific alarm/event, such as every time this incident has been logged. ALL incidents found in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table as a result of the last Agent Server session are marked as acknowledged and their active times are set to zero. If these entries do not require reasons and/or notes then they are automatically added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. If the entries require reasons and/or notes, then they will remain in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table until these entries have been completed by the operator. For a description of each of the tables and their fields, see AlarmManagement Database Tables . -->

About the Connectors Top About the Connectors The Adroit DB Generator requires a specific Connector to connect to and access the information stored in each required database of the 3 rd party application. Each Connector can create one or more Links that actually connect to the specific applications and are configured to create .WGP files from them. Since these Connectors are separate modules (.DLL files) that can be added or removed, you can develop your own Connectors to allow the Adroit DB Generator to creates Adroit agent databases from your 3 rd party application. The Connector DLL files: Adhere to the following naming convention: dbconn_*.dll, where * represents the unique name of the specific Connector. For instance, the CSV Connector file is called dbconn_csv.dll Are located in the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . There are two categories of Connectors: Device-centric Connectors : This is the more common Connector where its Links configure agents from information (tags) within individual front end devices. For instance the OPC Connector Link configures agents from the items within an OPC Server. Complex Connectors :

its Links configure agents from information (tags) within individual front end devices. For instance the OPC Connector Link configures agents from the items within an OPC Server. Complex Connectors : This Connector creates Links that globally configure agents (NOT device specific). For instance, a CSV Connector Link can create a fully configured Adroit agent database (.WGP file) from information contained in CSV files. Note: The Connector category determines how the Links of these Connectors are named. The functionality of the Connector determine the following Connector attributes: if the 3 rd party Connector can be remotely accessed or not, determines whether the Adroit DB Generator can access the Agent Server remotely or whether it has to be installed on the same Agent Server computer on which such 3 rd party programs themselves are installed. if the Connector supports templates, determines whether you can use templates to determine your own customised agent creation, scanning, logging and/or alarming default settings or not. Note : Those Connectors that support templates, implement them uniquely by using the features and fields of information available to the Connector’s specif

ing and/or alarming default settings or not. About the GSM_SMS driver Top About the GSM_SMS driver The sole function of the GSM_SMS driver is the sending and receiving of SMS messages to and from SMS GSM modems. This driver has been specifically designed to simply its use with any cellular SMS protocol. For this reason, Windows drivers for the modem are NOT required, since this driver provides its own interface to the modem via the serial port assigned to it. Note: This driver is ONLY designed to work with SMS GSM modems and, in particular, has been designed and tested using the WAVECOM WMOD2 GSM modem. The devices configured for this driver, can be used in one of following two modes, depending upon the configuration of its Use with Command Agent checkbox setting: Note: For details, concerning the configuration of devices, see Configuring Devices . If checked, the default setting, this device can only be used by a Command agent, which bypasses the scanning sub-system, so that the full SMS message of up to 160 characters can be utilised. In addition, the Command agent provides extensive functionality for both sending and receiving SMS messages. For further details, see Command Agents . If unchecked, this device uses the scanni

ilised. In addition, the Command agent provides extensive functionality for both sending and receiving SMS messages. For further details, see Command Agents . If unchecked, this device uses the scanning sub-system, as normal, replacing the former User-driver functionality, which was also difficult to configure, of sending 79 character SMS messages, configured in the Text, String or Notifier agents. Therefore the Notifier agent can still be used to automatically route alarms from Adroit by SMS to the relevant personnel. For details, see Notifier Agents . Accessing Agent Slots Top Accessing Agent Slots Because of Adroit ‘s open architecture, it is extremely easy to read and/or write agent slot values, provided you know the name of the agent and slot. For details, see About Agents or About Agent Data (Slots) . Slots within agents can be accessed, as follows: The actual agent itself may change values within one or more of its slots. An Expression agent, for example, will generate a new value whenever one of its inputs changes. Another agent within the same Agent Server may read or write one or more agents’ slots. For example, a Scan agent updates the agent(s) and slot(s) it scans whenever values in the front-end device change. Windows within the Adroit user interface can access slot values within agents. For example, Mimic Display Value Behaviours read slot values, whereas Mimic Operator Action Behaviours write slot values. Custom applications using the Agent Server Applications Programming Interface can access slot values. For instance OLE Interface or ActiveX Control . Note: All slots generally offer safe read access, but caution must be exercised when writing slot values. -->

Account Policy Top Account Policy The Windows based Account policy controls how passwords must be used by all user accounts. It defines such things as the maximum password age, minimum password age, minimum password length, and whether or not a password history is maintained. The Account policy determines whether all user accounts are subjected to lockout. If lockout is enabled, then a user account becomes locked if there are a number of incorrect attempts to log on to that account, occurring with no more than a specified amount of time between any two of the bad logon attempts. A locked account remains locked until an administrator unlocks it or a specified amount of time passes. Locked accounts cannot log on. The Account policy also determines whether or not a remote user will be forcibly disconnected from all connections to servers in the domain if that user’s logon hours expire, and whether users must log on before changing their passwords. -->

ACK Commands Top ACK Commands Function: To acknowledge alarms reported by an agent within the Agent Server. Note1: Alarms are always globally acknowledged. Note2: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a security and operational risk through the remote acknowledgment of alarms. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note3: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. To globally acknowledge an alarm via SMS: ack,tag[.alarm type] Where ‘ tag ’ is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, ‘[.alarm type]’ is optional and allows you to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance “ANA_1.High” only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas “ANA_1” acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format: ack,tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type] To globally acknowledge alarms via Putslot: use the new globalAck slot of the Command agent and use the following format: tag[.alarm type] Note: This method does NOT use SMS to acknowledge

larm type] To globally acknowledge alarms via Putslot: use the new globalAck slot of the Command agent and use the following format: tag[.alarm type] Note: This method does NOT use SMS to acknowledge alarms, nor are you limited to only using the Putslot utility, any method can be used that sets the value of this slot. Where ‘ tag ’ is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, ‘[.alarm type]’ is optional and allows you to to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. Active Clusters Foundation Top Clustering Agent Servers Clustered Agent Servers, previously known as hot standby, provide both client and server redundancy enabling high availability of the system. Typically, redundancy can be applied to all the levels within the plant. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . There are three general components in Adroit which are aware of redundancy, namely, the clients, the servers and the server I/O, as illustrated below: In Adroit , an Agent Server can be setup to be a cluster server, which is a set of two Agent Servers running a replicated database (WGP file) on the same project. A cluster Agent Server can be networked with other normal (non-cluster) Agent Servers. The general idea of clustering is that the master server services all the I/O and client tasks, while the standby server replicates the master server. If the master server or computer fails, the standby server takes over as master and the UI’s and scanning tasks take appropriate action. There are three key mechanisms in Active Clu

the master server. If the master server or computer fails, the standby server takes over as master and the UI’s and scanning tasks take appropriate action. There are three key mechanisms in Active Clusters namely catch-up , replication and switchover . A clustered Agent Server: can be networked with other normal (non-cluster) Agent Servers. is either in the mode of master or standby server is either in the state of healthy or unhealthy. A cluster Agent Server is either in the mode of master or standby server and can either be in the state of healthy or unhealthy. Note: Certain agent types on a cluster server require synchronization of internal data structures with their master partner. For details, see Real-time Catch-up . Also, some agents in an Agent Server have internal states that are unknown to and unsynchronised with the standby computer. Examples of such agents are: the Expression agent, the Recipe agent, the Counter agent, the Statistical agent and all other internal agents that do some calculation internal to the Agent Server. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-control

t do some calculation internal to the Agent Server. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. Add a Group Top Add a Group Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . To add a group: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Click the Add Group button to display the Create New Group dialog. text: Adding the slots we're interested in Top Adding the slots we're interested in For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . Initially the Properties collection object contains no Property objects, but it provides a method named Add that is used to add Property objects to the Properties collection. Each Property object in the Properties collection defines a slot to be monitored. The Add method accepts one parameter, the required slot name. The following VBA code shows how to add the value and rawValue slots to the Properties collection: Set prop = props.Add("value") Set prop = props.Add("rawValue") Once the Properties collection is set up, it must be associated with a tag as part of a Request object. In order to facilitate this, each Request object provides a method named Add that handles the creation of the Request object. The Add method accepts a tag and properties collection (i.e. agent name and list of slot names) as parameters. The following VBA code creates requests for Analog tags AN01 and AN02, value and rawValue slots: Set req = reqs.Add("AN01", props) Set req = reqs.Add("AN02", props) -->

text: Adding your own Queries Top Adding your own Queries PLEASE NOTE: This help topic assumes that you are familiar with working with databases and creating SQL queries. Instead of only using the default queries to analyse your logged incidents, you can add your own queries to the Adr_AM_UserQueries table of the AlarmManagement database. Then these queries will also appear in the View Data and View Graph dialogs of this AlarmManagement agent. WARNING! It is recommended that you do NOT edit any table in this database, apart from Adr_AM_UserKPIs and Adr_AM_UserQueries ; otherwise you WILL lose data. Note: If you want to remove the queries you have created, simply delete the Adr_AM_UserQueries table and they will be re-created when the Agent Server starts up. First you need to create the SELECT SQL statement for your query. In this example, we will add a custom downtime reporting query that: Displays the actual reason and sub reasons (not just their IDs) Displays the downtime in the hh:mm:ss time format Displays the category name instead of the category ID Displays the incident name instead of simply the incident ID Displays the unacknowledged time in the hh:mm:ss time format Example entri

ime format Displays the category name instead of the category ID Displays the incident name instead of simply the incident ID Displays the unacknowledged time in the hh:mm:ss time format Example entries returned by this custom query: Note: the Category name (instead of CategoryId) column, the display format of the UnacknowledgedTime and Downtime columns and the textual descriptions provided in the Reason and Subreason columns. The SQL syntax for this query is, as follows: SELECT TOP %t Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.Idx,DT,Process,Adr_AM_Categories.Category AS Category,Incident,Data,Description,Filter,Priority,Shift,Operator,Acknowledged_dt,Acknowledged_by,Cleared_dt,convert(varchar,convert(datetime,1.0*UnacknowledgedTime / (60*24*24)),8) as UnacknowledgedTime,convert(varchar,convert(datetime,1.0*ActiveTime / (60*24*24)),8) as ActiveTime,Adr_AM_Reasons.Reason as Reason,Adr_AM_SubReasons.SubReason as Subreason,Notes FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Categories ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.CategoryId = Adr_AM_Categories.CategoryId INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Reasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_Reasons.Idx INNER JOIN Adr_AM_SubReasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalInciden

oricalIncidents.CategoryId = Adr_AM_Categories.CategoryId INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Reasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_Reasons.Idx INNER JOIN Adr_AM_SubReasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_SubReasons.ReasonIdx AND Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.SubReasonId = Adr_AM_SubReasons.Idx WHERE dt > '%b' AND dt < '%e' ORDER BY dt DESC To add your own query: Open SQL Server Management Studio and connect to the SQL Server that contains the database that the required AlarmManagement agent is connected to. Display the db.Adr_AM_UserQueries table. Right click this table and select Edit top 200 rows . This displays an editable grid of the queries. Select the bottom new (NULL) record and type in the name of this custom query into the Name field e.g. “Custom downtime”. This is name that is displayed in the Query list box when selecting the query. If necessary, provide the necessary Description to help your operators and other users to know what this query will return e.g. “Provides the actual reasons and the downtime in hh:mm:ss time format...”. Either type in the required SELECT SQL statement into the Query field or, in this case, paste it. Note: When pasting in a query

rovides the actual reasons and the downtime in hh:mm:ss time format...”. Either type in the required SELECT SQL statement into the Query field or, in this case, paste it. Note: When pasting in a query, ensure that this SELECT SQL statement copies as a SINGLE line without any carriage returns! Select the next NULL record to commit (save) this query (newly edited record). Restart the Classic User Interface and open the View Data dialog of this AlarmManagement agent to use this new query. You will now find a new query called “Custom downtime” in the Query list. Other things you can do: If necessary your query can support: One or more of the following constraints: these constrains are provided by the View data dialog so that your users can choose which incidents they need to analyse. Top (%t): This allows your users to specify the number of topmost (most recent) incidents that are to be returned by the query. For instance, this %t constraint is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC From (%b) and/or To (%e)

ype)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC From (%b) and/or To (%e): These constraints allow your users to specify the time period during which the required incidents occur. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# AND dt < #%e# If necessary, you can provide ONLY one of these constraints, without the other. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# Now (%now). This allows users to specify the current date and time. For instance you can obtain the last 8 hours in SQL by using the following expression: WHERE dt > DATEADD(Hour, -8, '%now') AND dt < GetDate() Shift times: This constraint is enabled when you specify the From (%b) and/or To (%e) constraints (see above), which allows your users to specify the shift during which the required incidents occur. Operator ( %o). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged against a specific operator. For instance: WHERE Operator='%o' Category ( %c). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged for a specific category. For instance: WHERE CategoryId='%c' One or more of the following KPI targ

ERE Operator='%o' Category ( %c). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged for a specific category. For instance: WHERE CategoryId='%c' One or more of the following KPI target values: these are the ideal values that you want to achieve. Average alarm rate (%AAR). This per hourly count is 6 by default. For instance, this %AAR KPI target value is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC Burst rate (%BR). This per hourly count is 60 by default. Percent upset count (%PUC). This number is 30 by default. Percent upset (%PU). This percentage is 2 by default. Intermittent alarm period (%IAP). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. Bulk acknowledgement period (%BAP). This time period in seconds is 1 by default. Average alarm duration (%ALD). This time period in seconds is 60 by default. Average acknowledgement duration (%AKD). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. General Overview In order to understand Adroit it is important to understand the basic architecture of the product. Below is a diagram, which represents the basic standalone architecture. Figure 1: Basic S

al Overview In order to understand Adroit it is important to understand the basic architecture of the product. Below is a diagram, which represents the basic standalone architecture. Figure 1: Basic Stand Alone Architecture • Front end device (FED): The front-end device is a general term used for a PLC; OPC server; RTU; a controller; or any software package that allows third party communication (i.e. OPC, SIMATIC NET). • Protocol driver: Adroit supports +- 100 different protocols. Once a new driver has been installed and configured to talk to a FED, it is called a Device. A single protocol can support multiple Devices. An example of this is the user can have multiple FEDs which use the same protocol (i.e. MODBUS Ethernet), each FED will have its own IP address/Address. A device will need to be created for each FED. • Agent Server (AS): The Agent Server (I/O Server), is the real-time database, which handles the real-time values and if configured, will handle all post-processing, logging and/or alarming the data. • SmartUI Server (SUIS): The SUIS is a middleware server which exposes data from a number of disparate sources, using the datasource, and also acts as a repository for the g

and/or alarming the data. • SmartUI Server (SUIS): The SUIS is a middleware server which exposes data from a number of disparate sources, using the datasource, and also acts as a repository for the graphic forms or mimics. It also acts as the manager of access, and broker for the unified data model implemented across all data types that may end up in the • Datasource: Each source of data (i.e. Adroit Agent Server) requires a datasource plugin before it can be associated with the SmartUI Server. This provides the ability to expose its data as data elements. An example of a data element is Adroit.Analog.SAMPLEANALOGUE.value. The SmartUI Server connects to data using two different types of datasources: • The SmartUI Server allows multiple sources of data to be available to the configuration of a system in a unifed manner. Scan Point Licensing ---------------------------- Normally a scan point license is consumed whenever a tag is scanned to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other areas that consume scan point licenses as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. 1. Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. 2. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan

gent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. 2. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. 3. Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot), using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface (MISSRVR) or the Adroit ActiveX component (AdroitX.OCX) will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked". Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. 4. Any tag (agent.slot) writes from the Adroit OPC Server will consume one scan point license per unique tag. 5. Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and / or used to send SMS messages to it. 6. The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for each unique value of an SNMP object that is polled (monitored), written (controlled) o

cified by this agent and / or used to send SMS messages to it. 6. The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for each unique value of an SNMP object that is polled (monitored), written (controlled) or trapped (received as an SNMP event). 7. Any agent created for a UDT agent type created by the UDT Agent Type Designer consumes (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. ONLY in HMI Mode: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. 7.) Adroit Logging Factor Top Adroit Logging Factor When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world. Up until 1992 the generally accepted default practice was for users to datalog all points at 1 second. However, due to CPU, HDD speeds and serial protocol speeds, the fastest data could only logged at 4-5 seconds. Therefore the log file created by Adroit was deliberately engineered to always be 20% of the expected size, since Adroit only stores data when it in physically changes. This logging design started to become a problem when hardware and protocol speeds improved OR where high logging time deadband values (or sample rates) were used especially for Analog agents where one could be assured that its value WAS going to be different at each sample period. In these cases, only 20% of the specified historical data is actually recorded. The legacy default for Adroit ’s proprietary logging of using a 20% datalog compression factor has been REMOVED for all new installations, since it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods. However, if a legacy WGP file is o

logging of using a 20% datalog compression factor has been REMOVED for all new installations, since it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods. However, if a legacy WGP file is opened by a new installation of Adroit , that the logging periods configured for some or all of the Datalog agents will exceed the allowable size limit of 5000000 samples (or 95 MB) per Datalog agent. This will occur since the legacy method of accommodating this 20% datalog compression factor allowed the required log period to be up to 5 times greater. In these cases these "non-compliant" Datalog agents will display "error load completion" events. Note: Ensure that you have enabled the logging of Adroit system events in order to identify these non-compliant Datalog agents. For details, see Enabling the logging of Adroit system events . To remedy these "non-compliant" Datalog agents either set the LogCompressionFactor value in the Adroit registry back to its legacy default of 5 and restart the Agent Server OR reconfigure the logging periods of the affected Datalog agents, which should typically require the currently specified logging period to be divided by 5. -->

General: Datalog system buffer size (Kb) This setting specifies the size of the global "datalog change queue", which is 500 Kb, by default. Click for more details: All changes arriving at the data logging subsystem are added to a "datalog change queue". This ensures that these historical updates do not affect the throughput of any real-time updates. These changes are stored in this queue until Adroit reads them off. Therefore, the size of the queue must be able to handle the maximum spike of changed values that a plant can expect. This maximum number of changes is generally proportional to the number of tags logged. The default size of 500Kb, allows for approximately a spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) rate of plant changes will exceed the rate at which the data logging subsystem is able to operate. In this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement and the computer will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers

n this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement and the computer will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers OR less tags need to be logged. For this reason we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor "SubManQueueLen" performance counter of the Agent Server to ensure that it always tends towards 100%, as this counter indicates the free datalog buffer queue. If this value is steadily decreasing, then the rate of datalogging is exceeding the rate at which the values can be committed to disk and the Flush lazily global logging setting should be turned ON. Note: The default value is big enough to handle short term spikes in putslot rates and should not need to be changed. Tip: When specifying the required buffer queue size, use the provided buttons to increase/decrease this value in 64 KB increments/decrements. Flush lazily (LazyFlushing = 1) This setting determines how Adroit writes logged values to disk, which is ON (checked) by default, so that Adroit logs its values to the file cache of the Windows operating system. If you uncheck this option (turn it OFF) then logged data is immediately written to disk. Therefore, if the computer is not on a UPS and there is a power failure, ALL datalog values that have not been committed to disk by Windows will be LOST. If unchecked, all logged values are IMMEDIATELY written to disk but this increases the CPU load and slows the Agent Server down. For instance, by only triggering the log when the value is between certain limits or at particular times of the batch, instead of logging every change in value. To further reduce the size of your datalogs, you can check this setting (turn it ON), so that you can specify a Time deadband and employ one of the datalog Compression Methods. For details, see Data Logging Compression Methods . Settings that affect the operation of the data logging system that are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =

are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =1) This setting causes the Agent Server to attempt to create the necessary tables in SQL at startup, for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, which is ON (checked) by default. This can increase the time the Agent Server takes to startup, especially if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL. If this option is UNCHECKED (turned OFF): Adroit creates the necessary tables when creating NEW datalogs (from the Configurator). Adroit does NOT check for the existence of these tables when the Agent Server starts up. This means that datalogs will NOT write if their tables do not exist. Therefore, if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL and you have ensured that the datalogs for these EXISTING values have their necessary tables, then UNCHECK this option (turn it OFF) to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Disable database table name prefixes (DisableADOTableNamePrefix = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to creat

CK this option (turn it OFF) to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Disable database table name prefixes (DisableADOTableNamePrefix = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to create tables for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, by using the following table name format AdroitRawLog_[tablename], which is OFF (unchecked) by default. If you prefer Adroit to ONLY specify the table name and hence create shorter table names, then check this setting (turn it ON). This removes this "AdroitRawLog_" table name prefix, so that Adroit only uses the specified table name. Add normal timestamp fields to database tables (LogADODataTimes = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server NOT to log readable timestamps for values that are logged to SQL databases, which is OFF (unchecked) by default. So that ONLY the Adroit timestamp of the change in value is provided, this is not ‘readable’ in SQL as this does not conform to the DateTime value type. If you want Adroit to provide an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adr

e an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adroit to re-create them with an added timestamp column. Tip: We recommend that you check this setting (turn it ON) before logging values to the SQL database. Use only proprietary logged data for trends (ProprietarySetPreference =1) This setting prevents Adroit from using data from SQL for trending, regardless of the circumstances, this is OFF (unchecked) by default. Typically you would turn this setting ON if you use at least 2 log sets to log ALL your values, one that logs to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and another that logs to SQL. In this case, by enabling this setting Adroit will ONLY trend data from the log set that logs values to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and NEVER trend data from a log set that logs values to SQL. This ensures that your trends quickly retrieve and display their historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatib

eir historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatible database. UI settings (no restart required): Create datalog agents automatically (AutoCreate = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to immediately create a Datalog agent when you log an agent from the Configurator, which is ON (checked) by default. Since each agent has a default logging slot that is automatically selected, you can uncheck this option (turn it OFF) if you usually need to log another slot. In this case, a confirmation dialog is launched, asking the user whether a new Datalog agent should be created, before a slot of an agent can be logged. Settings that ONLY apply to the Configurator dialog within the Classic User Interface. -->

Agent Functionality Top Agent Functionality The "functionality" of an agent can be defined as the sum total of all the inherent knowledge built into an agent type or the operation or method of the agent. For details, see About Agents . The functionality of an agent is structured, much like the data or slots of an agent as having both generic and type-specific functionality. For details, see Data Structure of an Agent . Generic functionality is something that all types of agents possess, whereas type-specific functionality is confined only to agents of the specific type. Some of the generic functionality possessed by all agent types are, for example, the ability to add, remove, copy, save, and load instances. For instance, consider the following partial description of the functionality provided by the Analog agent: Functionality Configuration Generic Functionality Generic Functionality Adding Removing Copying Editing Add the instance ANA02 to the Agent Server Remove the instance ANA02 from the Agent Server Make a copy of the instance ANA02 for use as an editing template Edit the slot values of ANA02 Specific Functionality Specific Functionality Scaling Alarming SqRooting Scale the r

Agent List CSV File Format Top Agent List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store the agents which are alarmed by this agent. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx- AGNTLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: Tagname: the name of the agent that is being alarmed. Note: This does not specify which slot (value) of this agent is being alarmed. Typeindex: this specifies the zero-based index number of the required alarm type. This can be calculated when the required TYPLST.CSV file is opened in MS Excel, by subtracting two from the specified row number of the required alarm type. For example if the required alarm type is in row 51, then its index value will be 49. For details of the format of this CSV file, see Type List CSV File Format . Route number: A valid route number from the route list file. Acknowledge: 1 is a normal acknowledgeable alarm, while 0 is an alarm that cannot be acknowledged. Reserved: 1 Reserved: 0 Reserved: 0 Inhibit time: The future date/time when this incident (alarmed tag) will be re-enabled, as specified using the

rm, while 0 is an alarm that cannot be acknowledged. Reserved: 1 Reserved: 0 Reserved: 0 Inhibit time: The future date/time when this incident (alarmed tag) will be re-enabled, as specified using the Inhibited until checkbox of the Alarming dialog. It is saved to the CSV as the two parts of a FILETIME variable e.g. if this is not set then the following value is saved: ",0 0" Note: Inhibit times are DISCARDED when IMPORTING alarm configurations. Delay time: The number of seconds that the alarm system should wait, once this incident (alarmed tag)becomes active, before this incident is recognised as being ‘officially’ active. Conditional expression: An expression that must be true before this incident becomes active. -->

Agent Naming Convention Top Agent Naming Convention The following rules apply when naming agents: Agent names have a maximum of 32 characters. Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ -->

Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) Top Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) The first bit in the status word, statusBad or statusBit00 , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For further details of this status word, see Agent status words or Slot status words . This bit itself is a combination of statusConnectionBad (a.k.a. statusRemoved), statusScanBad and statusAgentBad . For details, see Connection Bad , Scan Bad or Agent Bad . Note: This statusBad bit CANNOT be set directly but will only be set depending upon the values of the other three bits for the specified agent (agent status word) or slot (slot status word). If the statusScanned bit of an slot is set, on start up the Agent Server switches also turns on the statusScanBad bit of this slot as well, until the first successful scan transaction for the slot, at which time the Scan Agent will reset the statusScanBad bit of this slot. -->

text: Agent Persistence Files Top Agent Persistence Files Agent persistence files are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent. Their purpose is to ensure that none of this data is lost. Previously this data could only be saved by frequently saving the entire Agent database via a Script or Expression agent. However, this practice is dangerous as .WGP files can corrupt if a power failure occurs during the save. Note: This is a GLOBAL setting for each agent type, which is set in the respective agent configuration dialog. Once enabled, a persistence or (.WORK) file is created for each agent, which is saved when the data of this agent is updated. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Statistical and/or Counter agents, saving their persistence files can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. These persistence files are stored in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. These agent persistence settings are currently saved to the following location in the registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Persistence See Also: Project f

ns\Default \Work. These agent persistence settings are currently saved to the following location in the registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Persistence See Also: Project folder . Agent Referencing Convention Top Agent Referencing Convention The following convention can be used when referring to agents: [\\AgentServerName\]AgentName This allows agents to be specified or referred to, as follows: Explicitly , by including the Agent Server name. For instance \\AS1\ANA001 This ensures that there is no ambiguity in specifying the required agent. In general, this format may be used in any Classic UI dialog except when adding or copying agents. Implicitly agent names, by omitting the Agent Server name. For instance ANA001 In this case Adroit will first search the Agent Server it is currently connected to for that agent, implicitly assuming it is on that server. If it does not find the agent, it will look in all the other Agent Servers in the same project for agents of the same name. If only one agent is found on a remote Agent Server, it will use that one. If more than one agent of that name is found on the remote Agent Servers, then the action taken depends on the mode of the local Agent Server (as specified in the Adroit Setup utility), as follows: If this is a Stand-alone / Distributed server then any duplicate agent names found on two or more remote Agent Serve

e of the local Agent Server (as specified in the Adroit Setup utility), as follows: If this is a Stand-alone / Distributed server then any duplicate agent names found on two or more remote Agent Servers will be ignored by the user interface. If this is a Cluster aware server or Cluster server then the duplicate tag name found on the first (alphabetically) remote Agent Server will be used. When that becomes unavailable, the tags on the next Agent Server will be used by the user interface, and so on. Note: If a duplicate agent name is found on the local Agent Server (if running) and any remote Agent Servers, the local agent will always be used. -->

Agent Server Communication within Networks Top Agent Server Communication within Networks Agent Servers with the same project name are typically connected by means of Agent Server broadcasts, so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Servers in the project. For further details on projects, see About Adroit Projects . Note: Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds, to indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. Agent Server broadcasts are highly effective for relatively small Agent Server networks, which are connected on the same domain. However, this approach is inflexible and explicit Agent Server connections are required instead for the following two networking configurations: Inter-domain Agent Server networks, since the Agent Server broadcasts do not operate across domains or over a WAN Large scalable Agent Server networks , since it may be undesirable to maintain a large, potentially resource intensive, grid of fully connected Agent Servers. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if

ble to maintain a large, potentially resource intensive, grid of fully connected Agent Servers. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. For further details of mechanisms provided by Adroit to connect Agent Servers together and their limitations and how to configure each of these mechanisms, see Agent Server Connection Methods . -->
