Agent Server Connection Methods Top Agent Server Connection Methods Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, the ability to refer to agents within another Agent Server. Note: Proxy agents are automatically created when an Agent Server accesses an agent that exists in a remote Agent Server. Using the Project Name: This is the default method for connecting distributed Agent Servers, in which case you specify the SAME project name for ALL the Agent Servers that need to connect to each other, which adds them to this project. Network broadcasts are then made between ALL these Agent Servers to provide each other with two-way access to their agents. Click here for the limitations of this method and/or how to configure this method: Disadvantages: In practice each Agent Server within a project typically only connects to agents in SOME of the other specified Agent Servers, which results in unnecessary network traffic between the Agent Servers that are not actually communicating with one another. This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across

This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across domains or routers/switches (a WAN). You need to use the explicit connection mechanism to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. Agent Status Top Agent Status The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a header or generic slot and so is common to all agent types, and shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad. In contrast, the statusRaw header slot the agent shows the status of the agent, without any regard for the status of the individual slots. For instance, if one of the agent slots is scan bad, the agent status slot will not necessarily show scan bad unless the agent itself has been marked as scan bad. For details on the structure of data in an agent, see Data Structure of an Agent . This status slot is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent. Each bit of this 32 bit word is also exposed as a slot, allowing up to 32 status flags to be accessed at any time. Note1 : In addition to this overall agent status word, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent, which can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. For details, see Slot Status Words . Note2: The first bit in the status word

word, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent, which can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. For details, see Slot Status Words . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note3: These bits can be viewed and/or set via the Agent Header configuration dialog. For details, see Editing the Header of an Agent . This status slot is divided into two portions: The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each having a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration bits. For details, see Common Status bits . The second 16 bits (16 to 31) are known as the Specific Status bits and they are agent type-specific. Their equivalent slots are called statusBit16 up to statusBit31. For details of these slots, see the Agent Types and their Slots Reference . For

Specific Status bits and they are agent type-specific. Their equivalent slots are called statusBit16 up to statusBit31. For details of these slots, see the Agent Types and their Slots Reference . For instance an Analog agent uses the first type-specific bit to indicate a Low Alarm condition, whereas an Expression agent uses this bit to indicate a result value Equal to Zero. Write access is restricted to the control bits (agentStatusBit xx ), where xx is: 01,02,03,05,08,09, or 11. -->

Agent Subscriptions Top Agent Subscriptions The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of “listening” for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). The process of subscribing is setting up the “listener”, by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any “listeners”. The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs. Subscriptions are the basis of most communication within the Agent Server, and between the Server and the connected clients, (Operators for example) . -->

Alarming Overview Top Alarming Overview The alarm system is a critical component for any process, which alerts your operators when components of the process are operating outside of their normal functioning. Adroit provides a flexible alarming capability in that any slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of any agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. can be alarmed. In this way any situations, ranging from plant upsets or process variable excursions to failures within the Adroit system itself can be monitored. Alarming is managed by an Alarm agent, which communicates the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). when they occur, to the relevant personnel and/or applications. You can announce an alarm by using one or more of the following methods: by a siren or through the activation of audiovisual multimedia by a list of unacknowledged and acknowledged alarms by SMS or m

You can announce an alarm by using one or more of the following methods: by a siren or through the activation of audiovisual multimedia by a list of unacknowledged and acknowledged alarms by SMS or mobile pager messages or electronic sign display by logging the alarm to an OLE DB compliant database by logging the alarm to the Windows application event log by printing the alarm to hardcopy by launching a process-specific page of hypertext help by graphical display on a mimic by textual display on a mimic In the past alarms were hardwired into the panels, which limited their number; now alarms are software-driven, which can lead to an unlimited number of alarms. While one’s intention is often to keep the operators better informed by increasing the number of alarms, the result is that operators become overloaded and confused and may even start ignoring alarms! Therefore LESS alarms are MORE effective. Alarm Management is therefore an important aspect of process control as it counteracts inefficient alarming. This allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. For more details about creating alarms in Adroit , see

inefficient alarming. This allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. For more details about creating alarms in Adroit , see Alarming in Adroit . For more details about displaying alarms in Adroit , see Displaying Alarms in Adroit . For more details about industry guidelines concerning Alarm Management and how this is addressed by Adroit , see About Alarm Management . -->

Alarming strategy Top About Alarming Strategies BEFORE any agent is alarmed it is RECOMMENDED to create and use an Alarming strategy. An alarming strategy is simply a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Also once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, if required. Although this may seem unnecessary to take the time to create such a strategy, as with all planning a little time spent in the beginning is richly rewarded by the end of a project. An alarming strategy is necessary for the following reasons: It simplifies the initial engineering of the alarming. It ensures that the required alarms will be sent to the desired destinations and can be correctly filtered. It eliminates confusion, with regard to the often complex routing of alarms. It prevents the re-engineering of the alarming, if a mistake is detected after the initial alarming configuration has been performed. Although this is not a definitive description of creating an alarming strategy, the following issues need to be considered when this is being formulated: Display of Alarms: Determine which alarm destinations will be used i.e. how the alarms

ption of creating an alarming strategy, the following issues need to be considered when this is being formulated: Display of Alarms: Determine which alarm destinations will be used i.e. how the alarms will alert the relevant plant personnel and the standards that are to be used for each destination. For instance: capitalization rules; the number and width of columns to display etc. In this way it is possible to ensure a consistent look and feel for the displayed alarms, which will assist the plant personnel in responding to alarms quickly. Filtering of Alarms: An alarm priority can be specified for each agent, so that alarm agents can filter out all the alarms generated by low priority agents, if necessary. However, since this alarm priority is tag-specific rather than alarm-specific, it cannot be used as an efficient alarm filtering mechanism, for instance if we only want to display a sub-set of the alarms configured for an agent. The only mechanism in Adroit that can achieve this is to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism. to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism. Decide on the number of agents to alarm per Alarm agent - there is no limitation for this. Decide on required number of alarm routes to use. Note: Do not use route 0 or 1 as these are predefined Adroit system routes. Decide which routes need to be logged persistently i.e. to the Eventlog and which should be sent to DbAccess for access from 3rd party MES applications etc. Note: Ensure that the alarms generated from a single agent are routed using the SAME alarm agent. For instance, the Hi and HiHi alarms of an Analog agent must both be routed using the SAME Alarm agent. Decide which alarms must be sent as SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. , by allocating a route for SMS's. Although you probably will need to have more than one rout

S Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. , by allocating a route for SMS's. Although you probably will need to have more than one route that uses a Notify agent or Command agent as a destination. AlarmAgent Name of alarm agent. Type Name of alarm type. Route Number of alarm route number. Note: If a Route of –1 is specified then the specified alarm will be deleted. Ack 1, if alarm must be acknowledgeable, otherwise 0. TypeEnum Number of alarm type enumeration, if the Type parameter is not used (is empty). Note: This must be -1, if the Type parameter is being used (is specified). The function returns a properly initialised, but empty, OLE Automation VARIANT struc

Allowing Commands to be Performed Top Allowing Commands to be Performed Although all Command agents are able to send and receive textual messages, it is necessary to manually specify whether a Command agent should analyse the SMS messages that it receives for commands, for the following reasons: Security: once enabled, these commands can be used to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server. Licensing: once enabled, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number and Specifying Additional Callers . Note: By default a Command agent is not able to receive textual commands. Furthermore, it is also necessary to specify which commands this Command agent is able to perform. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: The Command agent is ONLY able to perform the commands that have been specifi

ecifying Permitted Commands or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: The Command agent is ONLY able to perform the commands that have been specifically selected, since certain commands pose a greater security and operational risk than others. To enable a Command agent to perform textual command messages that it receives: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, check the Enable commands checkbox, the default is unchecked. WARNING! Once this checkbox is enabled, scan point licenses will be consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and used to send SMS messages to it. By default, NONE of the available commands are selected, since certain commands pose a greater security and operational risk than others. Note: Once this checkbox is checked, the AllCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to receive commands. For details, see Specific Status Bits . -->

Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Top Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources. Adroit drivers can make use of a different PLC addressing to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the PLCs used need to have separate addresses and both PLCs need to be able to be independently accessed by the Adroit drivers. Note: This only applicable to network-able (RS485, RS232, Ethernet, L2, Allen-Bradley Data Highway, Modbus + etc...) communications. A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front-end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves the driver connecting to the alternate (address Y) port and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs thr

dary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves the driver connecting to the alternate (address Y) port and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. -->

Applying Security Policies Top Applying Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager allows you to implement the specified security settings on the local and/or a remote computer. It is also possible to save these security settings to create a global Adroit security policy (security configuration), which can be applied to another Adroit computer, by simply opening this policy in its Adroit Security Manager. For instance: you may have one security configuration for your remote Classic User Interface or operator–only computers and one for your Agent Server computers. To implement all the enabled security policies on the local computer: this applies ALL the security policies (options) that you have enabled to the local computer. Note: It is recommended that you log off the computer to ensure that these changes are made. Click on the Apply policy menu item. This applies all the security policies to the local computer that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked. IMPORTANT: These security policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. To apply or deploy the selected options on a remote computer: this allows you to apply ALL the secu

policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. IMPORTANT: These security policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. Click on the Deploy policy … menu item. Select the required computer using the Browse for Computer dialog. This applies all the security policies that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked to this remote computer. Note: It is recommended that the specified computer is logged off to ensure that these security changes are made. Note: You need Adminstrative rights on the selected computer in order to perform this configuration. To save the security configuration: this saves the configured Adroit groups and users and their group memberships and all the security policies that have been enabled and/or the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings. This allows you to create different Adroit security configurations for different computers. For instance: you may have one security configuration

the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings. This allows you to create different Adroit security configurations for different computers. To apply a saved security configuration: this applies the Adroit groups and users and their group memberships and all the security policies that have been enabled and/or the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings to this local computer. Click on the Open … menu item. Locate the required security profile (*.sec.ini) that contains the required settings. Click the Open button. -->

Audit Policy Top Audit Policy Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer’s security log. Windows can record a range of security event types, from a system-wide event such as a user logging on, to an attempt by a user to read a specific file. Both successful and unsuccessful attempts to perform an action can be recorded. Use the Audit policy to determine the types of security events Windows NT-based Operating Systems will log. When administering domains, the Audit policy affects the security logs of the domain controller and of all servers in the domain, because they share the same Audit policy. When administering a Windows computer that is not a domain controller, this policy affects only the security log of that computer. Entries in a security log can be reviewed using Event Viewer. -->

text: Automatic master mode assignment Top Automatic master mode assignment In automatic mode, the systeminfo.serverMode is automatically controlled by the state of the partner server and the state of the local systeminfo.serverstate slot. Rules and implications Starting conditions for a new cluster server. Each server can be optionally configured to make itself master after a configurable period of time elapsed after this server has started (loaded). When this time period has elapsed after startup, if the server has not yet detected another cluster server in that project, then it will set itself to master. If, however, it does detect other cluster servers and no master server exists in that list of servers, then it will elect itself as master if it is the lowest alphabetically named server (i.e. closest to ‘a’) in its list of healthy standby cluster servers. Consequences on the cluster of adding a new cluster server. No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when adding a new server to the cluster. All cluster servers loadup as standby servers. Therefore, if a master already exists in the cluster, adding a new server will not cause an automatic master mode switch between t

server to the cluster. All cluster servers loadup as standby servers. Therefore, if a master already exists in the cluster, adding a new server will not cause an automatic master mode switch between the servers. If it is required that a newly started server take over as master, and then the options in (4) below can be used. Consequences on the cluster of removing a cluster server. The process of removing a server incorporates both normal program termination and abnormal program termination (software or hardware failures). No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when removing a standby server from the cluster. However, when the master server is removed, the remaining healthy standby server will become master. Consequences on the cluster when changing a server’s serverMode and/or serverState slots: The serverMode slot of a healthy standby server is set to master. The server hosting this operation will first set the remote cluster server serverMode slot to standby and only then set itself to master. The serverMode slot of a healthy master server is set to standby. The server hosting this operation will not take any further action. The healthy remote standby server will

then set itself to master. The serverMode slot of a healthy master server is set to standby. The server hosting this operation will not take any further action. The healthy remote standby server will detect the change and switch to master mode. The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action. The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a master server. The master server will simultaneously set itself as standby, so that an unhealthy master is never obtained in the cluster. The remote server will detect the change (from healthy master to unhealthy standby) and become the master server. The serverState slot is set from unhealthy to healthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action. An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when: a healthy master server is removed when the current healthy master server becomes unhealthy the user sets the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby. This results in a new master and the Adroit system will ensure that the

ts the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby. This results in a new master and the Adroit system will ensure that the existing master is relegated to standby, thereby ensuring that two master servers cannot exist in the cluster. Suggested method of operation Start both Agent Servers in the cluster at the same time, and then the server with the lowest alphabetical name (i.e. closest to ‘a’) will become the master server. In an unplanned master server computer or software termination, the standby server will take over and the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. If, however, a master server takeover is planned, simply set the desired standby server as master and the current master will be delegated to standby. Thereafter, the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. A planned takeover can be implemented either before a planned computer shutdown occurs or when the repaired computer is brought back into the cluster and is instructed, using the manual override, to take over as master. -->

Automatic Sending of Values Top Automatic Sending of Values The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For details of the other methods of sending SMS messages, see Sending SMS Messages . The following mechanisms can be used to send these automatic messages: On change: In this case an SMS message is sent whenever the value of the specified tag changes. For details, see Automated Sending On Change of Value . On significant change: In this case an SMS message is ONLY sent when the change in the value of the specified tag exceeds a specified deadband. For details, see Automating Sending On Significant Change of Value . By triggering: In this case, an SMS message is ONLY sent when it is triggered by another tag i.e. when the value of this tag changes. For details, see Automating Sending By Triggering . Tip: This last mechanism can be used to send or report values at pre-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. The received automatic SMS message, adheres to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName

-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. The received automatic SMS message, adheres to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName = value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. Automatic WGP File Backups Top Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Both the number of days for which these files are to be saved for and the maximum number of backup files can be specified to avoid backup duplication and conserve disk space. WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note1: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: name: is the normal name of the WGP file yymmdd:

estarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: name: is the normal name of the WGP file yymmdd: is the date of the save e.g. 20041101 hhmmss: is the time of the save e.g. 163715 v: is an incremental version number Note: This version number will increment when this WGP file is saved, even if nothing has been changed in the WGP file. n is the number of agents stored in the WGP file Note: This is still stored in the first line of the WGP file, as before. Note: In addition to automatic backup, Adroit WGP files also contain version information. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . -->

text: Available Agents Top Available Agents The most fundamental building blocks of Adroit are intelligent objects called agents, which in addition to being able to manipulate their own data can read and write to other agents and so influence them. For further details, see About Agents or How agents can be used . An Adroit configuration is therefore made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. For details about how to reference agents, see Agent Referencing Convention . Each agent type provides externally accessible data attributes, or slots. For a description of the slots provided by each agent type, see Agent Type Slot Reference . The following is an alphabetic list of all the available agent types: "The Accumulator agent" on page 1 : to analyse an accumulating process value to calculate its difference in value (or delta) between successive events or over a specific time period. The AgentGroup Agent : combines agents that have something in common into groups. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are communicated to the necessary personnel and/or applications. The AlarmList Agent : lists current or unacknowledged incidents to display in an Alarm List Viewer window. The AlarmManagement Agent : configures and records your active incidents so you can improve your alarming configuration. ICMP (PING) Agent : determines the existence of a remote device on the network. The Integer Agent : stores an integer number +/– 2147483647 (32 bits). The IOT Agent : can represent any object containing multiple properties (or slots). The Marshal Agent : provides the functionality of 16 Digital agents in a single agent. Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files Top Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For this reason, it is essential that this file, along with the other Adroit project files, be frequently backed up to ensure that the integrity of this data is preserved. Since if this file is either deleted or becomes corrupted without having a recent backup, many man hours of effort will be lost. Adroit WGP files, from Adroit 6 onwards, provide two additional features to assist with their regular back up, as follows: WARNING! These features are merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! Automatic backup of WGP file on each save: To further ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups, WGP files can now be automatically backed up each time they are saved. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . Note1: If this is implemented, then at most onl

en the regular backups, WGP files can now be automatically backed up each time they are saved. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . Note1: If this is implemented, then at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. Version information saved in the WGP file: In addition to providing an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes, this versioning information can also be used to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . For details on creating a backup procedure to guarantee disaster avoidance and to easily transfer a project to another system, see Creating Backup Procedures . -->

Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Top Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. The table will consist of a number of fields or columns; and each field may be linked to a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . Note1: Table names and field names should not contain spaces as each database vendor supports spaces differently. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. The following transactions are supported: insert

vendor supports spaces differently. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. The following transactions are supported: insert, update, delete and retrieve: An insert or an update transaction is used to transfer information from Adroit into the table, as follows: An insert transaction simply takes the values of tags and inserts a new entry into the end of the table, this is useful for accumulating a history of information on tags. An update transaction is responsible for keeping a record or a row in a table updated with the values of tags. A delete transaction can be used to remove a number of rows in a table. A retrieve transaction is used to transfer information from the table to Adroit . This is useful for applying a recipe management system or for updating Adroit with the results obtained from a 3 rd party application. These database transactions can be executed in the following ways: On demand by poking a one into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact ever

e into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact every twenty-four hours synchronised at six 'o clock in the morning. By triggering , based on a list of tags e.g. when the digital tag PUMP.value switches on, or, when the analog tag DAM_LEVEL.value changes. By using a combination of triggering and scheduling . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the transactions, e.g. to transact every five seconds but only if the tag DAM_LEVEL.value has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple transactions. -->

Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit Top Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means. It is the user's method of informing the Agent Server that something in the server is not healthy and it needs to relinquish it's master state. Manual master mode assignment . Automatic master mode assignment . -->

Best Practices Top Best Practices These are methodologies with regard to the use of Adroit that have been proven over time to lead to the successful implementation of SCADA projects. Tip: A commitment to using the best practices of Adroit is actually a commitment to using all our knowledge and experience, which has been gained painstakingly over time, to ensure your success. Project Directory Structure The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc. For this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created at the root drive (or wherever the data files are required to be stored), typically called ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default ', this project folder should contain the following directories: \CSV, which should contain all your exported data. \CustomAgents, which contains all the custom agents created for the project. \Data, which should contain all the configuration pertaining to the Agent Server, such as .WGP files, *.BAS and database files used for reporting etc. \Datalogs, which should contain all datalog files. \Mimics, which should contain all mimic, trend, al

rtaining to the Agent Server, such as .WGP files, *.BAS and database files used for reporting etc. \Datalogs, which should contain all datalog files. \Mimics, which should contain all mimic, trend, alarm and event windows, bitmaps etc. Note: This folder is typically the only subfolder that should be added to the Adroit Path . \Wizards, which should contain all wizards. \Work, which can contain persistence files for Counter and/or Statistical agents, which save the statistical values these agents calculate. Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector. Usage examples: Displaying a value on a label or button with applied string formatting. Driving a gauge control from the value of an Adroit agent. Driving a slider control from the value of an Adroit agent and writing this value back to Adroit when the slider is manually adjusted. The Bind Value Behaviour provides the following options: To Control Property: this is the default option, where a value (data element) is linked to a property of a control/vector. If this is a String property, then you also have the option of applying string formatting to this value before it displayed. This allows a data element (value) to drive the value of a property of a control/vector. From Control Property: this connects a property of a specific control or vector to a value (data element) and specifies which event of this control or vector is used to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. Both (To/From Control Property):

This facilitates a two-way feedback connection between the specified property of the control/vector and the data element. Calculating statistics from Analog values Top Calculating statistics from Analog values The Analog agent can be enabled to calculate the following statistics from its value slot: sum (total), average, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and direction of change (trend). These statistics are only calculated, when the Integer statsPeriod slot is set to the number of minutes that you want the value slot to be recorded for statistical evaluation. This is a "rolling" period, which specifies the maximum sampling time from "now" (the current time) into the past for the specified period. In this case the value slot is recorded every second over this timespan and the statistics are calculated from these recorded values. IMPORTANT: Since the calculation of these statistics can affect performance if used excessively, please ensure that you ONLY calculate statistics for the Analog values you need them for. Setting the statsPeriod slot to 0 (the default value) disables the calculation of these statistics for an Analog agent. Tip: You can use the Statistical period (mins), 0 to disable field of the configuration dialog to configure this statsPeriod slot for an Analog agent. These statistics are

istics for an Analog agent. Tip: You can use the Statistical period (mins), 0 to disable field of the configuration dialog to configure this statsPeriod slot for an Analog agent. These statistics are saved into the following slots of the Analog agent, so that they can be separately reported, as needed: Note: If necessary, you can reset these statistical calculations by setting the Boolean statsReset slot to 1 (True) which clears the recorded values. statsAverage : The average of all the recorded values. statsMax : The highest recorded value. statsMin : The lowest recorded value. statsStdDev : The standard deviation of all the recorded values. statsSum : The total of all the recorded values. statsDirection : This compares the newest recorded value (the current value slot) to the oldest recorded value and displays the results of this comparison, so that you can determine the general direction in which it is changing (its trend) as follows: 0 typically means that the value has not changed. 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. However, you can also specify an option

. 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. However, you can also specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value. In this case set the statsDirDev slot, to the required decimal percentage value (a value from 0 to 1) so that deviations in value less than or equal to this specified percentage result in the statsDirection slot being set to 0 meaning “no change”. For instance, if you set the statsDirDev slot to 0.10, then only when the newest recorded value differs from the oldest recorded value by more than 10 % will the statsDirection slot display whether the current value is higher (1) or lower (-1). -->

Calculations in Expressions Top Calculations in Expressions Examples of expressions . An expression can be thought of as a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, which are evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Mathematical Operators . Mathematical Functions . This order can be overridden by using brackets. Each term of the expression is composed of primary elements, which can either be signed (or complemented) numbers or variables (v1 to v20, and v99 which is equivalent to "value"), or sub-expressions. This recursive definition of an expression means that expressions can be nested to any level of complexity. Note: v1, V1, v01 and V01 are all valid representations of the input slots. Each Expression agent contains an expression field in which you enter an ANSI-C expression string. The expression can include spaces, round brackets and new line characters for clarity, as well as C and C++ style comments after the expression to document its purpose (i.e. // comment or /* comment */). Note: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configur

or /* comment */). Note: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configuration. -->

Catch-up Top Catch-up When a new server is added to the cluster, it must become a mirror image of the active member of the cluster. The new server must restore its historical data (historical catch-up) that it lost during the down time. This historical synchronization or Datalog catch-up is facilitated by a new agent called the SystemDatalog agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. Note: Datalog catch-up is not supported when OLE DB logging is being used as this would only further delay a task which is already time consuming and CPU intensive. As OLE DB logging is logging to a database, this database could be equipped with the querying/replication tools required to fill any holes that exist. Historical data catch up of the newly added standby server -->

Command-line Options for Driver Monitor Top Command-line Options for the Driver Monitor The following options can typically be either entered into the Command line options edit box in the Options menu of the Driver Monitor Launcher and allows you to further customise this application for your specific requirements: /A This option toggles the output display of the Datascope screen between the default hexadecimal (binary) format and ASCII format Tip: We recommend that you ALWAYS display the Datascope in ASCII format, even for known Binary(hex) type protocols, because the newer drivers provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format and also convert the hexadecimal display to ASCII to remain compatible. For further details, see Datascope screen . /L This option will log the communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. The logged information is typically stored in a .TXT file with the same name as the device name. The following additional options can be used in conjunction with this /L option: /F <filename> This sub-option allows you to specify the name of the file that is used to log the Datascope screen e.g. /Ferr

ollowing additional options can be used in conjunction with this /L option: /F <filename> This sub-option allows you to specify the name of the file that is used to log the Datascope screen e.g. /Ferrors.txt specifies a file called 'errors.txt' /T This sub-option adds timestamps to the logged data, so that time at which the data is logged to file will also be recorded. /H This option logs the device-specific communication messages and errors to an HTML page to preserve the color of the datascope to make the troubleshooting process easier. The output file created by this option has the same name as the device name and a .HTM extension. Note: The log files created by the /L and /H options are located in the folder in which this utility is launched. Common Device Configuration Top Common Device Configuration Although the dialog displayed when adding or configuring a device is protocol driver specific, this dialog will generally contain the following groups of configuration parameters: Note: This protocol driver configuration for each device is saved in the system registry; therefore it is necessary to reconfigure the devices if they are to be run on another computer. For further details, see About Protocol Drivers . The rates at which the scanning or communication occurs can be defined for the individual I/O ports. Primary and secondary parameters Each device contains primary and secondary parameters that define the available connection channels (or routes) and parameters. The secondary information is optional and is used in the event of a failure on the primary connection, or vice versa. How this secondary port works is simple, if the driver is using the primary configuration parameters and the communication fails, the driver will switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible. Once the primary port becomes available again, the driver may be forced into reverting to it by b

l switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible. Once the primary port becomes available again, the driver may be forced into reverting to it by breaking the secondary port link, long enough to force the driver to do the switch back. This cycle may be repeated as often as fault conditions occur. Communication Failure Handling . PLC Details This group of details relates to how to address the FED (front-end device), and will contain details such as routing information or ID’s on a multi-drop that is specific to the FED’s protocol. text: Common Status bits Top Common Status bits The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent, each bit of which is also exposed as a slot. For details, see Agent Status . The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each bit has a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These Common Status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration groups, as follows: Note1: These are NOT contiguous groupings of bits, for instance the first bit statusBit00 is a condition bit NOT a control bit! Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . The first group is called Control bits, which can be modified by the user. Each bit can therefore be set or reset by the user, to control an agent’s operator, logging, alarming, and scanning

dling) . The first group is called Control bits, which can be modified by the user. Each bit can therefore be set or reset by the user, to control an agent’s operator, logging, alarming, and scanning functionality. The second group is called Condition bits, which are not directly modifiable by the user, and may only be viewed. They report on an agent’s integrity and alarm state, etc. Note: All agent Specific Status bits are also Condition bits, since they are not directly modifiable by the user. The third group is called the Configuration bits, which are also not directly modifiable by the user, since they only provide configuration information about an agent, namely whether or not it has been scanned and/or alarmed. -->

Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent Top Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent If the MultiState agent goes into an unspecified state (i.e. a combination of inputs which has not been defined), it will be reported as being in State00 and will set the AGENT BAD bit and consequently the BAD bit will be set also. Note: that this only happens on a transition from a valid to an invalid state. A new MultiState agent that has not been configured and has therefore never known anything except the invalid state will not have its BAD bits set -->

Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Top Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Condition Bits fan-in, which means that an agent condition bit is automatically set to 1 whenever one of the corresponding slot condition bits is set to 1. The converse, however, is not true, i.e. an agent condition bit being set to 1 does not cause the corresponding slot condition bits to be automatically set to 1. Note: The condition bit fan-in uses positive logic: only one slot bit needs to be set for the corresponding agent bit to be set, and resetting a slot bit does not necessarily cause the corresponding agent bit to be reset (because the corresponding bit for another slot may be set). Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don’t want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset. Bad . Connection Bad . Alarm(s) Unacknowledged . Subscriptions active .

Configuration Problems Top Configuration Problems The most commonly experienced fault in the first-time use of any communications link is incorrect configuration. In many cases, a single resource is used to communicate to multiple devices. Serial communications When configuring serial communications of any type, be sure to specify the correct data and stop-bit settings if available for selection. If these settings are unknown, then the documentation for the remote device should be examined to find out the following information: whether the settings are fixed and unchangeable whether they exist as dipswitch settings whether the devices are software configurable In the case of dipswitches or software configuration, it may be necessary to re-start the device for the settings to take effect. Because some of our older serial protocol drivers do not interpret error codes and translate them to English, I include a brief listing of serial communications error codes. These codes are separate from the Win32 codes. They can also be OR'ed together, and for that reason we supply the hex values here. 0x0001 = Receive Queue overflow 0x0002 = Receive Overrun Error 0x0004 = Receive Parity Error 0x0

om the Win32 codes. They can also be OR'ed together, and for that reason we supply the hex values here. 0x0001 = Receive Queue overflow 0x0002 = Receive Overrun Error 0x0004 = Receive Parity Error 0x0008 = Receive Framing error 0x0010 = Break Detected 0x0100 = TX Queue is full 0x0200 = LPTx Timeout 0x0400 = LPTx I/O Error 0x0800 = LPTx Device not selected 0x1000 = LPTx Out-Of-Paper 0x8000 = Requested mode unsupported (e.g. An error value of 12 is equal to 8 + 4 which means "Receive parity" and "Receive framing" error.) Networks If the communications are via a protocol such as TCP/IP, NetBIOS or other LAN protocol, the resource may be connected to the existing office LAN. To eliminate the possibility of interference, a "private" network should be created to reduce the chances of poor network termination or excessive traffic causing problems. Networking programs and Adroit protocol drivers rely on certain network drivers being operational before they can run. If this is the case, you will have to install any networking protocols required in the documentation. If the front-end computer is using one protocol, the Adroit scanning station must be running similar or compatible network lay

l have to install any networking protocols required in the documentation. If the front-end computer is using one protocol, the Adroit scanning station must be running similar or compatible network layers before communication can be established. To see which network software you have loaded in Windows, you must open the Network Connections in the Control Panel , select the existing network connection, right-click and select Properties , select the software component and network card in question in this dialog, and click on the Configure button. Also check that there are no disabled networking software components. -->

Configuring Accumulator Agents Top Configuring Accumulator Agents You are typically required to configure an Accumulator agent to analyse an accumulating process value and to calculate its difference in value (or change) between successive events or over a specific time (interval) . To do this, click on and read each of the following options: 1. Open the Accumulator agent dialog First, open the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog as follows: Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . If an agent does not exist, you may add an Accumulator agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . Right-click and select the Edit option to display the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog. 2. Define the accumulating value In the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog, you can specify the accumulating process value that you want to monitor and assess, in one of the following two ways: Find the inputTag property, click the browse button then select the slot which represents the ever-increasing process value. In this case, the selected value of this tag will be assigned to the inputValue slot. If the inputTag slot is NOT specified, then you need to drive the inputValue slot, typically by scanning t

value. In this case, the selected value of this tag will be assigned to the inputValue slot. If the inputTag slot is NOT specified, then you need to drive the inputValue slot, typically by scanning this to the required accumulating process variable stored on the front-end device or using a script or expression. 3. Specify how you want each period to be defined Typically, you define a constant interval of time over which the differential increases in value is calculated. The agent provides you with the ability to select the method you’d prefer to use. You do this on the intervalMode slot property, as follows: Note: The triggerNow slot (and button) performs a manual end of period, which is effective in any mode selected by this intervalMode slot. IntervalMode options 0 - 2 These first three interval options use the intervalTag , which is a tag you can browse to set when the end of an interval has occurred: 0 = Interval tag value goes to zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes fro

of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from a value of zero [0] to any non-zero value. 2 = Any interval tag value change The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes in value to any other value (a different value from its current value). IntervalMode options 3 - 4 The next two options let you to define the required interval by making use of the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the duration of each period in minutes: 3 = Synchronised (to clock - default) The agent forces the periods to be synchronised with the system time (i.e. the time of the Agent Server computer) . Therefore, the initial period of the current hour always begins at the start of the current hour (0 seconds or 0 minutes) which is how the current period is calculated when this agent is enabled. As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 mi

t is enabled. As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 minutes past the hour and end at 20 minutes past the hour, and so on. A further example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 3 with an interval of 10 minutes and the agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:10 for this mode (a partial interval of only 8 minutes to enforce the ending time of this period, which began at 10:00 even though the agent was only enabled at 10:02) . However, if this same agent is enabled at 10:45, then the first period will end at 10:50 for this mode (a partial interval of only 5 minutes to enforce the ending time of the current period, which began at 10:40). Important: If you are using this method, then you need to ensure that the specified interval is divisible into 60 or is a multiple of 60 otherwise period timing errors will occur. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interv

r. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interval number of minutes to this starting time. For example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22, and so on. IntervalMode option 5 If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to. 5 = Manual trigger The rate of change and its alarm limits only applies when using periods that have regular intervals. 4. Configure the required alarm limits and if necessary their deadband If necessary, you can configure the alarm limits and the deadband when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and preven

and when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. In other words, this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area outside these alarm limits, which the value must reduce by before the alarm is cleared. Important: The deadband slot ONLY applies to the alarm limits for the differential value and NOT to the rate of change alarm limits. Alarm limits The following alarm limits can be defined for the differential value in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog: The valueHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHighHigh default alarm type. The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm li

type. The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHigh default alarm type. The valueLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLow default alarm type. The valueLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLowLow default alarm type Note: Whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low alarm must, by definition also be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. Rate of change The following alarm limits can be defined for t

Rate of change The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. The rateHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHighHigh default alarm type. The rateHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHigh default alarm type. The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate is lower or equal to th

efault alarm type. The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLow default alarm type. The rateLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLowLow default alarm type. 5. Configure the SQL Server database to store the values of each period To maintain a history of the differential values for each period you must specify the SQL Server database and table that is used to store these records: Specify the connection string to this SQL Server database in the connection field by using the Data Link Properties dialog. For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in th

dialog. For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field. By default, this table name is set to the name of this Accumulator agent. Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups Top Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. To configure automatic WGP file backups Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. Click the Agent Server tab and click on the Advanced… button. Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. The following settings are contained within the WGP Versioning group: These files are created when the WGP file is saved for the period of time specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box, where # is the required number of days. The default period is 90 days and any backup WGP file older than this time will be deleted every time the WGP file is saved. Tip: It is recommended to set this value to the period of your existing Adroit backups, so as to avoid backup duplication. Note: A value of 0 will disable this feature and remove all the backup files on the next save. The minimum number of backup files that will always remain can be specified using the … but keep a minimum of # backup files edit box, where # is the required number of files. This should be used as a failsafe to prevent ALL the previous backups from being deleted if the WGP file is saved after the period specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box has elapsed. riod specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box has elapsed. The total number of backup file that are created can be limited, by specifying the required number in the … and a maximum limit of # files edit box, where # is the required number of files. In this way it is possible to regulate the amount of disk space that is used for these backups. Configuring Command Agents Top Configuring Command Agents The Command agent can receive textual commands in SMS messages that it is able to remotely configure or "command" Adroit . SMS messages can also be sent either manually or automatically and, if necessary, be sent via another Command agent to another recipient, such as a colleague or escalated up the management chain. This agent requires a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver, to be added and correctly configured, in order to send and receive SMS messages. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Each Command agent is able to send SMS messages to a single recipient. For details see, Sending SMS Messages or for details on specifying this required phone number, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . Note: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Sent SMS messages can be monitored for auditing purposes and if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period can also be sent to another recipient via an

of identical messages. Sent SMS messages can be monitored for auditing purposes and if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period can also be sent to another recipient via another Command agent, which can be used to escalate this message up the management chain, if necessary. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . Note: Although Command agents can also receive SMS messages from their recipient, one or more additional cell phone numbers can also be specified that are able to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . If a Command agent is required to receive COMMANDS within these received messages, this must be MANUALLY ENABLED. Since once enabled, these commands can be used to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities Top Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance so that you can filter your incidents, based on their priority. There are two ways to prioritise your incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). : Per Agent: Use this method if ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent have the SAME priority. Alternatively, use this method to specify the LOWEST priority for the incidents (alarm types) of this agent and then use the other per-incident method to specify the incidents that differ. Five levels of importance are supported from 0 the lowest up to 4 the highest. To configure an agent-specific priority: Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator dialog. For details, see To Select an Agent . Click the Header button. Specify the required priority level for ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent, in the Alarm priority edit box i

figurator dialog. For details, see To Select an Agent . Click the Header button. Specify the required priority level for ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent, in the Alarm priority edit box in the lower right corner of the Agent Header dialog, as follows: 0 : lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 2 (normal). The Alarm agent will discard any alarms that are triggered if its own priority filter is greater than that of the alarmed agent it is monitoring. Per Incident: Use this method if SOME incidents of an agent have DIFFERENT priorities. For instance the High alarm limit of an Analog agent will have a lower priority than the HighHigh alarm limit. Note: The agent priority setting is the default priority used when configuring an incident for the first time, thereafter the incident priority setting is always used. To configure an incident-specific priority: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . Configuring Monitored Tags Top Configuring Monitored Tags The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . The Tags tabbed page is displayed by default, when this utility is launched. This page contains and manages the list of tags (agent.slot), whose values are monitored by this utility. Interaction with this page is dependent upon whether the status of the tag monitoring process, as follows: Note1: The list of tags configured by this page is saved, when the utility is saved. Configuring the Agent Server Top Configuring the Agent Server The Agent Server is the storage facility for all real time and historical data. For further details, see About Agent Servers . The real time data resides within intelligent objects, known as agents, which exchange messages with other agents or picture objects either from their local host computer or from remote computer nodes elsewhere on the network. For details, see About Agents . Historical data is written to disk where it is available for rapid retrieval and on-line analysis. For details, see Logging Values . The Adroit database (.WGP) file or load file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For details, see About Adroit Database Files . The Agent Server Configurator creates, manages and stores the configured agents and their slots (values) in the Agent Server. For further details, see the list of available agent types and their slots (values). Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific men

f available agent types and their slots (values). Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Note: The Project Explorer can also be used to configure the Agent Server. For details, see The Project Explorer . Before you can create or edit any agents you must be connected to an Agent Server. If necessary, you can manually specify which Agent Server the Configurator should connect to and configure. For details, see Connecting to an Agent Server via the Classic UI . Note1: Only when these changes made to agents are saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents . Note2: These agents can also be exported to CSV files for editing by 3rd part

saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents . Note2: These agents can also be exported to CSV files for editing by 3rd party applications and then imported into the Agent Server. For details, see Exporting and Importing Agents . Related topics Agent Server Connection Methods : Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. Proxy servers : An Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Clustering Agent Servers : A mechanism for providing client and server redundancy, previously known as hot standby.
