Configuring the DBQuery Agent Top Configuring the DBQuery Agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below. The agent dialog provides the ability to set several options: (See the Configuration slots option for more information.) Enable or disable the functionality of this particular agent. Disable transactions executed on the standby server. Select the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the required tag list. Enter the required Table name . Enter the WHERE clause containing tag names within an angled bracket (< >) pair. The agent automatically substitutes these tags into values first and then performs the following example SELECT statement transaction: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) Enter a custom query. Let’s have a look at a few Custom Query examples. If a SELECT query returns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown belo

rns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown below: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC Because Adroit only uses the first record returned, the example custom query could effectively be changed to: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in the tag list will be ignored because you would add this information to the custom query. Custom SELECT queries will substitute the ‘Tagname’ entries in the tag list with values returned from the custom query, therefore it is important to ensure that the custom SELECT query requests the data in the order required by order of the ‘Tagname’ entries. Other Custom Query examples For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume f

st should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume failure with the above query. Delete records The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019. The query disregards the contents of the tag list in the dialog. DELETE FROM MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (1, 1, 123, 456 ,678, 901) or INSERT INTO MyTable (dt, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (<systeminfo.currenttime>, 1, 1, <f1.value>,<f2.value>,<f3.value>,<f4.value>) Execute Query Automatically The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes SELECT date,timestart,timeend FROM shift_adv_sh1 WHERE idx=<f1.value> Running Stored Procedures The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameter

Configuring the Shift agent Top Configuring the Shift Agent Edit an agent of type: Scheduler . Please use the following sequence when adding shift patterns: Entries that contain a Special date or Day of month value must always be specified first. Special date entries must use the format “yyyy/mm/dd” e.g. 2010/04/04. An example of a “special date” is a public holiday which falls on a different day every year e.g. Easter Monday. Day of month entries must use the format “mm/dd”. An example of a “day of month” is a public holiday which falls on the same day every year e.g. New Years day. Note1: Entries containing a Special date cannot contain a Day of month value too. Note2: Entries containing a Special date or Day of month value force (disable) their Day of week value. Configuring Windows Security Policies Top Configuring Windows Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager provides the following security policies, which affect the Windows operating system of the computer that these policies are applied to, as follows: Configure Power Users: All Adroit users must, at least, belong to the LOCAL "Power Users" security group over and above the default "User" group; otherwise they are not able to perform all the functions necessary to run Adroit on this computer. For instance: if you are NOT part of the Power Users group, although you will able to start the User Interface, you will not be able to start the Agent Server or the Adroit Setup utility. Also if the Agent Server is installed as a service, then the Agent Server will also start. Note: If you are running a domain and you are configuring the domain controller computer, you do not need to perform this configuration as this computer already has a POWER USERS group and the Adroit users are already assigned to this group. Enable Auto-Logon: If enabled this setting allows other users to start your computer and use the account that you establish to automatically log on. For instance: many SCADA inst

signed to this group. Enable Auto-Logon: If enabled this setting allows other users to start your computer and use the account that you establish to automatically log on. For instance: many SCADA installations create a user that is part of the Adroit Operator security group called DefaultOP, which is used to auto logon to Windows. For this reason, if you choose to create the default groups, this user is created for you; however you need to make this user a member of the Adroit Operators default group yourself. WARNING! Although enabling auto logon makes your computer more convenient to use, it can pose a security risk. Therefore it is recommended that the user account that you specify has the LOWEST access permissions for the computer and the Adroit installation. To BYPASS the Windows automatic logon to log on as a different user: Hold down the SHIFT key after you log off or after Windows XP restarts. Note: This ONLY applies to the first logon attempt of the computer. Connect ActiveX Method Top Connect ActiveX Method Connection Functionality . Method Connect(computer, server : string) : boolean; This method connects to a specific Agent Server. This call provides backward compatibility as changing the Server property achieves the same result if AutoConnect is TRUE. Using this method will clear the Cluster property. Parameters: Computer - contains the name of the computer where the Agent Server exists or full Agent Server pathname (computer.server). Server - contains the name of the Agent Server to connect to. If this parameter is left empty and a full Agent Server pathname is not specified in the Computer parameter, then the object will endeavour to find out the name of the remote server. This parameter is ignored if the Computer parameter contains a full Agent Server pathname (e.g. john.as). Returns: If the connection succeeds the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE. Use LastError / LastErrorNum to determine the cause of failure. -->

Connect OLE Function Top Connect OLE Function See Also: List of all the OLE Functions . When it starts up, an Adroit OLE Server Data Object will attempt to connect to the default Agent Server running in the local computer. If, however, it is required that the container application interact with an Agent Server on a remote computer, then the following function is used: VARIANT Connect ( LPCTSTR Computer, LPCTSTR Server ) The function takes two input parameters, of type constant ANSI or UNICODE character string (LPCTSTR): Computer: Name of remote computer. Server: Name of remote Agent Server. The function returns a properly initialised, but empty, OLE Automation VARIANT structure when it succeeds. Sample VBA code: p = dataObj.Connect("computer-A", "SERVER-A") -->

Connected ActiveX Property Top Connected ActiveX Property Connection Functionality . Property Connected : boolean; This property contains the connected status of the Agent Server. Control Bits (user modifiable) Top Control Bits (user modifiable) Control Bits fan-out, which means that a slot control bit becomes set or reset, whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits. The fan-out doesn’t happen to a derived status word as in the case of fan-in, but to the raw status value. Therefore if a slot control bit is already set when the agent control bit is reset, then this slot control bit will not be restored to its set state but will remain reset along with all the other corresponding slot bits. Global Inhibit . Log Inhibit . Scan Inhibit . Output Initialise . Operator Inhibit . Alarm Inhibit . Output Enable . -->

Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms Top Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms This topic describes the following best practice process for exporting mimics from the Classic UI and importing these as SmartUI graphic forms: Ensure that your Classic UI mimic is correctly configured Save your mimic in the Classic UI to a XAML file Ensure that the XAML conversion was successful Import this mimic into the SmartUI Ensure that your Classic UI mimic is correctly configured In particular, consider the following points: Note1: Mimics that have been saved in a zoomed state are automatically normalised before the mimic is exported. Note2: Scale picture elements are currently not supported and need to be recreated after importing. Note3: Rotated Rectangle picture elements are imported as polylines and therefore will NOT have rounded corners. Ensure that you have performed the required alignment of your picture elements before exporting the mimic, since the SmartUI uses a different method of aligning objects that takes practice to do. Ensure that all your configured Behaviours are working as desired before exporting the mimic, so that you do not

metadata.title: Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms

text: ince the SmartUI uses a different method of aligning objects that takes practice to do. Ensure that all your configured Behaviours are working as desired before exporting the mimic, so that you do not need to reconfigure them after importing the mimic. IMPORTANT: This especially applies to any template mimics that are being exported, because currently if their Behaviours are edited after importing then they lose their functionality and need to be re-configured. More details: during the importing process, SmartUI Template Sets are configured (which employ alternate sets of spider silks for each template), but when these Behaviours are configured after importing, their configuration is automatically changed to use SmartUI Templates instead (which uses a totally different mechanism of templatization, namely the use of graphic form aliases) This means that unless the appropriate aliases are configured, then this Behaviour loses ALL of its functionality until the necessary aliases are configured appropriately. For details, see SmartUI Templates. Convert all Operator Action Behaviours that use Ramp as a % to use unit(s) instead, since the % Ramp value increment/ decrement is not currentl

metadata.title: Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms

text: gured appropriately. For details, see SmartUI Templates. Convert all Operator Action Behaviours that use Ramp as a % to use unit(s) instead, since the % Ramp value increment/ decrement is not currently supported. Ensure that the Text picture elements have not been stretched in the Classic UI and that any stretched Text picture elements are replaced with a Text picture element of the correct size that has its font set to the required size. So that these do not need to be corrected after importing. Back to top Save your mimic in the Classic UI to a XAML file Save your mimic in the Classic UI, as normal Select Yes to the confirmation dialog to also create a XAML file. This XAML file is created in the same folder in which the mimic is created and simply appends the .XAML extension to the end of this name after the .mim. If this confirmation dialog is NOT displayed, then configure the Adroit 10 Classic UI to save mimics as XAML files (and trends as XML files) first, as follows: Launch the SmartUI Config Editor Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. To create an alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. for an agent, you must provide two of the following three components: a descriptive name for the specified condition, this usually takes the form of a descriptive abbreviation. Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report Top Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report The Scanning Monitor utility can generate a report of your current scanning configuration of an Agent Server to indicate how well this scanning configuration is configured. To generate the scan configuration report: Either browse to the Adroit installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) in Windows Explorer and open the command prompt (SHIFT + right click on folder) and type in the following command and press ENTER: Adrcomms.exe [computer.agentservername] /report Or copy or use the existing Scanning Monitor utility shortcut and add the ' /report ' to the end of the Target field. For details, see Launching the Scanning Monitor Utility . This report is saved to C:\temp\adrcomms report.csv. This c:\temp folder is created if it does not exist. The report is then opened, immediately after it is saved, using the current application associated with opening .CSV files (if one has been specified on the computer). To interpret this scan configuration report: The report is divided into the following sections: Details : describes the actual scan configuration of

Scores : this section attempts to rate the scanning configuration (as a percentage from 0-100%) based on the number of tags configured per Scan agent and the number of Scan agents per Device agent. -->

text: Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Top Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Often incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are set off in a chain reaction that distracts your operators as they only highlight a problem that has already been identified. First-out or SOE (Sequence Of Events) alarming strives to ensure that each incident is unique and is NOT caused by a condition that your operators have already been alerted to. You can implement first-out alarming by creating conditional expressions for your related incidents, so that if an incident becomes active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. , it ONLY enters your alarming system WHEN its conditional expression is SUCCESSFUL. In this way you can disregard the incidents that echo existing problems, so that your operators can focus on the real issues at hand. Note1: If the RESULT of the conditional expression for an incident is a NULL or zero value then the incident NEVER enters your alarming system, so your operators will NOT know about it. Note2: If BOTH a delay and a conditional expression is specified for an incident, then the conditional expression is evaluated BEFORE and AFTER the specified delay expires. To configure a conditional expression for an incident: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required expression for this alarm type in the Conditional expression field at the bottom of this dialog. Creating IOT Expressions Top Creating IOT Expressions The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to allow you to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions. These expressions are saved in the expression slot. Note: You need to insert empty lines to separate multiple expressions. The following example shows two separate expressions as they are displayed in the Expression edit box of the IOT agent dialog: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 As a side note, the expression slot of the IOT agent would actually be saved as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 How to define IOT expressions Note: Any status or controlling IOT slot can be alarmed by creating an IOT Alarm agent to alert the user of an anomaly. The Load template button allows you to load an XML file defining the slot structure of the IOT agent. The Save template button allows you to save the slot structure of the IOT agent to an XML file. Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would have the following structure: <IOT Name="AddingTwoNumbers" Description="This adds two real values together"><Slots><Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/></HeaderSlots></IOT> And the expression slot of this agent would saved as: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 Which, appears in the Expression edit box in the configuration dialog of this IOT agent as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 Note: The use of the empty

Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots></HeaderSlots></IOT> SecsInMinute . expression =status16=slot(secs)>30 Note: This example also shows that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent in order for them to be used, in this case they need to be referred to using the convention status nn in any expressions that you create (where nn is the required status bit number from 16 to 31). Expressions using status slots However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention. So when you use: status16 = slot(z) > 100 You can also use: status(hi) = slot(z) > 100 In addition to referring to the status slots as the status nn or the named status( slotname ) convention, interchangeably, you can also use these on the right hand side of the equation, if needed. As a result, you could have the following expression: status17 = if(status(enabled), slot(abc) > 100 Alarming status slots These status slots used in expressions can be alarmed using IOT Alarm agents . -->

Creating Macros Top Creating Macros Macro can be created to simply the process of specifying commands, since a macro is simply an abbreviation or alias for an ENTIRE command, which once defined, can be used when issuing this command to this Command agent . Before macros can be used in messages, it is necessary to alert this Command agent to their possible existence in its received messages, so that it can correctly interpret them. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Although macros can provide the most intuitive and the shortest command names, they are also the MOST restrictive, since this entire command must be pre-configured in this Command agent, before it can be used. For this reason, they can be used to further restrict or limit the SET-table commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . Note1: Pseudonyms can be used as placeholders for individual tags (agent.slot), if required. For details, see Creating Pseudonyms . Note2: Macros, like pseudonyms, are specific to the Command agent in which they are defined and are not global to all Command agents. Creating Pseudonyms Top Creating Pseudonyms Pseudonyms can be created to simply the process of specifying commands, since a pseudonym is simply an abbreviation or alias for a tag (agent.slot), which once defined, can be used to represent this tag in commands that are sent to this Command agent . Before pseudonyms can be used in messages, it is necessary to alert this Command agent to their possible existence in its received messages, so that it can correctly interpret them and so that any outgoing messages will have the pseudonyms replaced with the full tag. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Although pseudonyms can reduce the typing required to specify commands, they need to be defined for this Command agent before they can be used. For this reason, they can be used to to further restrict or limit the SET-table tags that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . Creating the Control Recipes Top Creating the Control Recipes A control recipe name may be selected from the control recipe list. A new name may also be typed into this field. The first control recipe in the list will have a numerical identity number (id) equal to zero. The second control recipe will have a numerical id equal to one, and so on. The master recipe slot currentRecipeId can be used to select a control recipe using its id. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. Start Control Recipe : Start the execution of the control recipe selected from the Control Recipe List . Only one control recipe per master recipe can be active at once. Stop Control Recipe : Stop the execution of an active control recipe. Add Control Recipe : Add an empty control recipe. Remove Control Recipe : Remove the selected control recipe. Edit Control Recipe : Edit the selected control recipe. See Edit Control Recipe for more information. Test Control Recipe : Test the validity of the selected control recipe. Advanced Control Recipe Properties : Edit the advanced properties of the selected control recipe. -->

Creating the Data Object Top Creating the Data Object For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . The first step is creating the Data Object. Visual Basic for Applications includes a language statement, CreateObject , for this purpose. CreateObject needs only the name of the object as its first parameter. The VBA code for creating an Adroit OLE Server Data Object is then: Dim dataObj As Object Set dataObj = CreateObject("AdroitServer") -->

Creating the Requests collection Top Creating the Requests collection For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . One of the objects exposed by the Data Object is the Requests collection, a collection of individual descriptions for required real-time data. Each description consists of a tag (or agent name) plus the names of all the slots to be monitored. The slot names are gathered into another collection called the Properties collection. Since the Data Object provides the Requests collection as one of its properties, the VBA code to gain access to the Requests collection is simply: Set reqs = dataObj.Requests A single request consists of the tag plus the names of all slots to be monitored. The Requests object provides a method (function) for the creation of blank sets of fields (the Properties collection). This method is named CreateProperties . VBA allows us to create the Properties collection by directly calling the CreateProperties method, which returns a Properties collection: Set props = reqs.CreateProperties() -->

Creating UDT agent types Top Creating UDT Agent Types The UDT Agent Type Designer creates separate Adroit agent types for each UDT (complex data type) that you require. Duplicate the EXACT structure of each UDT by adding properties (basic data types) and, if necessary, configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. IMPORTANT: UDT agent types must exist on all Adroit computers that require access to the UDT agents from the Configurator. Once you have created one or more UDT agent types, you can import them to other computers. For details, see Importing UDT Agent Types . PLEASE NOTE: Every instance (agent created) of an UDT agent type will consume (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. Note : You can only create UDTs that are composed of data types that can be represented by Boolean, Integer, Real, Datetime, String (80 characters or less) and VarString values. Array data types are NOT supported. To create a new UDT agent type Press the Windows key and start typing in UDT Agent Type Designer and select it from the list. The UDT Agent Type Designer utility is displayed. Click the Add new UDT agent type... b

ew UDT agent type Press the Windows key and start typing in UDT Agent Type Designer and select it from the list. The UDT Agent Type Designer utility is displayed. Click the Add new UDT agent type... button in the UDT Agent Types section. Specify the required name for this UDT agent type in the Create new UDT type dialog. Tip : Use a short yet suitably descriptive name as this name appears in the list of agent types in Adroit . Note : Once you have added a name you CANNOT rename it later. Click the OK button. Specifying the Properties for your UDT Specify the first property (component data type) of this UDT in the Add new UDT property dialog. Note: A property of a UDT is equivalent to a slot of an agent. Type in the required name of this data type. Note: If necessary, you CAN rename a property later, by selecting the required property and clicking the Rename selected UDT property... button. WARNING! Renaming properties invalidate any configurations using the older slot (property) name. Click the OK button. Open the Type list box and specify the required data type for this property. Click the OK button. Open the Type list box and specify the required data type for this property. Tip :Ensure that the Selected UDT Properties section indicates the correct basic Adroit data types to represent this property. Note : If you cannot find the required data type then contact support so that we can add it for you. Only clear the Readonly checkbox, if you want to prevent the user from editing the value of this property in the agent edit dialog. Only clear the Public checkbox, if you want to hide this property from the agent edit dialog. Click the Add new UDT property... button in the Selected UDT - Properties section and repeat steps 5 to 10 for each of the component data types within this UDT. Therefore the result of this expression must either be True (1) or False (0). Note: The result of this expression must either be True(1) or False(0). Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Top Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Tag groups are primarily used manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. For details, see Tag Groups . The following criteria are used for creating different tag groups: Physical location: Tags from different parts of the process or plant, can be placed in different groups. Polling Requirements: Tags that require different poll rates need to be placed in the appropriately configured groups. Communication type (Read/Write requirements): Tags requiring the same read / write ability need to be within the same group, as follows: Tags within Normal groups are only able to have their tag values read i.e. to have one-way communication from WanServer to WanClient Tags within Control groups are able to have their tag values read and written i.e. to have two-way communication from WanServer to WanClient AND also from WanClient to WanServer. -->

Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Top Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Since the introduction of the Custom agent a number of customers have put this agent to good use, which is what it is there for. But as with all tools there is both a proper and improper way of using them and the method used directly affects the achievable results. Therefore the following points or guidelines are recommended concerning the prudent use of this agent: If the Custom agent is used purely as a pure container agent i.e. no scripting attached, this should not cause any problems. When using large numbers of intelligent Custom agents (those containing scripts): Always monitor the virtual memory usage of the AS.EXE (Agent Server) process (from startup) during the design and commissioning phase - typically by using the Windows Performance Monitor. Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the C

droit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc As this KPI determines when you should convert your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents, as follows: For 32-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 2 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: exceeds 1.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. approaches 1.5 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. For 64-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 4 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: exceeds 2.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. approaches 3.0 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. Always monitor the CPU usage of the AS.EXE process. Natively, the AS.EXE process runs at about 1-2% CPU load, very rarely over 5%. If your custom agent configuration causes the CPU load to exceed 10-20%, t

s monitor the CPU usage of the AS.EXE process. Natively, the AS.EXE process runs at about 1-2% CPU load, very rarely over 5%. If your custom agent configuration causes the CPU load to exceed 10-20%, then you should ALSO consider converting your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents. Ensure that the code used to create an intelligent Custom agent is optimised. Since EACH instance of this agent uses the SAME CODE to perform its functions. So when the code is poorly written, EVERY error is exacerbated, which can reduce the performance of the entire Adroit system. Custom agents normally have multiple slots scanned, which is no problem in itself. But please ensure that ONLY the required INDIVIDUAL slots are output enabled and NOT the ENTIRE Custom agent. Click for more details: Note: The scan dialog does this by default. Historically, users have simply output enabled the whole agent and this practice was acceptable because, typically, only one slot was scanned in the analog, digital or marshal agents. However, when an agent has multiple slots scanned AND is globally output enabled, any changes to ANY of this agent’s slot values will cause a write message to the scan

alog, digital or marshal agents. However, when an agent has multiple slots scanned AND is globally output enabled, any changes to ANY of this agent’s slot values will cause a write message to the scanning subsystem resulting in scan degradation. In the case of Custom agents the extent of this scanning degradation depends on the number of Custom agents being used and the level of activity on these agents. Note: This rule also applies when configuring scan inhibit. How to Use the Custom Agent Designer -->

Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration Top Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration Data Execution Prevention (DEP) prevents damage from viruses and other security threats that attack by running (executing) malicious code from memory locations that only Windows and other programs should use. However, when this is NOT configured to use the default setting (typically this occurs on Windows Server 2003 although can occur on other operating systems that provide this such as Windows XP etc.), then the Agent Server can become unable to read the HASP at start up, which will cause the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. To check whether DEP is enabled on your computer and to ensure that it is appropriately configured for Adroit to function correctly, please perform the following steps: Right click on My Computer and select Properties . Select the Advanced tab and click the Settings button under the Performance heading. This will display the Performance Options dialog. Select the Data Execution Prevention tab - if you do not see this tab, it is not installed on your computer. The default setting is Turn on DEP for essential

l display the Performance Options dialog. Select the Data Execution Prevention tab - if you do not see this tab, it is not installed on your computer. The default setting is Turn on DEP for essential Windows programs and service only , however computers that exhibit the above symptom will have Turn on DEP for all programs and services except those I select enabled . If not, the problem lies elsewhere. If the DEP option has been enabled for all programs, click the Add… button and browse for and add both the AS.EXE and ASS.EXE executables from the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . Reboot the computer. -->

Data Logging Compression Methods Top Data Logging Compression Methods Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONCE during the specified deadband period: IMPORTANT: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual The logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband. Average a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband.

alue is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband. Average a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Minimum The lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum The highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Of the provided methods, the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time deadband period and this average is then logged at the end of this period. For this reason a 1-hour average (as opposed to a 1-hour interval raw log) will provide a more accurate representation of what happened in the plant, than the same raw log. Since the raw log value will only represent the instantaneous value in the hour, not the average for the hour. -->

Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent Top Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent The method of data sampling offered by the Statistical agent is called STREAMING, whereby all the collected input values are placed in one sample for analysis. Each input value may be collected on an event basis, and is called a STREAM EVENT. The Stream Event method takes the input agent’s values, either when triggered by another agent, or when its input value changes, and calculates the statistical data (Maximum, Minimum, Average, Standard Deviation, Total and Rate) for all the values collected, treating the values as being part of a single sample. -->

text: Data Structure of an Agent Top Data Structure of an Agent Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, which are referred to as agent attributes. Most of these attributes are accessible to clients of the Agent Server as slots of the agent. For details, see About Agent Data (Slots) . An agent's "state", at any instant in time, is defined as the collective values of all its data. Agents have both generic and type-specific data. Generic or header slots are found in all types of agents. Note: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Examples of header slots are: agentDescription for describing purpose of the agent status a 32 bit word recording agent status Type-specific slots pertain only to agents of the specific type. Examples of type-specific slots, this time taken from an Analog agent, are: rawValue: used to hold the raw or unconditioned value read in from a front end device value: conditioned or scaled value of the Analog rawValue in engineering units of your choice engMin: minimum scaled value in engineering units An illustration of the actual values for some of the s

Database Folder Top Database Folder The WanClient application requires a folder to store the files that contain the tag link database, which it manages. For further details on what this database is and what it contains, see Tag Link Databases . By default, this folder is called ‘WanlinkDB’ and is created as a sub-folder off the Adroit installation folder, so its default location is ‘ C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \WanLinkDB’. However, an alternate location and / or name can be specified for this folder, if necessary, by adding the following registry key to the Adroit registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Wanlink Then add the following String value to this registry key and set it to the fully qualified path of the desired folder: (REG_) SZ DatabaseFolder = the fully qualified path of the desired folder e.g. C:\WanClient\Database Note: If this specified folder does not exist, then it will be created as soon as WanClient is launched. WARNING! It is recommended that ONLY advanced computer users should configure the registry, as any mistakes made can severely affect the operation of your computer. -->

Datalog backup and retrieval Top Datalog backup and retrieval Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files, when their associated .LGD files wrap, as follows: these .LGB backup files are created in a “backups” sub-folder that is automatically added to the folder containing the .LGD file; these .LGB backup files are created on a per tag basis, so if you log 10 tags to the same .LGD file, then 10 backup files are created and maintained; each .LGB backup file contains a month of data, so the current .LGB file is updated with new data (each time the .LGD file wraps) and a new .LGB file is only added once a month has passed and each .LGB backup file adheres to the following naming convention: log$agent$slot M-yyyy-mm , where yyyy is the year and mm is the month of the year. In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number

M-yyyy-mm , where yyyy is the year and mm is the month of the year. In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number of files that are created. More details: When creating monthly datalog backup files in Adroit 8.4 , a separate file was created for each day of the month that had data logged, since the file name also included the day that the data was logged. For instance: 1. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-21 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-21-m-11 2. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-22 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-22-m-11 In Adroit 10 , the name of the backup file only specifies the year and month so that now only one file is created for the month. For instance: 1. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-21 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11 2. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-22 10:00:00 would also go to a backup file called 2017-11 This feature can also extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files, since larger log files have the side effect of causing the Agent Server to take longer to

d 2017-11 This feature can also extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files, since larger log files have the side effect of causing the Agent Server to take longer to start up. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. Note: By using this backup feature, you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands. Once created, the datalogging subsystem automatically retrieves the data from these .LGB files, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. This .LGB file-data retrieval process may slightly increase the time required to obtain and view this historical data. More details: In addition to creating .LGB files for Adroit to retrieve historical data, you can also create the associated .CSV files to enable third party applications to trend or report this data too. IMPORTANT: If .CSV files are being created, Adroit ONLY only looks for and uses the data in the .LGB files. Therefore if you have deleted a .LGB file but still has the .CSV file for the same period, Adroit is unable to re

les are being created, Adroit ONLY only looks for and uses the data in the .LGB files. Therefore if you have deleted a .LGB file but still has the .CSV file for the same period, Adroit is unable to retrieve the historical data for this time period. Since multiple backup files are created, a housekeeping feature ensures that the files older than a specified number of days (default 90 days) are deleted from this backup folder. Note: If you want to keep data older than the specified housekeeping period, for future retrieval, then ensure that you have a MANUAL backup procedure in place that moves the old .LGB files are the required folder. This new datalog feature makes the existing backup capability of the Systemdatalog agent redundant, which is configured in the Options section, when logging a tag, by checking the Enable (system datalog) backups checkbox. Datalog Catchup Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog Top Datalog catch-up Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog The progress slot: This displays the progress of the current synchronization process as a percentage of datalog agents that have been synchronised on that Agent Server in the cluster. The tagRestoring slot: This displays the datalog agent that is currently being synchronised by the systemDatalog agent. The information slot: This contains general information regarding the synchronization process including error messages if an error occurs or if the synchronization process is stopped unexpectedly, for instance by putting a 0 unto the start slot, or if the cluster partner is unavailable. The realTimeRate slot: This indicates how many points were datalogged by all of the datalog agents in the last second. The catchupRate slot: This indicates the rate at which data points are being merged into the local datalogs from the cluster partner. The totalRate slot: This is the sum of the realTimeRate and the catchupRate slots. The Qfree slot: This represents the percentage of the datalog buffer queue that is currently free. -->

Date Agent - Slot Details Top Date Agent - Slot Details The Date Agent stores a date and time value. It has the capability of returning the value in a number of ways as depicted by the slots. If TRUE is put into setTime , the date agent will set itself to the current time. The user may change the time stored in the date agent by writing to any slot, except the asciiTime slot. The user may format the way the date and time stored by the agent is displayed in the asciiTime slot, by setting the format slot in a specific way. Note: You should never externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent from a mimic using an operator action. The localtime slot must be used for viewing the time and the ucttime slot MUST be used for manipulating the datetime value. This is by design of the Date agent only. All other time slots in Adroit can be viewed and edited directly. It is generally a bad idea to store an alphanumeric or broken down time in the Agent Server, because clients may exist in different time zones. This is why all times native to the Agent Server are stored in UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which

n different time zones. This is why all times native to the Agent Server are stored in UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time. If clients in different time zones read the same time slot, their time displays should differ. If the conversion to local time is done on the Agent Server level, as it is done in this agent, the user should take care to be totally aware that the time conversion to local time is done in the time zone of that Agent Server, and not in the time zone of the client the user is using. Date and Time Settings Top Date and Time Settings By using the Date and Time option you can change the date, time and time zone of your system's clock. It is important that your system date and time are always accurate as many of the Adroit applications use this to record information and to print reports. For example the Event viewer and Scheduler. To set the date and time . WARNING: Never turn the PC clock backwards because certain internal transactions made after the back-tracking are ignored or rejected due to their timestamp now being "suddenly in the future". This will cause erratic Behaviour in Adroit . The Support Desk cannot deal with problems caused by rolling the system clock backwards. Golden Rule: Don't fiddle with your PC clock!! -->

DbAccess Agent - Slot Details Top DbAccess Agent - Slot Details The DBAccess agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle using Microsoft's OLE DB technology. This agent is located in the following file: T_DBACCESS.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function badTransactions INTEGER Increments when an unsuccessful transaction is made, this slot is not saved and starts at 0 when the Agent Server restarts. connectionString VARSTRING The OLE DB provider's database connection string. dbRowCriteria VARSTRING This identifies the row in the table to transact on. dbSQL VARSTRING SQL string disableStandby BOOLEAN Disable logging, when this Agent Server is clustered and is in standby mode - to prevent duplicate logging. eventlogErrors BOOLEAN Enable or disable the eventlogging of transaction errors. goodTransactions INTEGER Increments when a successful transaction is made, this slot is not saved and starts at 0 when the Agent Server restarts. information VARSTRING General information or error information. For instance, this contains the string "Transaction succeeded' after every successful transaction. listOfDBFields VARSTRING A CSV

arts. information VARSTRING General information or error information. For instance, this contains the string "Transaction succeeded' after every successful transaction. listOfDBFields VARSTRING A CSV string containing a list of database table fields. listOfDBFormats VARSTRING A CSV string identifying the format of the data in the database. listOfTags VARSTRING A CSV string containing a list of input tags. listOfTriggerOpts VARSTRING A CSV string identifying the type of trigger. listOfTriggers VARSTRING A CSV string identifying the tags that will trigger a transaction. runNow BOOLEAN Do a transaction now. runTime INTEGER The time in milliseconds taken to do the last transaction. scheduleOption INTEGER 0 = None 1 = Use any starting time 2 = Use given starting time schedulePeriod REAL The time delay in seconds between scheduled transactions. scheduleStartTime TIME Synchronise the scheduling of transactions at this point in time. start BOOLEAN Enable or disable the connection to the database tableFieldList VARSTRING The list of fields found in the table. tableList VARSTRING The list of tables found in the database. tableName VARSTRING The name of the table in the database to transact o

se tableFieldList VARSTRING The list of fields found in the table. tableList VARSTRING The list of tables found in the database. tableName VARSTRING The name of the table in the database to transact on. transactionType INTEGER 0 = Insert 1 = Update 2 = Delete 3 = Retrieve triggerOption INTEGER 0 = do the transaction when triggered, 1= do the transaction using schedulePeriod and only if triggered. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 Disconnected State is on if there is no connection to the database. status bit 17 Connected State is on if there is a connection to the database. status bit 18 Transaction error State is on if a transaction with the database fails. status bit 19 Overrun error Works only for scheduled transactions. State is on if the transaction time took longer than the scheduled delay period, i.e. runTime in seconds > schedulePeriod in seconds. status bit 20 Connection error State is on if there is a problem connecting to the database. status bit 21 Transaction success State is on if a transaction with the database succeeds. Note: This status slot (and the "transaction error" status slot) is turned off prior to e

ng to the database. status bit 21 Transaction success State is on if a transaction with the database succeeds. Note: This status slot (and the "transaction error" status slot) is turned off prior to executing a new transaction but the user is free to turn it off manually before executing a transaction. Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the Adroit database file (.WGP), see: DbAccess Agent - Database File Format . -->

DbAccess Agent Details Top DbAccess Agent Details This dialog box is divided into the following sections: Agent Details: This specifies the name and type (DbAccess) of the agent Transaction information: Duration of last transaction: Indicates the amount of time in milliseconds, for the execution of the last transaction with the database. Information: Shows the status of the connection to the database table and any other errors associated with the current transaction with the database. This contains the following string: "Transaction succeeded" after every successful transaction. SQL Statement: Displays the constructed SQL statement that is used to perform the transaction with the database. Refresh: click this button to get updated transaction information. Note: If a connection fails, due to network problems etc. the DbAccess agent will recover and continue transacting. -->

DbAccess Scheduling Configuration Top DbAccess Scheduling Configuration Enable the Run every option to configure scheduling, which also enables the Synchronised at and And only if triggered options. Specify the time delay period and then the required units of time, the default units are seconds (the other available units are minutes, hours and days). Synchronised at can be enabled to set the starting time of the scheduling, this also enables its associated browse button . When clicked this enables the Enter the starting time for scheduling dialog. To configure this starting time: either use the Date and/or Time edit fields to specify the required future time or click the Now button to set the time and date to the current time. -->

DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering Top DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering This enables the remote execution of the configured transaction by the DbAccess Agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling are configured in the dialog box which is displayed after clicking the Edit… button in the main edit window of the DbAccess Agent. The remote-execution mechanisms of the transactions are: Triggering only: This is used when the transactions are only required after a particular condition has been met by the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions . When one of the conditions, in the list of triggers, is met – then database transactions are executed by the DbAccess Agent. Scheduling only: This is used when the transactions are required at a set period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the scheduling to be configured . Triggering and Scheduling: In this case a transaction will be executed when its scheduled and whenever a condition in the list of triggers is met

time. This requires the scheduling to be configured . Triggering and Scheduling: In this case a transaction will be executed when its scheduled and whenever a condition in the list of triggers is met. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling . (Note the And only if triggered option remains disabled for this option) Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the scheduled transaction will only be executed if a condition in the list of triggers is met at the configured transaction ‘Run Every’ time. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple transactions. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling and enabling the And only if triggered option. -->

DbAccess Trigger Configuration Top DbAccess Trigger Configuration In order to use triggering as an option, at least one triggering expression is required, which involves a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). and a triggering condition. Each triggering expression consists of the following columns: Index column: This is added to each trigger automatically and is only used as a means of reference. Trigger column: This contains the tag that is be compared to the triggering condition, to determine when the transactions are to be executed. Either type in the tag directly into this column or click on the column and use the displayed browse button (...) to browse in required the tag. Condition column: This contains the triggering condition, namely: when zero, when non-zero and when changed. Buttons To add a new triggering expression, simply click the button. To remove a triggering expression, click the button. -->

DBQuery Agent Slot Detail Top DBQuery Agent Slot Detail The DBQuery agent contains various slot categories. Select the options below to view more information on each category. DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds may be entered that will determine the execution interval of the transaction. A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query

ion interval of the transaction. A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that wil

f [0] will disable the pulse. Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. text: Default agent groups Top Default agent groups The Agent Configuration dialog allows you to limit the available agent types displayed in the Type list to better facilitate the selection of the required agent when designing your system, by checking or unchecking the following default agent group checkboxes in the of the Agent filter section of the Agent Configurator dialog: Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Basic : these agent types form the basic building blocks of a system and are used for gathering, handling and processing data to and from the physical external world. Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, MultiState, String, StringList, Timer Advanced : these agent types provide pow

andling and processing data to and from the physical external world. Accumulator, AgentGroup, Alarm, Alarm List, AlarmManagement, ARec, Command, DbAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Recipe, Scheduler, Script, Shift, Statistical MIS/MES : these are very specific and usually quite complex agent types used to do monitor, control and solve higher level shop-floor and general industrial challenges. MaxDemand, OEE, PID IT : these agent types facilitate the integration and management of SCADA and IT Audit, DumpConfig, ICMP, Perfmon, SNMPMgr System : these agent types are used internally to perform certain SCADA and other specific functions. Note: Instances of these Agents are created automatically and cannot be added manually by the user. these Agents are created automatically and cannot be added manually by the user. Default Alarm Management Queries Top Default Alarm Management Queries The following queries are displayed by the View data and unless otherwise noted the View graph dialogs: Tip: You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements. Click for more details: Click the Edit KPI's button in the Edit AlarmManagement agent dialog; in the Edit Alarm Management KPI values dialog, double click the appropriate KPI (row) to change its value. Current incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions are still active and/or which have NOT been fully responded to. In other words they still need to be acknowledged and/or have their required reasons specified and/or have their required notes specified. On the basis of 6 alarms per hour this should never have more than 6 incidents under normal operating conditions or 60 under abnormal operating conditions. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions have returned to normal and which have been fully responded to, if necessary, for the specified period of time. In other words they have been acknowled

ncidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions have returned to normal and which have been fully responded to, if necessary, for the specified period of time. In other words they have been acknowledged and/or had their required reasons specified and/or had their required notes specified. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration during set time periods. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by operator: Incidents which have been logged against the specified operator. This can be used to analyse the effectiveness of your operators. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by category: Incidents which have occurred for a specific category. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration for specific process areas. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Outstanding reasons and notes: All incidents that still need reasons and/or notes specified. Only those current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled are added to this list. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Incident count per hour: The total numb

ents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled are added to this list. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Incident count per hour: The total number of incidents that occur over each hour of the specified duration. In other words this query returns the number of logged incidents per hour for the specified duration. Typically each number should be between 6 (normal conditions) to 60 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Burst rate: The number of incidents that occur in a 10 minute window. Calculation: Burst rate = 6 * Maximum alarm count in a 10 minute period. (this is calculated as a per hour count, hence the 6 *) This is an important measure of the usability of an alarm system and the operator's capability to deal with alarms. Typically this should be between 1 (normal conditions) to 10 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Percent upset: The number of hours where there are more than 30 incidents per hour. If you want to specify a more appropriate maximum number of alarms, then change the PUC [Percent upset count] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. Calcula

ere there are more than 30 incidents per hour. If you want to specify a more appropriate maximum number of alarms, then change the PUC [Percent upset count] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. Calculation: Percent upset = 100 * [Number of hours where alarms exceeds 30/hour]/[Total number of hours]. This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: Overloaded > 50% Reactive 25%-50% Stable 5%-25% Robust 1%-5% Predictive < 1%. Priority distribution: The priority distribution for incidents occurring over a period of time. Typically this should be 5% high priority alarms (>Normal priority), 15% medium priority alarms (=Normal priority) and 80% low priority alarms (<Normal priority). But different industries have different standards. Standing alarms: The number of current incidents at the end of an hour. Typically this should be 9. But different industries have different standards. Most frequent alarms (count by type): The most frequent alarms over time, filtered only by the type. Most frequent alarms (count by type and category): The most frequent alarms over time, filtered by type AND category. This shows which incidents take longer to acknowledge and therefore is an indication of the amount of work an operator has to do for an incident before acknowledging it. In addition, by limiting the number of displayed significant places, it is possible to increase the total number of values that can be reported. Note: This setting is ONLY specific to this Command agent only and does not apply globally to all Command agents. To specify the default floating point formatting: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Delaying Incidents Top Delaying Incidents Sometimes you do not want incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). to enter your alarming system as soon as they become active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. , this is typically for one of the following reasons: To prevent intermittent alarms from flooding your alarm system and distracting your operators from the other more important incidents. To ensure that this alarm is raised when the operator needs to respond to it, not too early and not too late. In these cases, you can configure a delay appropriate for each incident . This delay is simply the number of seconds that the alarm system should wait, once an incident becomes active, before this incident is recognised as being ‘officially’ active and is made known to your operators via the configured Alarm routes. Note1: If the incident is cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) ha

recognised as being ‘officially’ active and is made known to your operators via the configured Alarm routes. Note1: If the incident is cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) has returned to its normal operating state. before the delay has expired then the incident NEVER enters your alarming system, so your operators will NOT know about it. Note2: This delay must NOT be LESS THAN the scan period of the tag that creates the alarm otherwise the incident will ALWAYS enter your alarming system, and the time delay is ineffective. Note3: If BOTH a delay and a conditional expression is specified for an incident, then the conditional expression is evaluated BEFORE and AFTER the specified delay expires. To configure a delay for an incident: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required delay for this alarm type, in seconds, in the Delay (secs) field at the bottom of this dialog. Note: If this value is zero, the default setting, t

ent list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required delay for this alarm type, in seconds, in the Delay (secs) field at the bottom of this dialog. Note: If this value is zero, the default setting, then no delay checking is performed and as soon as the incident becomes active it is routed to your operators. -->

Demand Logging Top Demand Logging Batch type processes often require one to log variables only at the end of a batch. In these circumstances, it is not desirable for the data log subsystem to log every change it receives during the execution of a batch. In these cases, Adroit can be configured to only log data values on an exception basis with a configurable time deadband (or maximum logging rate), this is known as (on) demand logging. Configuring demand logging: Use the following three slots of the Datalog agent: Slot Type Description LogNow BOOLEAN The current value is logged to disk every time this slot makes the transition from 0 to 1. Trigger STRING An optional tag (agent.slot) configuration which is monitored for a zero to non-zero transition. When this occurs, a log will take place. Mode INTEGER A variable to control the mode of operation as follows: Normal – change based logging only Demand based logging only Demand and change based logging If necessary, you can ALSO use the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by configuring the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting. For details, see Advanced Datalog Configuration (g

talog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by configuring the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting. For details, see Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) . -->

Demand Scanning Top Demand Scanning What is demand scanning and how should it be used? Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system

y useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for eac

ecome aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adro

icking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instea

at uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to thi

er partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server. this page. Signal Strength: This signalStrength slot is displayed within the Edit Command agent dialog and indicates the strength, in percent, of the current signal of the GSM modem that is being used to transmit and receive the SMS messages. According to the GSM specification, the signal strength must be greater than 29 % to reliably transmit data. According to the GSM specification, the bit error rate must NOT be greater than 40 % signal strength to reliably transmit data. ata. Note1: If this is checked, it does NOT mean that SMS messages will not be sent or received, it only indicates that the current conditions are unfavorable for their successful receipt or delivery i.e. this should be used for troubleshooting purposes only.
