Diagnostic Counters Screen Top Diagnostic Counters Screen The "Diagnostic Counters" Protocol Driver Monitor screen provides a comprehensive list of counters maintained by Protocol Driver. Example screenshot: These counters are all zeroed when the Agent Server starts, and for some drivers, also when the device agent starts. These diagnostic counters can be used to troubleshoot your device communication problems, by providing the following information: “ Transactions ” increment every-time a transaction succeeds. A transaction fetches one or more data points. “ Retry's ” increment every-time a transaction is retried. xxx errors increment when there is a problem communicating. For example, Write errors increment when DTR signaling is configured but not received; by device failure or the cable not having that line wired in. xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communic

l the available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. Retry’s: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. Note: These default dri

mes the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. Note: These default driver performance counters, as well as any driver-specific counters, can also be displayed using the Perfmon agent . Disabling Simplified File Sharing Top Disabling Simplified File Sharing By default Windows XP, VISTA and Windows 7 enables simplified file sharing. This setting must be DISABLED on clustered Agent Server computers because it interferes with the inter-communication between the clustered Agent Servers by making incorrect assumptions regarding this communication. If this setting is ENABLED on a clustered Agent Server computer then under certain conditions one of the cluster partners does not see/detect the presence of its cluster partner. In other words, one cluster partner detects both Agent Servers, while the other detects only itself. This causes the master-standby switchover to fail, resulting in an unstable cluster configuration. How to disable this simplified file sharing setting: Open Windows Explorer. (Click the Start menu, Programs, Accessories and Windows Explorer item.) Open the Tools menu. Displaying Alarms in Adroit Top Displaying Alarms In Adroit incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). (alarms) are stored in alarm lists, which allow them to be displayed and/or acknowledged, typically by using Alarm List Viewer windows in the Classic UI which connect to a SINGLE alarm list at a time. Both the Alarm agent and AlarmList agent provide alarm lists, with the following differences: While the alarm list of an Alarm agent contains ALL the incidents of the agents that it is monitoring, an AlarmList agent ONLY contains the incidents of the agents that are specifically routed to it. ONLY the alarm list of an AlarmList agent allows users to LOCALLY acknowledge alarms. BOTH alarm lists (of an AlarmList and Alarm agent) allow users to GLOBALLY acknowledge alarms. Typically AlarmList agents are only required when you want to view alarms by process area or device. However, if you use MORE THAN ONE Alarm agent, you are UNABLE to display ALL the active incidents for your process in ONE Alarm L

only required when you want to view alarms by process area or device. However, if you use MORE THAN ONE Alarm agent, you are UNABLE to display ALL the active incidents for your process in ONE Alarm List Viewer window, UNLESS you create a GLOBAL AlarmList agent and route ALL your incidents of ALL your Alarm agents to this GLOBAL AlarmList agent. This may mean that you need to specify more than one AlarmList as an alarm route destination for an incident, if you ALSO want to route an incident to another AlarmList agent, say one that only displays incidents for a specific plant section. For more detail on the merits of globally and locally acknowledging alarms, see About Alarm Acknowledgement . Dual mode tags Top Dual mode tags When using tags within control groups, it is recommended to also add these tags to normal groups too, so that these tags become ‘dual mode’ tags. However, the ORDER in which these groups are defined within the WanClient tag link database is important, as follows: The normal group is defined ABOVE the control group: This will update the local Agent Server with the current tag value within the remote Agent Server on the appropriate WanServer computer first. The normal group is defined BELOW the control group: This is akin to making the client Agent Server the master for this tag, in that the current tag value within the local Agent Server on the WanClient computer will always be sent first. Note: Tags within control groups can be written to a remote WanServer Agent Server, to update their tag values. This is in addition to merely receiving their tag values, as is the case within normal groups. However, in BOTH cases, dual mode tags enable the Mark bad scan bad indication methodology to be successfully employed when using the On comms start event. For further details, see Scan Bad Indication Methodologies . -->

Edit a Group Top Edit a Group Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . To edit a group: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Click the Edit Groups button to display the Edit Groups dialog. Note: This dialog can also be used to delete groups . In the List of Groups list box, select a tag group that is to be modified. In the Group Title edit box, specify a name for this tag group, which must not be more than 90 characters in length. The Group Type list box, ONLY specifies the communication type originally selected for this group, as follows: Normal: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) should ONLY be fetched (read) from the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. Control: This should contain tag l

ues (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) should ONLY be fetched (read) from the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. Control: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) can be BOTH fetched (read) from AND sent (written) to the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. In the Poll Period edit box, specify the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and specifies a 1 second polling rate. Note: Poll periods can be specified from 1 to 2000 seconds. Uncheck the Enabled checkbox, if the tag links within the tag group is not to be communicated to for a period, but will be required in the future and so should not be deleted. Click the Ok button to accept the changes made to the list of tag groups or the Cancel button to discard any configuration changes and return to the WanClient Configurator. -->

In the Local Tag edit box, specify a name of the required Adroit tag, located in the local Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer. The Method list box, is disabled, since this only applies to tags within normal groups, in which case the WanServer will return the current value of the specified remote tag.

Effective Alarm Characteristics Top Effective Alarm Characteristics The characteristic of an effective alarm is that it should be: Relevant: requiring acknowledgment and corrective action i.e. NOT an event that can simply be ignored. Unique: does not duplicate another alarm and is not a secondary consequence of a previous alarm. Timely: is not triggered too long before any response is needed or too late to do anything. For instance, when monitoring for over temperature the High alarm is the most important event, not the High-High alarm because the damage is probably already done at this point! Prioritised: indicates the importance with which the operator deals with the problem. Understandable: has a message that is clear and easy to understand. Diagnostic: identifies the problem that has occurred. Advisory: indicates the action that is to be taken. Focusing: draws attention to the most important issues. While the AlarmManagement agent can ensure that the first four characteristics are met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. For details about using the AlarmManagement agent

met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). , see Configuring Incidents . -->

EnableUnchangedValueWrites Top EnableUnchangedValueWrites WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros Top Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros act as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . Before these can be used, however, it is necessary to specify whether a Command agent should examine its received messages for pseudonyms and/or macros, so that these can be correctly interpreted. To alert a Command agent to possible pseudonyms and macros in received messages: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Pseudonyms and Macros tab. Ensure that the Expand pseudonyms in messages checkbox, is checked. Note: Once this checkbox is checked, the ExpandPseudos specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate that any pseudonyms and macros specified in a received message will be correctly interpreted and any outgoing messages will have the pseudonyms replaced with the full tag. For details, see Specific Status Bits . -->

Enabling the Changing of OID Values Top Enabling the Changing of OID Values You can change (write to) OID values in the managed device, so that you can remotely control the device from Adroit . Each OID value that you want to control requires an associated tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). , since the OID value is only written to when the value of this tag changes. text: Enhanced Data Logging Top Enhanced Data Logging The data logging sub-system of Adroit provides the following enhancements: Improved performance : using the datalog change queue to improve the data logging sub-system performance. Demand logging : configuring Adroit to only log data at specific times or events, such as at the end of a batch. Multiple log sets : instead of specifying only a single rate and period per datalog agent configuration, you can create multiple log sets within a single datalog agent. Improved Integrity : the Agent Server ALWAYS honors the data log settings as found in the agent database (WGP) file to prevent Datalog agent exceptions. Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) : all the global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub-system can be configured from a single dialog, whenever a user logs a tag. To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure . -->

Evaluation Options for Expressions Top Evaluation Options for Expressions There are two options available to you in this group, whether the expression is to evaluate continuously or only when triggered by a change in the trigger input slot. If the continuous option is selected then a new result will be generated whenever any of the inputs change or even if the expression itself changes. By design, a triggered Expression agent will always generate subscription updates for the value slot even if the value slot has not actually changed, which can lead to unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. These unnecessary subscription updates can be disabled, by adding the PropagateTrigger registry value. Note: When selecting the Continuous option ensure that there are no cyclic relationships between outputs and inputs. If such cyclic dependencies exist for a continuously evaluating expression Adroit is likely to become unresponsive. -->

Event Log Settings Top Administrative Tools - Configuring Event Logs As Adroit utilises the Applications log of Windows, you need to configure this event log to set an appropriate size to contain and/or overwrite old events. To configure the Windows event logs From the Start menu, click on the Control Panel link and double-click on the Administrative Tools applet. Double click on the Event Viewer icon. In the left pane, expand the Windows Logs item and do the following for each of the event logs i.e. Application, Security and System: Right-click on the event log and select Properties and in the General tab: Set the Maximum Log size to suit your requirements. A typical Adroit event record uses 500 bytes of disk space, therefore if the maximum log size is set at 512 Kilobytes, then it is possible to accumulate 1024 event records. Note: It should NOT be necessary to perform the following configuration, as this is automatically configured by Adroit . The existing Adroit configuration must be extended to provide support for the routing of only certain important alarms to various personnel. The plant consists of four dams that are modeled using the four analog agents, dam_level_1, dam_level_2, dam_level_3 and dam_level_4. Each of the analog agents are currently alarmed on the high and high-high alarm limits using route 2 of the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Route 2 sends alarms to an alarm list agent, dam_level_alarm_list, and to the local event log. The high-high alarms for the analog agents, dam_level_1 and dam_level_2 are very important to Harry and Sally and they would like these alarms to be routed to their cellular phones when these alarms become active. text: Examples of Expressions Top Examples of Expressions IMPORTANT : There are cases when certain operators do NOT follow their prescribed order of precedence - so please use parentheses to enforce the required precedence in your expressions. Example of altered precedence: Consider the expression: v1 | v2 & v3 These operator precedence rules say that & has precedence over | So this IS the same as: (v1 | (v2 & v3)) However, you add a ! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3)) However, this is not the case, it is actually treated as the following by expression agents: (((!v1) | v2) & v3) Do if true – else stay the same v1? v2 : v99 IF v1 TRUE, value = v2, ELSE value = old value (v99) Logic expression !v1 & !v2 means value IS (NOT v01) AND (NOT v02) ( e.g. if v1=1 and v2=1, then v99=0) v11| v12 means value IS v11 OR v12 Nested expression v01 <= v02 ? 0 : (v01 >= v03)?1 : v99 means: Turn a digital on then value goes too low, but leave it on until the value goes above the HI, with: v1=input value, v2=lo and v3=hi Totaliser expression (v0

Extended SQL Querying Top Extended SQL Querying If no row identifier is specified, then the selected (update, delete or retrieve) transaction could return multiple records and even if a row identifier was specified, the first record returned was always used for the transaction. Note: It is assumed that the user is familiar with the SQL querying language and is able to perform SQL queries unassisted. However it is also possible to specify which record is to be returned first, by adding the following commands to the SQL Query in the Identify Row edit box: In order for the DBAccess agent to use the first sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname In order for the DBAccess agent to use the last sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname DESC Note1: "fieldname" refers to the name of the field by which the table will be sorted in ascending order (from the largest to the smallest) Note2: Only add the "$" character if this is the ONLY SQL query command. Extracting Logged Data Top Extracting Logged Data Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract which retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting only of DataLog agents (see Grouping Agents Together ), or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period. Tip: To provide decimal resolution for real logged values that are retrieved using this Extract utility, use the ExtractFloatResolution registry value. The data is then converted into a CSV (comma separated value) file format, which can be opened by a third, party application such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. When using the Extract utility to transfer logged data from Adroit to an external system for further processing, you can reorder and/or remove some of the default CSV columns, as follows: Use the command line parameter: -COL to define the required subset and/or ordering of these default columns in the CSV file. Simply append the lowercase letters that represent each default columns to the end of this -COL command line parameter, in their required order. The following lowercase letters: d, t, n, c, v, u, q represent the following respective default columns: Date, Time, (tag)Name, D

the end of this -COL command line parameter, in their required order. The following lowercase letters: d, t, n, c, v, u, q represent the following respective default columns: Date, Time, (tag)Name, DesCription, Value, Units, Quality. Usage example: -COLctv will produce an output CSV file that ONLY contains the Description, Time, Value columns in this order. Note: The existing keywords -TERSE, -UCT, -UNIT still work as they did before. The syntax of the command is as follows: extract mc.as,ag[,start[,end[,intl[,csvfile]]]] The abbreviations are as follows Note: no spaces between arguments, [ ] denotes optional : Symbol Description Format Example mc computer name Text with no spaces [ ] denotes optional i.e. if computer is not local AEPCY4 as Agent Server Text with no spaces WestPlant ag agent group of datalog agents or a datalog agent Text with no spaces REPORT01 or LOG$ANA01$value Either start start date:time yyyy-mm-dd:hh:mm:ss or existing agent.slot (of type string) 1993-10-5:10:20 (default 24 hours ago) or START.value end end date:time yyyy-mm-dd:hh:mm:ss or existing agent.slot (of type string) 1993-10-6:10:20 (default current time) or END.value Or start time period hh:mm:ss or

Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations Top Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations Calculation duration The OEE agent uses a background engine to update the monitored KPI or OEE in real-time. Any changes made to the input slots, determines how this background engine does its calculations. Note: Ensure that your Adroit license has specified the required number of OEE agents, which are specified in groups of 10. WITHOUT specifying the licensed number of OEE agents, only one instance of an OEE agent has its background engine enabled. All other agents will appear not to be running. By default, the agent records the OEE or KPI based on shift numbers, which are determined by the Shift agent specified by the Shift tag field of the edit dialog ( shiftAgent slot). For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . At the end of each shift the OEE or KPI is recorded and automatically reset for the start of the next shift. If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a “per batch” basis, then: Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. Note: The action of re

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: ” basis, then: Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. Note: The action of resetting the agent, automatically creates an OEE data snapshot entry before resetting the data. Tip: If the KPI or OEE is affected by the type of product being produced, then use different OEE agents for the different products. Running time KPI calculations are performed against runtime. Therefore the OEE agent uses the BOOLEAN running slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference runningTag ) that informs the agent whether the process (or machine) is running. Running time is typically automatically incremented by the agent while this BOOLEAN value is ON. IMPORTANT: The OEE agent only supports BOOLEAN tags - so you cannot use an expression value tag. Note: The OEE agent expects that this slot will be OFF if the available slot is OFF. If not, runtime will continue to increment even though availability is OFF. However, it is possible that the process/machine is running but there is no physical production because, for example, a gear has stripped. This causes the measurement variable (the in

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: lability is OFF. However, it is possible that the process/machine is running but there is no physical production because, for example, a gear has stripped. This causes the measurement variable (the input1 slot) to remain static or go to zero i.e. inactive. If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the running time and will raise a downtime alarm status. As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the running time. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot. Available time Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum available time. This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot shoul

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: ermine the maximum available time. This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF. Tip: This slot can be controlled by the output of a Scheduler agent that is configured with the applicable maintenance/lunch/tea times etc. For details, see Configuring the Scheduler agent . Complex mode and KPI calculation To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case the input1 slot is divided by time. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode. Note: OEE agents operating in complex mode CANNOT calculate OEE. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Total for the Shift for input 2)/Target KPI OEE calculations The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the followin

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: mode CANNOT calculate OEE. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Total for the Shift for input 2)/Target KPI OEE calculations The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production. Calculated as the equipment uptime (actual production – see 2.5 above) divided by the time that the equipment was available (see 2.3 above) for use. Performance Percent of total parts produced against the design capacity (optimal production rate) per time frame. Quality Percent of good sellable parts out of total parts produced per time frame multiplied by the Quality factor % value. Quality factor Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefor

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: multiplied by the Quality factor % value. Quality factor Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefore, the OEE agent calculates the quality using the reject and total counts for the shift, which is multiplied by an external quality factor, expressed as a percentage. This Quality factor % value (the qualityFactor slot) is the external quality factor whose value (0 to 100) must be driven externally. The default value is 100%. -->

General Description Top General Description Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. The word "replicate" is key to understanding the operation of Wanlink. In other words, Wanlink allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN), because data can be read from the Agent Server and also written back. But the transmission and reception of this data behaves in an indirect manner, and not directly as a normal remote node would, since speed is the most important limiting factor when communicating across a WAN. Wanlink, is comprised of two components, namely the WanClient and the WanServer , where the WanClient component performs all the tag and communication configuration so that one WanServer to have multiple WanClient connections. Therefore a computer running an Agent Server and a WanServer, can act as a data concentrator and only send the relevant, requested data to a number of remote Agent Server computers, each with their own WanClient. This is far more efficient, since the data replication to these WanClient computers can either be full or partial (depending o

a number of remote Agent Server computers, each with their own WanClient. This is far more efficient, since the data replication to these WanClient computers can either be full or partial (depending on the remote WanClient’s configuration) thereby increasing efficiency. Related links Quick Start How to use Wanlink -->

Getting to know the Collections Top Getting to know the Collections WOSA/XRT Data Objects make extensive use of the OLE collection construct. A collection is an object that is implemented such that a well-known set of methods exists for iterating over the collected sub-objects. The defined Behaviours provide for enumeration, addition, deletion, and access via index. A collection contains only objects of the same class. The way collections are named is to typically call the collection the plural of the collected object name. For example, if we create a collection of objects of class Tag, we would name the collection Tags. In this way, VBA language constructs can take advantage of them, since VBA implements a language semantic known as For Each...In . In practice, once could write VBA code that looks like: For Each T in Tags REM... do something with T.Property Next The code fragment above would enumerate through the Tag objects in the collection. Notice that we can call the current object in the collection whatever we want (in this case T). Since the collection manages only one type of object, VBA assigns the object to the name we specify. WOSA/XRT defines three collection objects: R

t in the collection whatever we want (in this case T). Since the collection manages only one type of object, VBA assigns the object to the name we specify. WOSA/XRT defines three collection objects: Requests, Properties, and DataItems. The following sections will explore these collections and the objects that they manage. -->

Grouping Agents Together Top Grouping Agents Together An Agent Group is a logical grouping of agents, contained within an AgentGroup agent, either for user convenience or to identify a section or a function of a plant. For example, all the I/O agents associated with Boiler No. 1, or all DataLog agents needed to compile, say, a Production shift report could be placed in groups. This has already been done for each of the agent types and for the three pre-defined agent groups of BASIC, ADVANCED and SYSTEM as determined by the postload Adroit database file . An Agent Group can also be used to control several agents contained within a group. For example, the control bits of an Agent Group agent can be used as a way of setting or resetting the equivalent bits for all agents in the group. An agent can belong to more than one Agent Group and these may be displayed by selecting the agent type from the Type list box and its specific name from the Tags list box and then clicking the Groups button. A list of current Groups to which the agent belongs is shown. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Co

. A list of current Groups to which the agent belongs is shown. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Counter agent, will appear in the Current groups list, prefaced by an asterisk (*) e.g. *TRIGGER. These ARE NOT group names. Similarly, the membership list of a given Agent Group can be displayed by selecting the group from the Group drop down list box, whereupon the members will be listed in the Tags list box. The AgentGroup Agent To create a new agent group . Adding agent types to an agent group : this adds one or more agent types to an AgentGroup agent. Adding agents to an agent group : this adds one or more agents to an AgentGroup agent. Listing the contents of an agent group : this displays the agents and agent types that have been added to an AgentGroup agent. -->

HASP Software Protection Key Top HASP Software Protection Key Adroit is licensed via the Agent Server. Typically, this is typically licensed via a HASP software protection key, which is programmed in accordance with the required licence. Note: If using a previous Adroit version HASP with an Adroit 10 installation, the message "Hasp Failure" will appear in the Event Log. Tip: To minimise the possibility of damage or theft, the HASP key may be installed internally within the computer case, using the AladdinCARD, which also provides additional parallel or USB ports. The key must be attached to one of the parallel ports (LPT1 or LPT2) or to a USB port on each Agent Server to provide network-wide protection. A printer cable can be attached to the other end of the key (when attached to a parallel port). WARNING! If this HASP key is lost, the cost of replacement is the current full value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. Historical Alarm mode Top Historical Alarm mode Historical alarm mode allows an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent to save your historical alarms to a SQL Server database. Up to now, an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent only allowed the fully fledged AlarmManagement system to be used for one hour. The main advantage of using this Historical alarm mode is that previously the life-cycle of an alarm, such as when it was initiated, when viewed, when acknowledged and when cleared (removed) could only be determined by looking at several lines from the relevant AlarmList, but now this Historical Alarm mode you allows you to see the full life-cycle of each alarm in a single row in the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table of the Adroit Historical Alarms database that is created for you in the specified SQL Server that you need to specify. IMPORTANT: But this Historical alarm mode does not give you access to the other functionality provided by a licensed AlarmManagement agent, which allows you to fine-tune and optimise your alarming system. Note: This table only contains those historical alarms whose conditions for complete acknowledgment have been fulfilled, in other words if reasons and/or notes

tune and optimise your alarming system. Note: This table only contains those historical alarms whose conditions for complete acknowledgment have been fulfilled, in other words if reasons and/or notes are mandatory for them that these have been specified in addition to acknowledging the alarm. Therefore, ONLY when your Agent Server license is not licensed for AlarmManagement does the AlarmManagement dialog contain a Historical Alarm mode check box. When you check this check box, then the next time that you start the Agent Server, the existing AlarmManagement database tables, if any, are removed and replaced with a minimal set of tables. IMPORTANT: You cannot run the AlarmManagement agent in both alarm management mode and this Historical Alarm mode at the same time and therefore after enabling Historical Alarm mode the AlarmManagement reports will not work! Note1: As usual, you need to have installed Microsoft SQL Server (Express) in order to use this Historical Alarm mode . Note2: If you do not check this checkbox then you can freely use (demo) the fully fledged AlarmManagement system for one hour. However, after enabling this checkbox you no longer have access to the fully fledged

u do not check this checkbox then you can freely use (demo) the fully fledged AlarmManagement system for one hour. However, after enabling this checkbox you no longer have access to the fully fledged AlarmManagement system, unless you uncheck the Historical Alarm mode check box and restart the Agent Server. You can use the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control in the SmartUI to connect to the AlarmManagement database and allow your users to locate and/or filter and/or print and/or export the historical Adroit alarms. Configuring Historical Alarm mode : describes how to configure an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent to log your alarms, so these historical alarms can be viewed later. -->

Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server Top Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server When a standby server joins a cluster, the historical data stored on the master server must be mirrored over to the standby server. This is done in an intelligent manner by only copying over the data that it requires, that is, the data stored by the master during the period that the newly added standby server was down. Note: This is only possible if the cluster Agent Servers have their system time synchronised . This data catch-up is performed by the SystemDataLog agent, called systemDl. For details, see The SystemDatalog Agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. -->

HMI Mode Top HMI Mode HMI mode is a lower cost, simpler version of Adroit and SmartUI , which is a stand-alone solution that supports the addition of up to 2 clients. This cannot be incorporated into a larger distributed project and does not support redundancy. HMI mode is licensed via the HASP and provides for a cost-effective, bulk implementation of HMI software. The Hasp agent LICENCE has a read-only slot called "HMIMode". If a HMI mode HASP is present then the slot value will be 1, otherwise it will be 0 for standard Agent Servers. HMI mode is therefore one of the components of an Adroit license. HMI mode is typically configured on installation. However, you can create configurations using the Full or HMI mode by using the Configuration dialog of the Adroit Config Editor utility. Note: You can only see if the current (active) configuration is running in Full or HMI mode, after checking the Allow Multiple Configurations checkbox. When using multiple configurations (when engineering multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running

multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running in Full or HMI mode. You can also create additional configurations that are based on existing ones, as needed. Note: If you have only installed the Agent Server and not the SmartUI Server, then you can manually put the Agent Server in and out of HMI mode by configuring the HMIMode registry value (this requires restarting the Agent Server). if the Agent Server is licensed for HMI and Adroit has not been configured for HMI mode the Agent Server will display a message box that it cannot continue and it will terminate. The user must either enable the HMI configuration or change the HASP. if Adroit has been configured for HMI mode and the Agent Server is not licensed for HMI, then the Agent Server will continue in HMI mode. s the following agent types: Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! Basic agents: Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, String, StringList and Timer IMPORTANT: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. How Maximum Demand is Calculated Top How Maximum Demand is Calculated Maximum demand or peak kVA demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. Your kVA usage is averaged over a “block” period, ONLY during defined periods of the day when electricity consumption is high. Block periods are typically 30 minutes but could be anywhere from 15-60 minutes in duration. If you are in doubt about the block period that is applicable for you, please speak to your electricity provider for clarification. The block period with the highest kVA value, over the duration of the current billing period (month), is your maximum electricity demand. Maximum demand calculation example: Assuming that the power consumption on a plant over a block period of 30 minutes is comprised of 5 different episodes of consumption as follows: 800 kVA for 5 minutes 200 kVA for 5 minutes 400 kVA for 10 minutes 800 kVA for 8 minutes 1500 kVA for 2 minutes Adroit calculates the maximum demand for that 30 minute period as follows: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA During each of the above five episodes the predicted maximum demand would have been: Episode1: (800*30) / 30 =

period as follows: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA During each of the above five episodes the predicted maximum demand would have been: Episode1: (800*30) / 30 = 800 kVA Episode2: ((800*5) + (200*25)) / 30 = 300 kVA Episode3: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*20)) / 30 = 433.33 kVA Episode4: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*10)) / 30 = 566.66 kVA Episode5: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA If this agent had a configured maximum demand limit of 600 kVA and the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled, then the MaxDemand status bit would have been on during episodes 1 and 5. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI Top How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI This explains the recommended method of configuring your Adroit system to calculate a KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. for specific equipment (machine/s) and/or an entire plant (process). KPIs are either: simple : some production value over time such as ton/hr, total produced or actual run-hours, etc. [KPI% = (Total input1/Run time)/Target KPI] OR complex : one production value against (divided by) another production value, such as kWh/ton. [KPI% = (Total input1/Total input2)/Target KPI] Note: If the SECOND variable is not specified, then the FIRST variable is automatically divided by time. The KPI can either compare actual performance with benchmark (optimum) figures or compare shift performances. For instance you could compare today’s total performance with that of the previous day and/or today's shifts with those of the previous day. text: How to effectively log your data Top How to effectively log your data Like any SCADA system one of the essential requirements of Adroit is to log values, so that they can be retrieved for long term analysis and reporting purposes. At first it would appear that this process is relatively simple, but the logging of values has evolved over the years into a fairly complex sub-system that requires a guide such as this one for you to use this effectively. For instance, in the past it was potentially necessary to log the same tag using different logging rates and log sizes and even different destinations so multiple log sets could be created within a single datalog agent. Now these multiple log sets are no longer required due to subsequent improvements made to the datalogging sub-system. When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, the first decision you need to make is the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Adroit provides the following methods of storing data: IMPORTANT: If rapid logging is required, then use the Datalog agent to log to the propriety Adroit database. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method uses the Datalo

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: methods of storing data: IMPORTANT: If rapid logging is required, then use the Datalog agent to log to the propriety Adroit database. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method uses the Datalog agent and has been specifically designed for the needs of the SCADA industry to provide improved HIGH SPEED logging performance, typically achieving sub-second logging rates. You should always use this logging method if you need REAL-TIME trending of your data within Adroit itself, such as in a chart on a graphic form. Note: Unlike in previous versions of Adroit the logging to databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default in Adroit 10 to force users to use the DBLog agent, which has been specifically designed for this task A table in an OLE DB database : This logging method is ideally suited for logging slow moving data and NOT for high speed logging and can use the following two agents, depending upon your intended reason for storing the data: IMPORTANT: BOTH these logging methods are MUCH SLOWER than when using the Datalog agent due to the inherent inefficiencies of the OLE DB interface, in interfacing with remote databases. Batch processing : In this case, use the DbAccess

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: ds are MUCH SLOWER than when using the Datalog agent due to the inherent inefficiencies of the OLE DB interface, in interfacing with remote databases. Batch processing : In this case, use the DbAccess agent , which is ideally suited for batch processing as it allows you to define your table structure and then map agents to the various fields, so that you can log both TEXT and NUMERIC values separately to create a single record per batch and then requires that you specify the unique trigger to log this batch. However, the DbAccess agent is not suited to logging a large number of tags to a database as it requires that you specify a trigger for each record that you intend to log and does not provide any tag importing functionality. Bulk logging of NUMERIC or DIGITAL tags : In this case, use the DBLog agent , which has been specifically designed to efficiently log large numbers of primarily NUMERIC (e.g. Analog) or DIGITAL tags to databases, by providing bulk triggering mechanisms and tag importing functionality and even housekeeping functionality to ensure that only the most current data is stored in the database. However, the DBLog agent is not suited to batch processing as it uses a

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: importing functionality and even housekeeping functionality to ensure that only the most current data is stored in the database. However, the DBLog agent is not suited to batch processing as it uses a predefined database table so it is more difficult to group the values that belong to the same batch and it can ONLY log TEXT by converting all the logged values to Strings . When logging to proprietary Adroit log files: As previously stated this is a fast logging method facilitated by the Datalog agent that is designed to provide improved logging performance, by using datalog (.LDG) files to store the active logged data and log backup (.LDB) files that store the historical data. You should always use this logging method if all you need to do is to display (report) your data within Adroit itself, such as in a chart on a graphic form. When configuring the Datalog agent, firstly select the required data-logging Mode , which depends upon how this process value is being used as follows: Continuous: the default setting, where Adroit logs data values as and when the value changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: uous: the default setting, where Adroit logs data values as and when the value changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details). This is the default setting as this mode typically applies to most process variables, whose values you want to record for trending etc. Demand: Adroit only logs a data value when the LogNow or Trigger is activated and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details). This mode typically applies to batch type processes, to prevent the logging of every change it receives during the execution of a batch and only log the value at the end of a batch, in this case: The Trigger edit field, allows a String tag (agent.slot) to be specified, which is monitored for a zero to non-zero transition, at which time a log occurs (provided it complies with the . When this occurs, a log occurs provided this value meets the conditions of the specified deadbands. The Log Now button is provided for manually triggering the logging. Both: this is a hybrid mode that uses both the Continuous and Demand data logging modes. Configuring the effective

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: ified deadbands. The Log Now button is provided for manually triggering the logging. Both: this is a hybrid mode that uses both the Continuous and Demand data logging modes. Configuring the effective logging rate It is important to understand that a value is only logged when it changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands , which can be used: to eliminate the nuisance values or noise that can clutter up a log file without providing any meaningful change in value or to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. So the effective logging rate is determined by configuring the Time... and/or Value deadbands, as follows: Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONC

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONCE during the specified deadband period: IMPORTANT: When using the Demand Mode , you need to configure the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting via the Advanced... button, in order to use these Datalog compression algorithms. Note: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time... logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual : the logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband (the default). Average : a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified. Minimum : the lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum : the highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. If you are using the Time... deadband to compress your log file to store more data then the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time d

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: Time... deadband to compress your log file to store more data then the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time deadband period and this average is then logged at the end of this period. In other words a 1-hour average (as opposed to a 1-hour interval raw log) will provide a more accurate representation of what happened in the plant, than the same raw log. Since the raw log value will only represent the instantaneous value in the hour, not the average for the hour. It is important to know that a value is only logged when it changes and when this change in value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands because this means that the specified Length... of the datalog (.LDG) file is only an estimation, which assumes that this value will change substantially at the effective rate of logging determined by the deadbands, however: if the value changes less than the effective rate of logging, then this log file will contain data for more than the specified duration but if the value changes more often than the effective rate of logging, these changes will not be recorded. The Datalog agent al

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: en this log file will contain data for more than the specified duration but if the value changes more often than the effective rate of logging, these changes will not be recorded. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Furthermore, you can use Out of limit logging to bypass this process and immediately log any out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the effective rate of logging, which is specified by the Time... deadband and using the faster log rate specified by the Out of limit logging -> Time... setting instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: s the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1 second intervals. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 10 sec and Out of limit monitoring Time = 1 sec and Upper limit = 225 and Lower limit = 215). Note: In this case he will be able to catch short voltage spikes whose duration whose duration are less 10 seconds, the normal logging interval. Example of this configured dialog: Note: To disable out of limit data logging, set both of the limit values are zero (default values), then NO limit checking is done and the Datalog agent operates normally by ONLY using the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ). Specifying the required logging period Typically the specified Length... of the datalog (.LDG) file should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog size should only be set for 1 day. Note: Any datalogs that ca

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: ses. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog size should only be set for 1 day. Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. When the allocated size of the datalog (.LGD) file is filled, it wraps (starts again at the beginning). At which time one or more datalog backup (.LGB) files are created to store this older (historical) data. The datalogging sub-system automatically retrieves this historical data from these files, when this data is required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. Note: To disable datalog backups for a particular Datalog, set the backupPeriod slot of this Datalog agent to 0 . Tip: You can use these datalog backup (.LGB) files to extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files, since larger log files have the side effect of causing the Agent Server to take longer to start up. In this case, while the active log (.LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for m

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: ave the side effect of causing the Agent Server to take longer to start up. In this case, while the active log (.LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. These datalog backup (.LGB) files also prevent the need to multiple proprietary datalog sets with increased periods and larger time deadbands and also replaced the legacy backup capability provided by the Systemdatalog agent. When the associated .LGD file wraps, each Datalog agent creates their own backup (.LGB) files, as follows: these .LGB backup files are created in a “backups” sub-folder that is automatically added to the folder containing the .LGD file; these .LGB backup files are created on a per tag basis, so if you log 10 tags to the same .LGD file, then 10 backup files are created and maintained; each .LGB backup file contains a month of data, so the current .LGB file is updated with new data (each time the .LGD file wraps) and a new .LGB file is only added once a month has passed and each .LGB backup file adheres to the following naming convention: log$agent$slot M-yyyy-mm , where yyyy is the year and mm is the month of the year. In Adroit 10 , the na

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number of files that are created. How to log the communication of a driver Top How to log the communication of a driver Introduction When troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device. Adroit provides a utility known as the Driver Monitor that is used for just this purpose and one of its functions allows it to display the Datascope window, which allows you to view and log the exact communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. This procedure describes how to create an HTML log file of the communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. So that if you are not a driver expert, you can email this log file to Adroit support, who will then be able to assist you with your driver problem. The advantage of an HTML log file over a text file is that this file format preserves the color of the Datascope window, which makes the troubleshooting process easier. text: How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time Top How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time One application of the Counter agents is to monitor device running/stopped bit to display motor running hours. Due to control system starts, stops, backups and communication breaks, it is often necessary to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) as an operator entry function. So that the Counter agent must resume counting from the new value. The Total On Time and Total Off Time, is saved by the Counter agent in its rawOnTotal and rawOffTotal slots as a millisecond based time value. In other words 1 hour = 3600000 milliseconds. Therefore in order to create a button to allow an operator to specify the Total On Time of a Counter agent, you need to add the following THREE Operator Action behaviours to it: The first operator action sets the contpause slot of this Counter agent to 0. The second operator action allows the operator to type in a new value rawOnTotal in milliseconds (where 1 hour = 3600000 milliseconds). The third operator action sets the contpause slot of this Counter agent to 1. -->

text: How to use the ICMP agent to ensure the availability of a networked device Top How to use the ICMP agent to ensure the availability of a networked device The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. exceeds specified High and High-high times. Things you need to know or do before you can assess the availability of a networked device: Ensure that the network supports the Internet Control Message Protocol. Ensure that you know the IP address of the required device and that this IP address does not change. ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. text: How to use the IOT agent to define an object Top Defining the structure of an IOT agent Configuration This agent does not possess any default status slots and is required to be configured externally. The IOT agent is basically not usable until it’s configuration is defined by using either the addSlot or the xmlSlots slot. Configuration of the agent slots is not currently supported by the agent dialog, however, you may import a XML slot definition file that defines the slots for any single IOT agent. It is typically called from an external source, for example, a browser or 3rd party application. Creating the structure of an object You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it. As only this code knows the identification of the IOT device, it should use the addSlot OR xmlSlots slots of this agent to programmatically create the slots as required. Using the addSlot The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float

metadata.title: How to use the IOT agent to define an object

text: lot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above Using the xmlSLot This XML structure requires that you always specify: the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatStr

text: description that describes the purpose of this property. The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . VarString : any number of characters Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used. Example of the XML structure The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlot

To facilitate easier reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name=" hi "/> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> Any number of <Slots> may be defined. The XML code above can be saved to an XML file as a template and loaded in the IOT agent dialog. text: How to use the Scanning Monitor Utility Top How to Use the Scanning Monitor Utility The Scanning Monitor utility is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. However, OPC Server devices not in "sync-poll mode", and telemetry applications will find this utility less useful. For details of the user interface of this utility, see Scanning Monitor Utility . Tip: The Scanning Monitor utility can generate a report of your current scanning configuration of an Agent Server to indicate how well it has been configured. For details, see Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report . After understanding the user interface of the program and selecting the required device from the Device List , one really needs to only look at 2 things, the "effective" scan rate (rate at which the driver actually returns data), and the polling rate you intended it to use, these 2 values are in column 5 and 6 of the Scan Job List . If the effective rate is consistently greater than the intended rate, you have a scanning backlog. Find the scan jobs with the shortest scan-times, as you select each one, check how many tags (scan points) are scanned in that task in the Tag List , which is i

metadata.title: How to use the Scanning Monitor Utility

text: nded rate, you have a scanning backlog. Find the scan jobs with the shortest scan-times, as you select each one, check how many tags (scan points) are scanned in that task in the Tag List , which is immediately below the scan job list. Consider the communications bandwidth cost of having a task with only one I/O point; at this point one can make the scan-interval of an expensive point longer to remedy this. If all tasks are responding slower than their intended intervals, then a re-evaluation of all the scan-times is needed. For further details concerning the scanning optimization benefit of grouping scanned data, see Scanning Optimization Tips . Since the right-click commands within the Scan Job List that change scan rates are not permanent (in other words saving the Adroit agent database will not save these online changes), it is necessary to perform the following procedure to make any changes permanent: To make permanent scan rate changes: Backup your Adroit agent database file (.WGP). For details, see Backing Up Agent Database Files . Stop the required device agent , and wait a few seconds for any backlogged polling to cease. Export the Device agent type , i.e. click the No but

In the Choose file to contain conversion dialog, select the location to save the Device agent files, it is recommended to leave this as the default location of the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and save the ‘Device.CSV’ file, then save the scan files for each of the device agents, of the name format DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent. When the next agent type message box is displayed, click Cancel , to stop the exporting process. In either a CSV or text editor, open the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent that the tags have been scanned to. text: How to use the SNMPMgr agent to Manage a Device Top How to use the SNMPMgr agent to Manage a Device This agent can both monitor and manage devices on a network, by using the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). Examples of devices that can be monitored using SNMP include routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. Things you need to know or do before you can manage a device: ensure that you know which SNMP version the device supports and that you know all of its connection settings. Since the SNMPMgr agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and SNMP version 3 supports additional connection settings. ONLY if this device is a computer, ensure that you have installed and configured the SNMP service on this computer. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service or SNMP Service Security Configuration . IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. please ensure that the device and your Agent Server license, complies with the specified SNMPM

For details of community strings, see SNMP Community Strings . if you want to control this device, then you need the read/write community string of this device. if you want to control (write) OID values in the device, ensure that their return types CAN be written to by the SNMPMgr agent. text: How to use Wanlink Top How to use Wanlink Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). The following diagram and explanation, briefly describes how Wanlink works and how it is configured: Where: Computer 1 is the "primary" Agent Server (AS1), which obtains its IO from its remote outstations. WanServer is also running on this computer, which is connected to AS1, no other configuration is required. When a remote Agent Server connects to the primary Agent Server using Wanlink, the remote WanClient will connect to and upload its configuration to the WanServer . The WanServer will then establish connection to the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1) and communication based on this configuration will commence from then on. Computer 2 is a Remote node, which is able to view and control data on (AS1) directly because it on the same LAN. Note : Since this computer does not have its own Agent Server, it directly accesses the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1). Computer 3, 4 are the "remote Agent Server

ly because it on the same LAN. Note : Since this computer does not have its own Agent Server, it directly accesses the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1). Computer 3, 4 are the "remote Agent Servers", these Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4), may or may not have local data derived from other IO sources. WanClient needs to be running on each of these computers. The Configuration file of each WanClient , must essentially specify how to communicate to the WanServer and which local tags in these remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) need to be "linked" to tags that reside in the primary Agent Server (AS1) and the communication settings to its WanServer connected to the primary Agent Server (AS1). Note: It is not necessary to link to all the tags in the primary Agent Server (AS1), only link those tags that are required. The WanClient configuration, is performed using the WanClient Configurator , in the following order: A server must be added , which contains the configuration necessary to communicate with the WanServer computer, the primary Agent Server (AS1) in this case and it specifies the database that will contain the links that need to be communicated. Note: This server is "remote" in that

e with the WanServer computer, the primary Agent Server (AS1) in this case and it specifies the database that will contain the links that need to be communicated. Note: This server is "remote" in that it is on the other side of the WAN from the computer that is running WanClient . Now the tags that are required to be linked must be grouped and these groups must be added . The following criteria need to be considered, when group the tags into groups: The primary consideration should be the type of communication is required between the two Agent Servers: Select a Normal group, for links that require a one-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are only able to view the value of a "linked" tag and any changes made to this tag will not be made to its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1). Select a Control group, for links that require a two-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are able to modify the value of a "linked" tag and its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1) will reflect this change. Note: With this method of linking a remote Agent Server ( Computers 3 and 4 ) can operate as if it was a remote node (

d its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1) will reflect this change. Note: With this method of linking a remote Agent Server ( Computers 3 and 4 ) can operate as if it was a remote node ( Computer 2 ) of the primary Agent Server it is being connected to ( Computer 1 ). The secondary consideration is the poll rate of the tags or the rate at which the WanClient will ask for changes from the WanServer , which only affects tag links that have been configured to be polled (this is described below). Once the tag groups have been created, the specific tag links must be added to their respective groups. When creating tag links, the following methods of linking can be used: Polling , in which case the WanClient will ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer at a fixed rate, so that in this case the WanClient will requests the tag from the primary Agent Server (AS1) every x seconds. This method also requires tags with the same poll period to be grouped in the same group. Subscribed , in which case the WanClient will only ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer on startup and when the value of the tag changes, this is recommended for critical data, since it is a more e

bed , in which case the WanClient will only ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer on startup and when the value of the tag changes, this is recommended for critical data, since it is a more efficient method of linking tags over a WAN. Note: This is also possible to manually edit the CSV files in which the links , tag groups and servers are stored, in order to perform bulk configurations etc. PLEASE NOTE 1: The full tag description must be specified when configuring a remote or local link in the WanClient e.g. "MYDIGITAL.rawValue" If the slot name is omitted, the tag link will fail. PLEASE NOTE 2: Historical data cannot be transferred over Wanlink, only current runtime values will be sent and retrieved. It is possible for a linked tag on a remote Agent Server (AS3),(AS4) to be logged as usual, but then Wanlink connection must be maintained at all times to ensure that no "holes" in the remote datalogs occur. -->
