These counters are all zeroed when the Agent Server starts, and for some drivers, also when the device agent starts. These diagnostic counters can be used to troubleshoot your device communication problems, by providing the following information: “ Transactions ” increment every-time a transaction succeeds. A transaction fetches one or more data points. “ Retry's ” increment every-time a transaction is retried. xxx errors increment when there is a problem communicating. For example, Write errors increment when DTR signaling is configured but not received; by device failure or the cable not having that line wired in. xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communicati

metadata.title: How to view the diagnostic counters of a driver's device

text: he available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. Retry’s: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. -->

ICMP Agent - Slot Details Top ICMP Agent - Slot Details The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. exceeds specified High and High-high times. This agent is located in the following file: T_ICMP.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function active BOOLEAN This is set to True when an ICMP message is being sent and/or received from the network device. catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used for datalog and real-time data catch-up). disableStandby BOOLEAN Disable this agent on the standby Agent Server, when the Agent Server is being clustered. failure_Count INTEGER The number of ICMP messages that were not received from the specified ipAddress . hi INTEGER The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send a message to the network device and receive

The number of ICMP messages that were not received from the specified ipAddress . hi INTEGER The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send a message to the network device and receive a reply has moved outside its acceptable range and therefore implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. hiHi INTEGER The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send and receive a message and from the network device has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and that urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. interval INTEGER How often you want to check the availability of this device on the network, in seconds, also known as the required poll rate. ipAddress STRING The IP address of the network device. Note: ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. last_Execution_Time TIME Specifies when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. pingNow BOOLEAN Performs an immediate ping. pingStatus STRING Provides a textual description of the status of the last ICMP mess

me TIME Specifies when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. pingNow BOOLEAN Performs an immediate ping. pingStatus STRING Provides a textual description of the status of the last ICMP message used to contact the device, as follows: OK from [IP Address] if it succeeded; Retries exhausted when retrying to contact the device (a timeout failure) and Host unreachable from [IP Address] if it is not possible to contact the device. retries INTEGER Specify how many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable. roundTripTime INTEGER The time taken, in milliseconds, to send the last ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. start BOOLEAN This is used to enable/disable the sending of ICMP messages to the specified ipAddress . timeout INTEGER Specify how long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable. Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers Top Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers Clustering in Adroit , previously known as hot standby, consists of a pair of Agent Servers (known as the master and standby) running a replicated agent database (WGP file) on the same project. More details: The master server services all the I/O and client tasks, while the standby server replicates the master server. If the master server or computer fails, the standby server takes over as master and its clients and scanning tasks take appropriate action. The following issues are important when implementing an Adroit cluster: Ensure that both Agent Server computers (and their clients) have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively. For details, see Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster . Ideally both Agent Servers, in the cluster, should be in the same Windows domain. If your Agent Server has a cluster partner that is on a DIFFERENT domain or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote Agent Server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . When naming the two Age

text: in or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote Agent Server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . When naming the two Agent Servers that you want to be a clustered pair, if you have a preference for a specific Agent Server to act as master, then ensure that the name of this Agent Server is alphanumerically lower than the name of the Agent Server that will be the standby partner e.g. if the preferred master Agent Server is called AS1 then the standby Agent Server should be called AS2. Ensure that you configure both Agent Server processes, in an Adroit cluster, to have the same (identical) Windows security permissions. If using the Agent Server Service on one of both of your clustered Agent Servers, ensure that the user account under which the Agent Server Service is running has network access to the partner machine. IMPORTANT: It is NOT sufficient that a user logged in on the Agent Server can access the remote machine through explorer since this applies to his / her user account. Improved Integrity Top Improved Integrity When a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is configured to be data logged in Adroit , it is the responsibility of the user to save the server database after the configuration changes have taken place. If this does NOT occur it would result in Datalog agent exceptions, since the configured Datalog agent is out of step with the data in the data log file. To prevent this from occurring the Agent Server ALWAYS honors the data log settings as found in the agent database (WGP) file. This means that the unsaved configurations will be LOST. -->

Improved Performance Top Improved Performance In Adroit data logging is a synchronous activity in that it is done internally on the same thread that creates the value change. Click for more details: For example, plant changes arrive into Adroit via one of the many scan threads. When a scan agent (or thread) has detected a value change, the thread updates the agent as well as any Agent Server clients interested in the information because of their subscription to this value. The datalog agent is one such client. Depending on the: size of the data log file speed of the hard disk available memory and other factors Writing the new value to disk (or to Window’s file caching subsystem) may take a long time. This affects the ability of the thread to timeously update the Agent Server with any other ‘real-time’ changes from the same scan transaction. Click for more details: For example, suppose 256 words of digital information changes every second, that is, 4096 discrete digital points changing per second. The scan agent must be able to effectively update every agent well within 240 uS per agent if it is going to be able to maintain the configured one-second-transaction rate. A sluggish data

per second. The scan agent must be able to effectively update every agent well within 240 uS per agent if it is going to be able to maintain the configured one-second-transaction rate. A sluggish data logging sub-system will definitely prevent this from happening. All changes arriving at the data logging subsystem are now added to a "datalog change queue". Click for more details: This mechanism is similar to the real-time update mechanism within Adroit , however; now the updates that occur because of historical logging requirements do not affect the throughput of the remaining real-time updates. This is a fast operation and releases the calling thread immediately. A separate, asynchronous thread reads the data from the queue and sends the change to the data logging mechanisms. From the above it is obvious that the size of the queue must be such that it is able to handle the maximum spike of changed values that a plant can expect. The maximum number of changes is generally proportional to the number of logged tags. This queue is global and has a default size of 500Kb, which allows for an approximate spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) ra

to the number of logged tags. This queue is global and has a default size of 500Kb, which allows for an approximate spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) rate of plant changes will exceed the rate at which the data logging subsystem is able to operate. Example: In this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement - the PC and/or its subsystems will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers. Tuning Parameters This data log system buffer queue size can be changed by clicking the Advanced button in the Datalog agent edit dialog , use the Datalog system buffer size (Kb) field to specify the required buffer queue size. It is recommended to use the buttons to increase/decrease this value in 64 KB increments/decrements. -->

Incident Icon colors Top Incident Icon colors The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident, as follows: The white icon means that no reasons or notes are required. The yellow icon means that ONLY reasons must be specified. The blue icon means that ONLY notes must be specified. The red icon means that BOTH reasons and notes must be specified. These colored icons indicate what the operator MUST specify for an incident before it is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table and is added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. Note: Even though reasons and/or notes may not be required, they can still be specified. Example: Categories tree shows a hierarchical structure of the categories, while the top right-hand Incidents list displays all the incidents in the selected category and the bottom right-hand category/incident details list displays the selected category/ incident configuration. Note: The incident details list is disabled when more than one incident is selected. -->

Increasing Logging Periods Top Increasing Logging Periods When the logging period is increased when using the Adroit proprietary logging, ensure that the WGP file is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur, for the following reasons: Note: This is NOT required when reducing the logging period. When the logging period is increased: The datalog subsystem create new space at the end of the existing LGD file and copy all existing history to this new space. The datalog subsystem also marks the old space as unused. On the next startup of the Agent Server, all the LGD files that contain unused regions will be compressed out. -->

Increasing the virtual memory available to the Agent Server Top Increasing the virtual memory available to the Agent Server The Agent Server and Agent Server Service processes can use up to 3GB of virtual memory on 32 bit Windows XP and Server 2003 and up to 4GB on certain 64 bit operating systems. Previously, these processes were limited to only 2GB. This feature allows users to extend their WGP file configuration and is particularly useful when your current Agent Server process is approaching the 1.6GB virtual memory limit, as measured by Performance Monitor (NOT Task Manager!). Implementation on a 32 bit operating system: 32 bit operating systems have a maximum of 4GB of addressable memory space. By default, Windows allows only 2GB per process and uses the other 2GB for Windows itself. To change this default, you need to do the following: On 32 bit Windows Vista and later versions of Windows: Use the IncreaseUserVA element in BCDEdit . Click for more details: In other words specify the following command: BCDEdit /set [{ID}] increaseuserva Megabytes , where: The /set command sets a boot entry option value in the boot configuration data store. The {ID} is the GUID that is associat

text: the following command: BCDEdit /set [{ID}] increaseuserva Megabytes , where: The /set command sets a boot entry option value in the boot configuration data store. The {ID} is the GUID that is associated with the boot entry. If you do not specify an {ID}, the command modifies the current operating system boot entry. Integer Agent - Slot Details Top Integer Agent - Slot Details The Integer Agent stores a 32-bit integer value. text: Introduction Top General Description Many Adroit users have various complex devices that contain one or more value properties. Ordinarily, in order for users to represent these complex devices, multiple instances of analog, digital or other common agent types, would be used to represent a single device. For example, your process may make use of a particular drive type; let’s call it Drive Type XYZ. Multiple drives of this type exist in your process. This drive type has a couple of properties, for example Start, Stop, Running, Tripped, Speed and Temperature, requiring each of these values to be mapped to four digital and two analog agents respectively, therefore 10 of these drives would mean 60 agents. Would it not be better to use a single agent representing a complete drive and containing the 6 items of information in 6 slots of the agent, so that, in this example only 10 agents would need to be used instead of 60? The Custom agent, has been designed to do just this, it is a generic agent type used to create user-defined agent types, by means of the Custom Agent Designer, and must not be used in its generic format. But in addition to representing, simple "container" agents, which

gent type used to create user-defined agent types, by means of the Custom Agent Designer, and must not be used in its generic format. But in addition to representing, simple "container" agents, which simply contain or encapsulate the values of a number of previous agents in a single user-defined agent, the Custom agent is also able to provide VB Scripting (or Java Scripting) intelligence to the agent to drive (control) other derived slots of this custom agent. For example, we can add an extra slot to this agent for defining a high temperature alarm value. The script would monitor the actual temperature such that when the temperature exceeds this value a status bit is set for alarming purposes. We can also set a Trip status bit when the Tripped signal is switched on. Furthermore, we can also disable the drive from starting if the temperature is too high. Note: Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will require a scan point license. Tip: Custom agents created via the Custom Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). This drive type XYZ example will be us

om Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). This drive type XYZ example will be used to explain the process of creating a user-defined agent using the Custom Agent Designer. The user-defined agent, created by the Custom Agent Designer, is known as a custom derived agent and will have the following three files associated with it: t_CustomDerivedAgentName.dll t_CustomDerivedAgentName.csv t_CustomDerivedAgentName.vbs / t_CustomDerivedAgentName.jav Note: This file is only required if this custom derived agent has scripting intelligence. Where, CustomDerivedAgentName suitably describes this agent type and is not the same as an existing agent name. Related links How to Use the Custom Agent Designer Custom Agent Usage Guidelines -->

IO Flags Top IO Flags In an effort to simplify the scanning configuration, the following legacy status slots that used to affect how a slot (value) was scanned: Scan Inhibit, Output Enable and Output Initialise are no longer stored in the header of the each agent for each of its slots. Note: The advanced header dialog no longer displays these statuses and putslots to these status bits are also disabled. Instead these settings are now stored in the scanning configuration of the Device agent in the Agent Database (.wgp) file along with the other scanning related settings, such as the scan address, scan rate etc, as an IO flags setting. Hence the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog contains an IO flags column in the list of scanned tags. Note: There is no slot that contains these IO flags, since they are now stored in the tag list of scanned values of a Device agent. When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. Therefore Adroit

to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. Therefore Adroit 10 Agent Database (.wgp) file are NOT backwardly compatible! IMPORTANT: When starting the Adroit 10 Agent Server for the first time and loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version, devices will most likely NEVER show healthy once all the devices are started. You need to save the Agent Database (.wgp) file FIRST and then restart the Agent Server and then you should see all the devices going healthy. The IO flags setting is a bit mask as follows: Value Bit Description Default 1 0 Input disabled ON supercedes the legacy statusScanInhibit flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInhibit flag set, will force Bit 0 OFF. Note1: This setting is the INVERSE of the Input disabled (Scan inhibited) checkbox, when scanning a tag. Note2: You can still use the statusScanInhibit header slot of an agent to prevent any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. 2 1 Output enabled OFF supercedes the legacy statusOutputEnable flag at the agent and

use the statusScanInhibit header slot of an agent to prevent any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. 2 1 Output enabled OFF supercedes the legacy statusOutputEnable flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusOutputEnable flag set, will force Bit 1 ON. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output enabled checkbox, when scanning a tag. 4 2 Output initialise OFF supercedes the legacy statusScanInitialise flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInitialise flag set, will force Bit 2 ON. If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output initialise checkbox, when scanning a tag. 8 3 Demand scan OFF New functionality – requires that the global configuration for demand scanning is enabled and that the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning. The IO flags setting is a sum of the values whose associated bit is ON. So for a newly scanned tag, the default of bit 0 (enable reads) applies, in which case IO flags is 1. If bit 0 (enable reads)

g. The IO flags setting is a sum of the values whose associated bit is ON. So for a newly scanned tag, the default of bit 0 (enable reads) applies, in which case IO flags is 1. If bit 0 (enable reads) and 2 (output initialise) are ON then the IO flags is 5 (1 + 4). For more details on demand scanning, see Demand Scanning . -->

IPEnableHeartbeat Top IPEnableHeartbeat WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". When using sockets as the communication mechanism between the Agent Server and its clients, the socket heartbeats will always occur, as clients will PING the Agent Server every 10 seconds. If you want the Agent Server to monitor that each connection remains healthy and to close unhealthy connections, then implement the following registry setting on the Agent Server computer: This setting enables the Agent Server to monitor the PINGs it received from each client and to also specify the required timeout value, in seconds, where if a PING has not been received within this time period then the connection to this client is deemed unhealthy and this connection (channel)

also specify the required timeout value, in seconds, where if a PING has not been received within this time period then the connection to this client is deemed unhealthy and this connection (channel) is closed by the Agent Server. HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI (REG_)DWORD IPEnableHeartbeat The default value of 0 disables monitoring and any other positive value (typically 1) will enable the monitoring and specify the required timeout value, in seconds, which is the specified value multiplied by a factor of 30. For instance setting this registry setting to 1 results in a timeout of 30 seconds, setting it to 2 results in a timeout of 60 seconds etc. -->

Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit Top Issues related to using Terminal Clients (Remote Desktop) to Run Adroit Problems running the Agent Server You cannot start the Agent Server as an application by using the Windows Remote Desktop (a terminal client). This is because Windows does not support USB ports when you use the Remote Desktop application, so any USB HASP is effectively invisible to the Agent Server. Note: This is not a problem when starting the Agent Server as a service from within a Remote Desktop. The resources (e.g. printer etc) of the computer used to remote desktop into the Agent Server computer are used by the Agent Server NOT the resources on the Agent Server's computer. This means that when you terminate the remote desktop session, these resources become unavailable which causes problems. Problems running Adroit Client Applications Adroit has terminal client (remote desktop) connection licencing rules whereby every Adroit client application takes a (remote node) connection licence regardless. An Adroit client is ANY application that makes a connection to an Agent Server, for instance: Classic User Interface Agent Configurator Adroit utilities, suc

metadata.title: Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit

text: emote node) connection licence regardless. An Adroit client is ANY application that makes a connection to an Agent Server, for instance: Classic User Interface Agent Configurator Adroit utilities, such as the Agent Browser Any Adroit OLE Automation (MISSRVR) or ActiveX client application. If the Classic User Interface is started from within a remote deskop session, and the Configurator is opened – then TWO connection licenses are required; otherwise either the Configurator and/or UI will be unable to connect to the Agent Server. Since BOTH the UI and the Configurator require their OWN connection licences when started using remote desktop. This change ALSO prevents the use of remote desktop for perform maintenance especially on stand-alone (no remote connection licences) installations. Since UIs cannot be restarted via Remote Desktop and/or the Configurator is unable to connect to the Agent Server. For this reason, Adroit has attempted to redress this limitation by NOT enforcing connection licences for the console user’s session. Typically when a user logs onto a computer, this user, known as the “console user”, always gets: Session 0 (on Window Server 2003 or Windows XP operating s

Typically when a user logs onto a computer, this user, known as the “console user”, always gets: Session 0 (on Window Server 2003 or Windows XP operating systems or older) or Session 1 (on Windows Server 2008 or Windows Vista operating systems or newer). When a remote desktop user logs on with the same user credentials as the console user, this remote desktop user inherits the same session number. When Adroit clients are launched via a remote desktop using the session of the console user (either session 0 or 1 depending on the operating system), then these Agent Server connections are treated as legacy local connections which do NOT require connection licences. Large Scalable Agent Server Networks Top Large Scalable Agent Server Networks This network configuration typically contains a large number of Agent Servers that are required to share information as if they were part of the same project so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Server. However, maintaining a grid of fully connected Agent Servers can potentially be resource intensive, for the following reasons: Many Agent Servers within a network all broadcasting their presence - many IT administrators do not like this. Many Agent Servers within a network all on the same project causing large agent tables to be transmitted in a "one to many" relationship. Large agent tables are generally created when agents are added or deleted. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. In this case, we recommend that you use the method, in which you can divide these Agent Servers into their own projects (or have each Agent Server in its own project if necessary), then use the list method for connecting these

that you use the method, in which you can divide these Agent Servers into their own projects (or have each Agent Server in its own project if necessary), then use the list method for connecting these Agent Servers and/or projects together. For further details of this and the other methods of connecting Agent Servers together, see Agent Server Connection Methods . If these Agent Servers are in different domains then you need to use explicit Agent Server connections. Click for details: For instance, consider this situation in which each section in a plant has its own Agent Server and its own local Classic UI and where all of these plant section Agent Servers are connected to a central gateway computer (known as a proxy server ), which also has its own local (or remote) Classic UIs. In this case The central gateway computer requires explicit Agent Server connections to be created for each of the plant section Agent Servers. Each plant section Agent Server, will only require explicit Agent Server connections to those servers from which data is required i.e. if its local Classic UI refer to tags, which are located on other plant section Agent Servers. For details, see Using the Same Command-line Options Infrequently . Frequent use: In this case it is recommended to create another shortcut for this application, especially if it is necessary to launch the required program with more than one command-line parameters configuration. For details, see Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently . Permanent use: In this case it is recommended to modify the installation shortcut for this application itself. If there is an already an existing WanClient or WanServer running on a computer, then if either program is run again, a warning will appear reminding the user than only one instance of each application is allowed. Tip: Both the WanClient and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Press the Windows key and start typing in the required application name and select it from the list, in this case: Adroit Wanlink Client , this launches the WanClient application. Limited Time License HASP Top Limited Time License HASP IMPORTANT: When a HASP is not detected when the Agent Server is started and the Agent Server is not being otherwise licensed, then the Agent Server will automatically run in limited time license mode. Use the limited time license HASP if the Agent Server is not currently licensed. This runs the Agent Server with a 120 minute operating license with 20000 scan points and 2 remote connections. When this period of time ends, the scanning of devices will stop and any remote server connections will be lost and not reconnected. Typically this can be launched from the Adroit Start menu by clicking on the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and clicking the Adroit Agent Server (timed license) item. Although it is also possible to launch the Agent Server with the following command line parameter: –demo e.g. C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \as.exe –demo There are message boxes and event log entries explaining these important events. Also the HASP agent provides the following status bits that indicate events relating to the use of this mode of licensing the Agent Server: TimedLicence : ON when the Agent Server is running in tim

s. Also the HASP agent provides the following status bits that indicate events relating to the use of this mode of licensing the Agent Server: TimedLicence : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode, which automatically occurs when the Agent Server is started and the HASP cannot be found. TimedLicenceExpired : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode and the timed license period has expired, so the Agent Server needs to be restarted to re-enable scanning. Note : To run the Agent Server Service in timed license mode, use the /-demo startup option, which is specified AFTER installing the Agent Server service, as follows: EITHER open CMD.exe and type in the following command: "net start agentserver /-demo" OR open the Services applet (in Administrative Tools), right click the AgentServer service, select Properties and specify –demo in the Start parameters edit field, then click the Start button and the Ok button. IMPORTANT: If using the Services applet, this ONLY starts this service in demo mode for a single session only. The demo mode is not applied to all instances of the service thereafter. -->

Logged Data Values CSV File Format Top Logged Data Values CSV File Format Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . After you have exported data logged values to a CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file, this file provides the following columns: date , time , value , comment The purpose of the comment field is to label each data log entry indicating how and when the value was derived. For every session, defined as the period between startup and shutdown of the Agent Server, Adroit always marks the first and last entries in the log as the post startup and last known values. For details, see Configuring EventLogging Agents . In Adroit , an EventOutput agent can be used to log alarm events to a SQL database. This requires the following main steps: Creating the SQL database and its associated ODBC data source , which is used by the EventOutput agent to refer to this SQL database. Create your SQL Database and save it. Tip: It is recommended to limit the size of the table and field names as ONLY 80 characters is available to represent the comma delimited list of these names in the EventOutput agent. Open the Start menu and select Run… Type “odbcad32.exe” into the Run dialog and click OK . Click on the System DSN tab in the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. Click the Add... button. Double-click the SQL Server entry in the Create New Data Source dialog. Tip: This should be the last entry in the list. Specify the name of this ODBC data source in the Name field of the Create a New Data Source to SQL Server dialog. In this example the following name is used: AdrEvtSQL Note:

Specify the required SQL Server computer in the Server field and click Next to advance to the next configuration page. Logging Values Top Logging Values "How to effectively log your data" on page 1 : guides you to use the fairly complex logging sub-system effectively. How to Log a Tag (agent.slot) : describes the procedure for logging process values in Adroit . The Datalog agent should ONLY be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. Therefore the logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Note: The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval that supercedes SQL logging via the Datalog agent. For de

agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval that supercedes SQL logging via the Datalog agent. For details, see The DBLog Agent . Although if the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration, then the SQL... button of the Datasource field will be visible in the Edit Datalog agent dialog. Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, first decide on the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Adroit provides the following methods of storing data: Note: The Disable logging on standby setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which typically do not require this setting as each Ag

ng on standby setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which typically do not require this setting as each Agent Server logs to their own datalog files. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method has been specifically designed for the needs of the SCADA industry to provide improved logging performance, typically achieving sub-second logging rates. Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files to automatically retrieve this data, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . This method stores original Adroit timestamps (a Windows FILETIME structure which represents the number of 100 nanosecond intervals since Jan 1 1601), which provide millisecond resolution for each recorded value. Note: When accessing these timestamps by using the

ME structure which represents the number of 100 nanosecond intervals since Jan 1 1601), which provide millisecond resolution for each recorded value. Note: When accessing these timestamps by using the OLE automation interface, this millisecond resolution is lost because the data type used to store this value is unable to store milliseconds. Each log file has a maximum of 53 million records, which can provide at least 30 days of logging at a log rate of 50 milliseconds! This rate is determined by configuring the required Time and/or Value Deadbands. Note: If the logging period is increased ensure that this change is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once, to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. Main.csv Top Main.csv This file stores the specific configuration of all the servers within the WanClient. The columns, in the order that they appear in the file: ID Number: This stores a unique number that identifies the server. Note: This number must never be greater than the number in the first column of the System.CSV file. Server Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the server, if the server is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the server is disabled this is 0. Server Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the server, if the server is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the server is not deleted this is 1. If the server is deleted then it will be added to the list of servers to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. Server Title: This stores the name that has been given to the server, which must not more than 90 characters in length. Server Database: This stores the name of the CSV file, that is also stored in the database folder . This file stores all the tag groups and tag links that belong to the server. IP Address: This stores the IP address of the WanClient computer or its computer name (

lso stored in the database folder . This file stores all the tag groups and tag links that belong to the server. IP Address: This stores the IP address of the WanClient computer or its computer name (provided that the network has a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve IP addresses from computer names). Port: This stores the IP port that is used by Wanlink for communications and this can only be set to 51114. Retries: This stores the number of times that communications are to be reattempted when the communications to this WanServer fail. Ping Period: This stores the period in seconds to wait after the communications to this WanServer fail before the WanClient will retry to establish communications. Connect Timeout: This is not being used. Transaction Timeout: This stores the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. The default value of 5 is required for fast networks and a value from 15 – 20 can be used for slower networks. Beep Enabled: This stores the Beep status of the server, which is configured from the Enable Beep menu item from the Diagnostics menu. If the server is beep enabled this is 1 and the server will beep every communication cycle,

he Beep status of the server, which is configured from the Enable Beep menu item from the Diagnostics menu. If the server is beep enabled this is 1 and the server will beep every communication cycle, otherwise if the server is beep disabled this is 0, and the server will be silent. Disk Log Enabled: This stores the Disk Log status of the server, which is either configured from the Enable Disk Log menu item from the Diagnostics menu or directly within the wanserver.ini file. To enable debug disk logging set this to 1 and a file called "wanserverlog.txt", is generated in the Adroit folder, that contains a shadowed list of the transactions that are recorded in the WanServer window, for troubleshooting purposes. Management Information Tools Top Management Information Tools A number of tools are provided with Adroit to facilitate the organization and communication of information from operations to management. Data can either be taken live from the Agent Server or collected from historical Data Logs. The data is then manipulated and reported by third party applications to provide relevant management information quickly. The tools have been designed to retrieve data from Agent Servers belonging to more than one project, providing management with the ability to get an overall view of their operations. They use several data retrieval methods listed below: DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent that provides a link between Adroit and various external databases, by using OLE DB technology. It is ideally used in applications where data inside the Agent Server is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job) for reporting reasons. It is not suited for fast logging of data. Managing Message Queues Top Managing Message Queues The Command agent uses a message queue because the sending and receiving of SMS messages are not instantaneous. This message queue provides temporarily storage, especially when a large number of SMS messages need to be sent at any one time or a large number of Command agents are using the same GSM SMS modem. If necessary, the total number of messages that can be stored in this queue can be limited, although once the queue is filled, any further messages that arrive will not be sent. It is therefore recommended to keep the default setting, of 0, which does not limit this queue length, since a large message queue does not pose a performance issue. It is also possible to purge all the messages from this queue, for instance, for testing purpose or when the message queue has been filled with unwanted or unnecessary messages. Note: These settings are ONLY specific to this Command agent only and do not apply globally to all Command agents. To specify the maximum number of queued messages: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General ta

o specify the maximum number of queued messages: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Agent Settings group, specify the required maximum number of messages in the Queue size edit box. Note: Any integer number from 0 to 1000 can be specified, the default being 0 i.e. an unlimited queue length. Tip: It is recommended to keep the default of 0 i.e. unlimited queue length. To remove all the messages that are currently in the queue: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Agent Settings group, click the Empty Queue button. WARNING! All messages currently in the queue will be removed and will need to be re-sent. Tip: This can also be performed through the direct manipulation of its Boolean emptyQueue slot. -->

text: Manual Master Mode Assignment Top Manual Master Mode Assignment In manual mode, the systemInfo.serverMode slot is completely controlled by the user. Rules and implications There cannot be more than one master server in a cluster. Hence making a server master will immediately switch the other server to standby mode. The serverMode and serverState slots between Agent Servers and within an Agent Server are not replicated. All other server and client clustering operations will operate as normal given the slot values, irrespective of whether a manual or automatic master mode assignment method is used. For instance, the automatic switching UI will track the first healthy master server in its list even if the UI detects more than one healthy master server, when connected to more than one cluster. Suggested method of operation As suggested in the above scenarios, start all or part of the cluster servers. Set the desired master server as master through the various means available to set the serverMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Adding a new clu

verMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. -->

Manually Edit Groups Top Manually Edit Groups Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . If it is necessary to bulk configure a large number of groups at one time, they can be manually edited. To manually edit groups: Groups are stored in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server . This .CSV file is located within the database folder and contains all the specific configuration of the tag groups and their tag links that have been configured within the specific server. The first 6 lines of the file are comment lines. The first two lines show both the name and IP address of the server, to which these tag groups and tag links are associated. The next four lines then provide configuration specific information. The columns, required when configuring a tag group, in the order that they appear in the file: [GROUP]: This is used to identify that a tag group, as opposed to a tag link, is being specified. Note: This must not be any spaces be

nfiguring a tag group, in the order that they appear in the file: [GROUP]: This is used to identify that a tag group, as opposed to a tag link, is being specified. Note: This must not be any spaces before the [GROUP]’ indication. Group Title: This stores the name that has been given to this tag group, which must not more than 90 characters in length. Group Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the group, if the group is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the group is disabled this is 0. Group Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the group, if the group is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the group is not deleted this is 1. If the group is deleted then it will be added to the list of groups to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. Poll Period: This stores the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and the rate will depend on the total number of configured groups. Buffer size: This is not being used. Group Type: This stores the communication type required by the t

0 implies "as fast as possible" and the rate will depend on the total number of configured groups. Buffer size: This is not being used. Group Type: This stores the communication type required by the tag links within the group. A Normal group, indicated by a 0, only permits the values of the tags links within this group to be fetched from the WanServer so that the values on the WanClient are updated accordingly. A Control group, indicated by a 2, also permits the tags links within this group to also send changes from the WanClient to the WanServer. -->

onfigured tag group [GROUP]-entry, to which they are then associated. Master Recipe Top Master Recipe The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. The following are the components of the Master Recipe: Step: Both master and control recipes consist of sequences of steps. Each step is numbered, and if any new steps are inserted or deleted, the steps are renumbered consecutively. It is important to note that any GOTO STEP references must be manually edited if there has been any change to the order or number of steps. Ingredient: An agent and slot corresponding to the process variable to be set or downloaded to a front end device (e.g. PLC). The keyword <NONE> when used as an ingredient indicates that no process variable will change for the step. This allows a phase action to take place without having to set any process variable. The ingredient must either be a valid agent and slot having one of the slot types STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER, REAL, or a null entry <NONE> when a control Phase Action entry is needed. Verification: This is the means of verifying the values written to a front-end device (e.g. PLC).

es STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER, REAL, or a null entry <NONE> when a control Phase Action entry is needed. Verification: This is the means of verifying the values written to a front-end device (e.g. PLC). It is represented by an agent.slot that is read after a definite period of the ingredient value being downloaded. This value must be a valid slot. If the value of this slot does not match the value written to the ingredient slot, verification fails. The verification check occurs at the end of a phase. Phase Boundary: Any step that has a Phase Action marks the end of a phase. Phase: A phase consists of all steps executed between phase boundaries. Phase Actions and Tag/Value : A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. Specific Status Bits . -->

Mathematical Operators for Expressions Top Mathematical Operators for Expressions Primary elements are primitive members of expressions like constants, variables or functions. Terms are separable parts of expressions, and can be signed terms or the product, quotient or modulus of two signed terms. Expressions are well-formed strings of terms, composed of symbols representing constants, variables, operators and relationships. Comments may follow an expression using C and C++ syntax (i.e. // comment or /* comment */). The order of precedence TYPICALLY begins at the top of the table, and is the same within each box. IMPORTANT : There are cases when certain operators do NOT follow their prescribed order of precedence - so please use parentheses to enforce the required precedence in your expressions. Example of altered precedence: Consider the expression: v1 | v2 & v3 These operator precedence rules say that & has precedence over | So this IS the same as: (v1 | (v2 & v3)) However, you add a ! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3))

Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3)) However, this is not the case, it is actually treated as the following by expression agents: (((!v1) | v2) & v3) Primary elements: NUMBER // Adroit real constant VARIABLE //variable input (V01, V02) mathFunc (primary) //mathematical function – primary //unary minus(result is negative of its operand) + primary //unary plus(result is same as its operand) ! primary //logical NOT ~ primary //bitwise NOT (1’s complement) Terms: primary / primary //division primary * primary //multiplication primary % primary //remainder (modulus) Expression relationships: term + term //addition term – term //subtraction term >> term //right shift (divide by 2) term << term //left shift (multiply by 2) term < term //less than term > term //greater than term <= term //less than or equal to term >= term //greater than or equal to term == term //equal term != term //not equal term & term //bitwise AND term ^ term //bitwise exclusive OR term | term //bitwise inclusive OR term && term //logical AND term || term

Maximum Demand Quick Start Top Maximum Demand Quick Start This explains the recommended method of configuring your Adroit system to monitor your maximum demand. Before you can monitor your maximum demand, you need the following: To know when your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. To know the maximum kVA demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, above which you are required to pay penalties. To know the block period duration used by your electricity provider to monitor your maximum demand. A front-end device (PLC) that monitors the pulse sent from your electricity provider to signal the start of each block period. [Otherwise, you can disable block pulses and allow to agent to determine block periods automatically based on current time instead.] A front-end device (PLC) that monitors the total kVA that your process uses. To monitor your maximum demand: Only enable this agent when maximum demand is being monitored Create a Scheduler agent, for instance called MDPERIODS, to specify the periods of high power use during which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. Contact your electricity provider for this information. For details, see Configuri

ERIODS, to specify the periods of high power use during which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. Contact your electricity provider for this information. For details, see Configuring the Scheduler agent . Edit an agent of type: MaxDemand . If necessary, add an agent of the required type, as follows: In the SmartUI Designer: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. Right click the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically, and select Create Tag . Specify the required Tag Name or agent name. The following rules apply when naming agents: Agent names have a maximum of 27 characters. Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes

r Agent Types or for Agent Groups. Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes the purpose or describes the value of this tag (agent) for ease of reference. Click the Finish button. If necessary, locate the required agent, as follows: In the SmartUI Designer: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit MaxDemand Agent dialog: Check the Enable OR use tag checkbox (the enable slot) Click the browse button to the left of the Enable OR use tag checkbox and select the Scheduler

t Configure . In the Edit MaxDemand Agent dialog: Check the Enable OR use tag checkbox (the enable slot) Click the browse button to the left of the Enable OR use tag checkbox and select the Scheduler agent you created and its value slot (MDPERIODS.value) to only enable this agent when your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. For details, see Selecting a tag from the Agent Explorer . Configure the other maximum demand-specific settings Specify the duration of the block period that your electrical provider uses, in minutes, in the Block period (mins) edit box (the blockPeriod slot). For instance, 30 minutes. Check the Enable block pulses checkbox (the blockPulseEnable slot) Specify the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent, in the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) edit box. Tip: If may be useful to specify a value slightly LESS THAN the actual maximum demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, so that there is time for counteractive measures to be taken when this is exceeded. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) to enable the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Le

is is exceeded. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) to enable the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Leave the default Reset configuration, unless you do NOT want to reset the current month’s calculations at midnight on the last day of the month. Click OK and close the configuration dialog of the MaxDemand agent. Configure the maximum demand-specific alarms for this agent Alarm the ‘PulseError’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know if the timing of these external block pulses are compromised i.e. as soon as a pulse does not occur at the period specified by the Block period (mins) value. Alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know when the maximum demand limit is exceeded. Scan the relevant values of this agent to the appropriate front-end device Scan the BOOLEAN blockPulse slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that monitors the pulse sent from your electricity provider to signal the start of each block period. Scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage. If you ALSO want to calculate the

ctricity provider to signal the start of each block period. Scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage. If you ALSO want to calculate the instantaneous power factor and reactive power component then also scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage. Display important values You could display some or all of the following MaxDemand agent slots: mdLimit : the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent. mdActual : the highest recorded maximum demand for any block period of the current month. demand : the actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. mdPredict : estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the demand slot against the remaining time for this block period. mdOverUnder : displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. timeToMD : indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, th

: indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. This specifies a positive or negative amount of kVA that needs to be removed or added to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Example: For instance, you can create a mimic that allows a manager to know that at the current consumption ( demand slot) that: the configured maximum demand (the mdLimit slot) will be reached in 12 minutes ( timeToMD slot) which is 3 minutes before the end of the period (the blockTimeLeft slot - timeToMD slot) and 30kW of load needs to shed (the kVASpare slot is a negative number) to not exceed the maximum demand OR if the process is running safely that 45kW o

period (the blockTimeLeft slot - timeToMD slot) and 30kW of load needs to shed (the kVASpare slot is a negative number) to not exceed the maximum demand OR if the process is running safely that 45kW of load can be added (the kVASpare slot is a positive number) to meet the maximum demand) for this block. If necessary, use this agent to control your maximum demand If you want to control the maximum demand by using this agent, then use the MaxDemand status bit of this agent to turn off non-essential equipment via a script. Since this status bit is ONLY set when the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled and the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Memsize Top Memsize WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". If you have a very large alarming configuration spread over many Alarm agents that is causing the virtual memory size of the Agent Server process to reach its upper 2 GB limit, then you can add the following value to reduce the memory usage of your Alarm agents: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Alarm (REG_)DWORD Memsize = 1000000, by default, the minimum value is 4000. This specifies the amount of available memory in Bytes. -->

Merging Data Logs Top Merging Data Logs Adroit provides a means of merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents. The .CSV file may have been originally created by the EXTRACT utility, or by choosing the EXPORT... button in the Datalog Retrieval dialog, or by using a text editor to modify existing files taking care to adhere to the format. The syntax of the command is as follows: merge mc.as,csvfile > jnlfile The abbreviations and examples are as follows: Note: No spaces are required between arguments. Symbol Description Example mc computer name AEPCY4 as Agent Server WestPlant csvfile csv file name or existing agent.slot (of type string) PERIOD01.CSV or CSVFILE.value jnlfile journal file name name of journal file used to record any error messages that may be displayed -->

Message Sending and Processing Slots Top Message Sending and Processing Slots The Command agent provides the following slots that are responsible for processing commands and sending SMS messages, which can be externally manipulated if required: The lastMsgReceived slot: the most recent data received by this slot, even if identical to its previous contents, will cause it to BOTH process the data and then to send this processed data to the rawValue slot. Note1: If this slot receives a command, which has been enabled for this Command agent, then this command will be performed before it is sent to the rawValue slot. For details on enabling commands, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: If pseudonyms and macros have been configured and enabled for this agent, then they can be also used when specifying this data. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . The value slot: the most recent data received by this slot will also be sent to the rawValue slot. Since this is a standard 80-character String slot and NOT a VARSTRING slot, like these other lastMsgReceived and rawValue slots, other agents are able to be @ scanned to it, so that their STRING slots can be sent by the Command a

haracter String slot and NOT a VARSTRING slot, like these other lastMsgReceived and rawValue slots, other agents are able to be @ scanned to it, so that their STRING slots can be sent by the Command agent instead. The lastMsgReceivedTime slot displays the time of the last message received. The lastMsgReceivedTimeStr slot displays the time of the last message received, as a (var)string. For instance, the value slot of the Command agent can be @scanned to the rawValue slot of a Notify agent, so that the Notify agent's alarm message can be sent to the recipient of the Command agent instead. For details, concerning @scanning, see Scanning from a Slot of Another Agent . The rawValue slot: this sends the most recent data received by this slot to its associated GSM_SMS device and as it leaves the Command agent, this data will also be placed in its lastMsgSent slot. For details on associating a GSM_SMS device with a Command agent, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Note1: This rawValue slot is also exposed as the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is

s also exposed as the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Tip: The lastMsgSentTime slot displays the time of the last message sent. These slots can either be modified programmatically, via scripting or manually, such as by exposing the required slot and sending messages to it directly by exposing it on a mimic and associating a Data Entry, Operator Action Behaviour to it. For details, see Adding an Operator Action Behaviour or its Data Entry action. -->

Methods of remotely sending messages to the Notify agent Top Methods of remotely sending messages to the Notify agent There are numerous methods available, by which, user-defined messages can be sent to the Notify agent remotely. The following are a number of suggestions: An operator action ‘Set Value" Behaviour can be configured in a mimic to modify the ‘value’ slot of a Notify agent, this will then send the text typed in at that point. @scan a string into the value slot of a Notify agent. Configure the value slot of a Frame or StringList agent, which has been pre-configured with messages, to output into the value slot of a Notify agent. Use a Script agent to place a specially built or customised message into the value slot of a Notify agent. -->

Overview This driver supports the Mitsubishi 3E Frames protocol, with communication to the Q/QnA/L/R and FX5 Series CPU’s. The 2nd Generation driver allows for the following features: a) Improved performance due to optimizations on mixed I/O to the same protocol area being transacted only once removing redundant transactions. b) Support for multiple channels, where due scan tasks are balanced over available channels, reads and writes are interlaced to prevent starvation. c) Demand scanning support, where read only I/O that is not on a mimic / graphic form and not logged or alarmed and not output enabled will be removed from the scanning system , the applicable tasks will dynamically be reduced in size and can merge into fewer scan tasks. For improved network performance and reliability, it is recommended that you install 2 network adapters into your PC. Use the first adapter for Adroit to Adroit and all other Windows connectivity. The first adapter may have all the default installation bindings. Use t

that you install 2 network adapters into your PC. Use the first adapter for Adroit to Adroit and all other Windows connectivity. The first adapter may have all the default installation bindings. Use the second adapter for Adroit to PLC connectivity and bind only to the TCP/IP protocol for PLC communications. 1.1. Upgrading from classical MITQJE71 Driver The scanning addresses are identical. If using the MITQJE71 driver, remove all of the old Device Agents, and create them again with the same names using the Q driver. Take care to note settings like the IP, port address and watchdog addresses. On the A-Series driver the Decimal or Hex notation used is important and does change over in this Q/QnA driver. Names of I/O types stay the same so far possible, this means that scanned I/O types existing in the A-Series driver that have different names (prefixes) in the Q Driver are promoted automatically to their new names. After saving, the WGP file cannot be loaded on the old driver again without the possibility of losing some scan-points. _______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-D_MIT_ETH.docx P

Overview The system allows telemetry functionality for efficient communication to highly distributed systems. We have attempted to support the most important aspects required for a distributed system, namely: • The need for time-stamped data so that events, rather than just register values, can be stored. • An event is a register value (16-bit or 32-bit) and a timestamp with second resolution. Time of arrival (100ms separation) is attempted to be maintained if change events are registered faster than a second. • The need to store in a buffer the events for later retrieval to a SCADA. This is especially needed at a time when communication becomes available and/or

e events are registered faster than a second. • The need to store in a buffer the events for later retrieval to a SCADA. This is especially needed at a time when communication becomes available and/or when the need arises to drill down and retrieve most specific data that would not normally require operator attention. For example, a temperature reading trend would only be of interest if say a high temp alarm were to be received. • Efficient means of communication especially if data costs are an issue. 1.1. Supported Hardware Adroit supports communication with the following PLCs: Mitsubishi FX3U with FX3U-ENET using the following “FXM2M613a” Library function block. In the case of the network described by this mimic, it would be necessary to configure seven SNMPMgr agents on the computer running the Agent Server. Monitoring Message Receipt Top Monitoring Message Receipt One of the methods in which SMS messages sent by a Command agent can be monitored, for auditing purposes, is to require a delivery report to be sent by the recipient as soon as the SMS messages arrives, which logged to the event log. This audit method verifies that the message has been delivered to the recipient’s device. Furthermore, a minimum time period can also be specified in which this delivery report must be received. If this is exceeded then this SMS message can be sent via another Command agent to someone else. In this way it is possible to escalate this message either to a colleague or up the management chain, as is necessary. Note1: It is also possible to ensure that the recipient receives and is aware of a message and, if necessary that this recipient responds within an appropriate time otherwise the message is escalated. For details, see Monitoring Message Response . Note2: For details on specifying the recipient for a Command agent, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . Monitoring Scanning in Adroit Top Monitoring Scanning in Adroit The Scanning Monitor utility is designed to assist experienced users in fine-tuning the Adroit scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance, by providing an intuitive report-like view of advanced diagnostic information. This utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server to and from its configured front-end devices, such as PLCs, RTUs etc. and is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. How to use the Scanning Monitor Tip: The Scanning Monitor utility can generate a report of your current scanning configuration of an Agent Server to indicate how well it has been configured. For details, see Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report . However, OPC Server devices not in "sync-poll mode", and telemetry applications will find this utility less useful. For additional ways to optimise the scanning configuration see Scanning Optimization Tips . To launch the Scanning Monitor Utility . For details on how to specify the Agent Server in order to monitor its scanning configuration, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . This util

n Tips . To launch the Scanning Monitor Utility . For details on how to specify the Agent Server in order to monitor its scanning configuration, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . This utility consists of following three hierarchically arranged list boxes, each of which expose increasingly detailed communication information for the selected Agent Server: Note: The contents displayed in a list depend upon the selection(s) made in the list immediately above it. The device list, which displays all the devices that have been configured in the .WGP file (Agent Server database file) of the selected Agent Server. For details, see Devices within Selected Agent Server Database . Note: This will ONLY list the devices, which have been used to scan tags within the current project that is running on the Agent Server, even though other devices may have been added and configured on the computer. The scan job list, which displays the scan jobs for the selected device or devices. For details, see Scan Jobs within Selected Devices . Note1: Any configured @scans will NOT appear in this utility because scan agents are NOT involved in @scanning functionality - these are simply internal slot-

, see Scan Jobs within Selected Devices . Note1: Any configured @scans will NOT appear in this utility because scan agents are NOT involved in @scanning functionality - these are simply internal slot-to-slot subscriptions that change in real time mode. Note2: Scan jobs are automatically created by Adroit to group the scanned tags together in such a way as to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. The tag list, which displays the tags (scan points) grouped within the selected scan job or jobs. For details, see Tags within Selected Scan Jobs . In addition to these lists, the Servers combo box and the Connect… button can be used to specify the Agent Server whose scanning configuration is to be monitored, while the Help button displays this help topic. Note: The name of the currently selected Agent Server and any connection-related errors are displayed within the status bar of this utility. For details, see Current Agent Server Connection Details . -->

Monitoring Tags (Values) Top Monitoring Tags (Values) IMPORTANT: This utility is NOT included in the Adroit installation and must be separately installed from the Additional Adroit Components installation. The Tag Monitor utility is designed to display the current values of one or more tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). values from a particular Agent Server without having to specifically draw a mimic to do so.
