ghtweight, report by exception, ISO-standard pub-sub messaging protocol specifically designed for the Internet of Things. The MQTT network consists of publishers, subscribers and a broker. The publishers will publish or send information to the broker, the broker will then relay those messages to the subscribers. The broker is the “middleman” in the network and could be situated in the cloud. A publisher/subscriber are the clients on the network and are linked together by topics. Each Adroit agent can be a publisher and/or subscriber, and acts as a client on the network. If Adroit is a publisher, then it will write values out to other subscribers (when the tag is scanned using Output enabled). When Adroit is a subscriber, then it waits for data on a specific topic from any publisher to that topic. There are three parts of an MQTT transmission: Message: This is the data that is passed through the broker to all clients subscribed to a specific topic on the MQTT network. Topic: Some brokers support topic strings with a maximum of 128 levels and a maximum length of 250 bytes, so an MQTT client connection that exceeds those limits will be closed. QoS: Quality of Service, ensures delivery

s support topic strings with a maximum of 128 levels and a maximum length of 250 bytes, so an MQTT client connection that exceeds those limits will be closed. QoS: Quality of Service, ensures delivery to connected clients: a. At most once - The published message is sent once, and if it does not arrive it is lost. b. At least once - Guarantees that the published message arrives, but there may be duplicates. c. Exactly once - Guarantees that the publish message arrives and that there are no duplicates. 1.1. Multiple Log Sets Top Multiple Log Sets Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. Instead of specifying only a single rate and period per datalog agent configuration, you can create multiple log sets within a single datalog agent. In other words, if you need to log a given tag (agent.slot) at different sample/window settings, you can simply create multiple log sets with these different permutations for the SAME tag, without creating separate datalog agents for each permutation. Click for the advantages of using log sets: The advantage of using multiple log sets is this case is that it prevents cumbersome configuration reduces the number of required datalog agents and subsequently decreases the memory requirements and thereby improves performance. Multiple log set usage example: For example, a user may wish to log a tag at 1 second for 2 days, and at 10 seconds for 7 days, and at 60 seconds for 30 d

equirements and thereby improves performance. Multiple log set usage example: For example, a user may wish to log a tag at 1 second for 2 days, and at 10 seconds for 7 days, and at 60 seconds for 30 days and at 1 hour for 365 days. Each of these interval/period specifications constitutes a log set. In the above diagram, two log sets are used for each of the two logged tags. The first log set may be at 1 second for 2 days and the other, 10 seconds for 7 days. It is possible to configure these sets in various combinations. For instance, all the slower logging rates for all tags may be logged to one file while the faster logging rate for all tags logged to another separate file. Alternately, the file for each tag (or set of tags) may be distinct from another tag (or another set of tags) even though each tag may have multiple sets of logging. Thirdly, it is also possible to place all logging into one central file. The data for each datalog agent can be extracted and saved to a CSV file for analysis. MultiState Data Model Top MultiState Data Model The MultiState agent models a logic table or truth table , which can be used to define the operating and control sequence for equipment and is typically used to control drive groups. Its logic or truth table has the following properties: Up to a maximum of 16 discrete states, such as, for example, Group Auto Ready and OFF, Group in hold, etc. Each state can have a description text up to 64 characters long. A maximum of 16 inputs , various unique combinations of which are used to define the discrete states. These inputs can originate from any Boolean, Integer, or Real data, but will be converted to Boolean TRUE/FALSE indications on being stored in a MultiState agent. MultiState inputs can be sourced either from agents, such as existing Digital agents or directly from PLC registers. This latter option is facilitated by the ability to scan directly into MultiState agent’s inputs (. rawValue slot) without going through an interposing conditioning agent like a digital, and can yield some very substantial benefits in terms of reducing the total number of agents that need to be engineered for a project. Any number of Boolean outputs , can be

ning agent like a digital, and can yield some very substantial benefits in terms of reducing the total number of agents that need to be engineered for a project. Any number of Boolean outputs , can be set TRUE or FALSE on attainment of a particular state. A current state variable, containing the agent’s currently active state. Because there are a maximum of 16 states, 16 agent- Specific Status Bits are used to hold the current state. This approach, namely having a separate bit dedicated to each state, leads to a smooth integration with the Classic user interface multicolor Behaviour, by allowing a different text, line and/or background color for each discrete state. In addition, these bits can be individually alarmed using existing Adroit alarming mechanisms, which means a wide variety of alarm strategies can be developed. If a Multistate input bit is driven by a Digital agent in addition to being scanned to the field, then this input bit will reflect the state of this Digital agent, ignoring any changes made to this Multistate agent’s "rawValue" slot from the field. Note: It is recommended that the Marshal agent be used for this type of application instead. A current state string,

gnoring any changes made to this Multistate agent’s "rawValue" slot from the field. Note: It is recommended that the Marshal agent be used for this type of application instead. A current state string, containing the state description text for the MultiState agent’s currently active state. Each state therefore has the following properties: A state number (1 -16), corresponding to the state’s bit position in the MultiState agent’s status word. A state description text string up to 64 characters long. A 16-bit input-true mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be TRUE for the state to be active (see Common Status Bits ). A 16-bit input-false mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be FALSE for the state to be active. An output-true list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set TRUE on attainment of the state. An output-false list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set FALSE on attainment of the state. -->

MultiState Operation Top MultiState Operation On reaching a new state, a MultiState agent automatically carries out the following actions: The new state is recorded as the current state. The new state’s description is recorded as the current state description. Any outputs in the new state’s output-true list are set TRUE. Any outputs in the new state’s output-false list are set FALSE. -->

Naming Agents Top Naming Agents Each agent (instance of an agent type) is referred to by its own unique name, so Adroit will not permit an agent name to be used twice within an Agent Server. Usually this name is defined by the user when the agent is created. However, some agents are created by Adroit itself, in which case a name is usually automatically generated. Note: It is important to adhere to the agent naming convention, when naming agents. For details, see Agent Naming Convention . Agent Naming in a Distributed System Furthermore, because of the distributed nature of Adroit it is possible for multiple Agent Servers to be part of the same project, so that Adroit cannot prevent agent names from being duplicated. Therefore, the following two approaches can be taken to resolve the potential duplication of names in a distributed installation when referencing agents: Either the user can ensure all agent names on all Agent Servers are unique, perhaps by keeping a master list. Adroit will assist the user with a prompt to warn him that he is adding a duplicate agent name, with an option to continue or not, whenever he attempts to add an agent name that exists on another Agent Server.

ll assist the user with a prompt to warn him that he is adding a duplicate agent name, with an option to continue or not, whenever he attempts to add an agent name that exists on another Agent Server. Alternatively, the user may permit duplicate agent names to exist on different Agent Servers but prefix the required Agent Server name to explicitly specify these agent names. For details, see Agent Referencing Convention . For further details about agents, see About Agents . For further details on projects, see About Adroit Projects . -->

Obtaining KPI Values Top Obtaining KPI Values One of the possible uses of the database of incidents logged by your AlarmManagement agent/s is to determine how well your process or your operators are meeting the KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. that you have set for them regarding alarming . The AlarmManagement agent provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1. If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. The AlarmManagement agent automatically calculates the following KPIs: The kpi24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour

he number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous 24 hour period. The kpiPrevMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous month. The kpiPrevShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous shift. The kpiShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current shift. The kpiTotal slot records the number of alarms per hour for the all incidents found in the database. Furthermore, the AlarmManagement agent provides you with the ability to obtain the values of 6 user-defined KPIs. IMPORTANT: Each KPI must be a SELECT query that is performed on the database of logged incidents that returns a SINGLE numeric value called kpi . Example of a KPI query: The following query returns a SINGLE value called kpi: SELECT COUNT(Idx) / (MAX(CONVERT(float, dt) * 24) - MIN(CONVERT(float, dt) * 24)) AS kpi FROM HistoricalIncidents These user-defined KPI Queries support the following optional parameters: The following parameters MUST ALL BE encased within a pair of SINGLE quotation characters: %

) AS kpi FROM HistoricalIncidents These user-defined KPI Queries support the following optional parameters: The following parameters MUST ALL BE encased within a pair of SINGLE quotation characters: %now - the current date and time Usage example (in SQL): The following example retrieves the average active time for the last 8 hours. SELECT AVG(ActiveTime) AS Kpi FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > DATEADD(Hour,-8,'%now') AND dt < GetDate() %s1b - shift 1 start time %s1e - shift 1 end time %s2b - shift 2 start time %s2e - shift 2 end time %s3b - shift 3 start time %s3e - shift 3 end time Usage example (in SQL): SELECT AVG(ActiveTime) AS Kpi FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE (dt >= '%s1b') AND (dt < '%s1e') The AlarmManagement agent therefore provides 6 sets of the following 3 slots, where [x] is a number from 1 to 6: kpi[x]Query: A VARSTRING slot, that contains the KPI query, which is saved in the WGP file. kpi[x]Description: A VARSTRING slot, that contains the description of this KPI, which is saved in the WGP file. kpi[x]: A REAL slot, which retrieves the value of the KPI query. IMPORTANT: If the KPI query returns multiple columns and/or rows and not a SINGLE value, this

this KPI, which is saved in the WGP file. kpi[x]: A REAL slot, which retrieves the value of the KPI query. IMPORTANT: If the KPI query returns multiple columns and/or rows and not a SINGLE value, this kpi[x] slot will be set to 0.0. Note: These KPI queries are automatically executed by the AlarmManagement agent when a new record is added to the Historical Incidents table. You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements AND add your own custom KPIs that your user-defined KPI Queries can use. Customizing KPI target values : If necessary you can set KPI target values that your own custom KPI queries and certain default queries use, so that these queries better comply with your specific requirements. -->

OLE Server Interface Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The OLE Server Interface allows third party client applications to interact with standalone or distributed Agent Servers. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™, Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. Note: The Adroit Server ActiveX Control (adroitx.ocx) is provided as an alternative to this OLE Server interface. See Adroit Server ActiveX Control . Monitoring Real-time Data describes the steps you need to take to provide continuously updating real-time data for your application. The examples are shown in VBA for ease of understanding. The Adroit Automation Interface describes the OLE Automation or Programmability Interface for Adroit OLE Server Data Objects, which is a set of OLE Automation methods and properties exposed by the Data Objects. These methods are callable as functions and these properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. Note1: Adroit also provides a scripting interface, namely the Adroit system object . This is not the

le as functions and these properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. Note1: Adroit also provides a scripting interface, namely the Adroit system object . This is not the same as the OLE Server interface; in fact, certain tasks can only be accomplished via the OLE interface, like adding and removing tags. It is possible, however, to use the OLE Server interface within this scripting interface. Note2: Any pokes performed, using this Adroit OLE Automation Interface will require a scan point license for each unique tag that is "poked". This also applies to the use of functions that use pokes internally, such as AlarmTag , LogTag , and ScanTag . Note3: Fetching values of logged data (by using the FetchChanges and/or FetchValues functions) does not use scan points. -->

OLE Server Interface API for Adroit Agent Servers Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) API for Agent Servers This OLE Server Interface Specification forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Agent Servers. It effectively defines a contract, by means of which third party client applications can interact in a rich variety of ways with standalone or distributed Adroit configurations. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™ , Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. It is an implementation of the Windows Open Services Architecture, Extensions for Real-time Market Data (WOSA/XRT) standard, as created by the Open Market Data Council For Windows (Microsoft Part Number 098-54432). Unlike other WOSA standards such as MAPI, ODBC, and TAPI, WOSA/XRT does not require new APIs to be defined, nor does it require any production code from Microsoft (other than the OLE DLLs). This is possible because WOSA/XRT leverages the existing architecture and binary standard provided by OLE. Specifically, WOSA/XRT uses the exist

OPC Definitions Top OPC Definitions OPC is short for OLE (Object linking embedding) for Process Control, it is a software technology designed, like OLE to allow different applications to exchange data, more specifically allowing an I/O server developed by a 3rd party to communicate to any SCADA. This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own drivers or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. An OPC Item: is a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. OPC Data Types: OPC is based on OLE, which uses Variants for all data transferred in transactions. A Variant is basically a block of data preceded by so

ally using a period "." to separate each level. OPC Data Types: OPC is based on OLE, which uses Variants for all data transferred in transactions. A Variant is basically a block of data preceded by some information indicating the actual type of data in the block. A program will automatically convert Variants received to a data type that it is familiar with. Conversions are standardised, and automatically occur in high-level programming languages. An OPC Server is a data source or I/O Server, conforming to the OPC Data Access Specification e.g. the Adroit OPC Server . An OPC Client is an application, which uses the data provided by an OPC server, such as HMI software. -->

Optimizing Datalog Catchup Top Optimizing Datalog Catch-up Tests have revealed that rate of Datalog catchup only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. or the rates at which historical data points are merged into the local datalog agents during a synchronization process are affected by the following factors: Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. The fragmentation of the disk on which the datalog files (*.lgd and *.lgi) are kept. This disk should be as unfragmented as possible. text: Out of limit data logging Top Out of limit data logging Out of limit monitoring enables Datalog agents to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the normal time deadband value and using the faster log rate specified by the out of limit time deadband instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: sinc

talog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1 second intervals. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 10 sec and Out of limit monitoring Time = 1 sec and Upper limit = 225 and Lower limit = 215). Note: In this case he will be able to catch short voltage spikes whose duration whose duration are less 10 seconds, the normal logging interval. Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe Top Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. A phase action can be any of the following keywords: GOTO STEP <step number>; DELAY <milliseconds> or VARIABLE. A GOTO STEP action will cause an active recipe to jump to the step given in the Tag/Value field. The Tag/Value for a GOTO STEP action may either be an explicit step number or an agent.slot that holds the step number. A DELAY action will delay the execution of an active recipe by the number of milliseconds given in the Tag/Value field. Note: The Tag/Value for a DELAY action may either be an explicit delay time or an agent.slot that holds the delay time. A VARIABLE action will alter recipe execution based on the value of the agent.slot given in the Tag/Value field, as follows: Slot value Action 0 Wait until the slot value changes to a value between 1 and 6 and then perform the action associated with this number 1 Go to next step 2 Go to previous step 3 Go to first step 4 Go to last step 5 Perform verification failure rollback 6 Stop recipe execution Note: the Tag/Value for a

text: Philosophy for End User Applications Top Philosophy for End User Applications The general philosophy is for the user to create an instance of a coarse grained object, and then instruct the object to create many finer grained objects inside itself. A coarse grained object corresponds to a connection to a known Agent Server, either running on the same computer as the application, or some other computer on a local- or wide-area network. In WOSA/XRT terminology, a coarse grained object is a Data Object , and a fine-grained object is a Request Object . A Request object formally describes the pieces of information we require from the Data object. It consists of data that identifies the information we want, plus data which names the specific fields related to that information. For real time Adroit data this corresponds to an agent and the associated slots we are interested in, whereas for historical data, it corresponds to a time and the associated agent.slots we are interested in. The individual fields of each request are stored as a Properties Collection . A single Request collection can hold many Request objects at once. Once we have created requests on the Data Object, the easiest way

dual fields of each request are stored as a Properties Collection . A single Request collection can hold many Request objects at once. Once we have created requests on the Data Object, the easiest way to get at the required data is to ask the object to paste links to the data into our containing application, which needs to be able to process the paste. When the links are pasted onto the application, the application activates the links, and the Data object supplies the application with ongoing updates. In addition to the basic WOSA/XRT features described above, our OLE server provides a number of Adroit -specific extensions. These include the provision of an output mode that permits the poking of values from a container application to an Agent Server, the ability to fetch values in a one-off fashion from an Agent Server, the ability to connect to a remote Agent Server, the ability to create and remove agents in an Agent Server, etc. -->

PID Alarm Limits Top PID Alarm Limits The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point). As such it is possible to define L, LL, H and HH for the PV and an H and HH alarm for the %Error, for each instance of the PID agent. The L (low)and H (high) inner alarms are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken, by the control algorithm, as soon as possible. The LL (low low) and HH (high high) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action, by the control algorithm, is now required. Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reache

t is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit . Any Alarm agent subscribing to the PID agent will detect these status bits. -->

PokeWithTime ActiveX Method Top PokeWithTime ActiveX Method Agent Functionality . Method PokeWithTime(Agent, Slot : string; Value : variant; Timestamp : datetime) : boolean; This method changes the historical value of a tag. Note: This can ONLY be used to change PAST values of tags NOT current or future values. However, a value that is the SAME as the previous time sample will NOT be accepted. For instance, if a value is being logged hourly and the value at 10:00 is 1 then you will be unable to set the 11:00 value to 1. But if the value at 10:00 is 0 then you will can set the 11:00 value to 1. Parameters: Agent: the name of the agent or tag (agent.slot) whose value is to be changed. Slot: the name of the slot whose value is to be changed. This parameter is ignored if the Agent parameter contains a tag. Value: the required value. Timestamp: the (historical) time when this value was changed. Returns: If the call is successful the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE. Use LastError / LastErrorNum to determine the cause of failure. -->

Printing Alarms Top Printing Alarms Before a new printer may be used, you must ensure that the host computer has the correct BIOS setting. The Parallel Port Mode must indicate Normal or Standard (SPP), NOT Enhanced (EPP). For further details see To set up a new printer . Note1: Typically, in order to perform line-by-line printing, no Windows driver should be installed at all, since the Windows spooler will internally cache printing until it has an entire page, so as to reduce CPU load while printing. However, specific printer drivers may be able to disable this spooling or page-caching method, and can thus work too. Note2: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry. Note3: The Time column of the EventOutput agent now supports MILLISECONDS. In the Configurator dialog box, select EventOutput from the Agent Type drop down list. Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Top Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Adroit provides extensive proprietary historical data logging facilities . As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values historically logged, subject to the proviso that they are of slot type Real , Integer , Boolean or 79 character String (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). When logged, the values are time stamped and are made available, via a DataLog agent , to any client . Examples of data log clients would be historical trends, the extract utility, OLE-aware 3 rd party applications such as external spreadsheets for reports etc. Historical values can be stored in one or more data files, each file containing the values of one or more DataLog agents. Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the

the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .C

etary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files to automatically retrieve this data, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . TWO files are created for each proprietary log, the .LDG file, which stores the raw data and its associated .LGI file, which is the lookup index file. The total amount of disk space required for data logging depends on the following factors: the number of data files used the number of agents being data logged the total number of values logged per agent the sampling time and length of time each value is logged for. Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches th

d eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches the end of the buffer. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend. PLEASE NOTE: Adroit ’s proprietary logging uses an in-built logging factor, which reduces the specified logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Note: If the logging period is inc

logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Note: If the logging period is increased ensure that this change is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once, to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . A data log file is composed of many buffers, one for each DataLog agent. Being event based, the speed at which each buffer is written depends on how often the value in the agent slot being logged changes, and its deadband. If necessary, the data log file can be periodically archived by file copy. Protocol Drivers Top Protocol Drivers Adroit has created a large number of protocol drivers that use Windows device drivers to communicate to a wide range of front-end devices e.g. Programmable Logic Controllers PLCs, RTUs etc. If necessary, specialised drivers can be developed. Before a protocol can be used to provide communication to a front-end device, it needs to be installed. Each protocol driver, provides the following services: The configuration of hardware I/O addresses to be scanned from the front-end device. The communication of these configured addresses to and from the hardware I/O. Note: Protocol Drivers using proprietary hardware adapters will require the relevant Windows driver for the adapter. Although an installed protocol driver provides the means of communication, the communication to each FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. is performed by a device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. that you need to be add to the installed protocol driver. These devices are essentially logical con

sing this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. that you need to be add to the installed protocol driver. These devices are essentially logical connections to the front-end devices they communicate to and a total of 65534 devices may be added and used for any one installed protocol driver. Note1: The protocol driver configuration for each device is saved in the system registry; therefore it is necessary to reconfigure the devices if they are to be run on another computer. Note2: You may use as many different protocol drivers and devices as you wish, until the sum of their scanned points exceeds your licensed number of scan points. For details, see Scan Points . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. Proxy Servers Top Proxy Servers A proxy server is an Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Since it only contains Proxy agents, it will not support scanning, alarming or datalogging. Proxy servers generally use an empty WGP file. IMPORTANT: If your proxy Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the other Agent Servers. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Proxy servers are used in environments where one or more clients need information from multiple Agent Servers. A client can only connect to one Agent Server so this server must hav

emote Agent Server. Proxy servers are used in environments where one or more clients need information from multiple Agent Servers. A client can only connect to one Agent Server so this server must have the capability to create proxies where needed. Proxy servers are also useful in environments where a user wishes to remove the burden of servicing multiple clients from an Agent Server. Those clients are connected to a proxy server and the remote server(s) then only services the proxy server leaving it more processor and network time for it's SCADA functions. Note: If your proxy server needs to proxy information from a remote Agent Server that is on a DIFFERENT domain or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote agent server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . All Agent Server types (Standalone, Cluster aware and cluster servers) have the capability to create proxy agents for agents that exist on remote agents servers on the same project. Cluster and Cluster Aware servers acting as proxy servers, have the unique feature of creating proxy agents even if there are more than one agent of the same name in a n

s servers on the same project. Cluster and Cluster Aware servers acting as proxy servers, have the unique feature of creating proxy agents even if there are more than one agent of the same name in a network of clustered Agent Servers. Therefore cluster proxy servers must be used if there are cluster servers on the same project. A Standalone server acting as a proxy server will not create proxies agents if two or more agents of the same name are found on a network. Therefore standalone proxy servers should only be used where there are no cluster servers on the same project. -->

Putting Values into Agents Top Putting Values into Agents Adroit provides a utility that performs a putslot operation. The putslot utility enables a specific value to be written to the target agent’s slot. Alternatively, a value obtained from another agent’s slot, by dereferencing it with an asterisk (*) prefix, can be used in the putslot expression both for the target agent’s name and the put value. It can be scheduled to start a process, allowing the scheduler to trigger commands (e.g. print, scan etc.) and to drive mimics and dynamic pictures. The syntax of a Putslot command is as follows: putslot [-ccomputer.server],[*]agent.slot,[*]value[,time] Note1: DO NOT insert spaces between arguments [ ] means optional. Note2: By default a connection to a local Agent Server is assumed, but if a computer.server is specified, prefix it with –c. ag) slot target slot RawValue value value to put or ~ to toggle value if Boolean slot 90.0 or "a string" or *ANOTHER.VALUE (asterisk dereferences tag) or ~ (~ absent = set value of slot) time time of change 04/10/1998 14:00:00 (dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss) Note: The command line input is now case-sensitive when changing the values of STRING slots. Examples: putslot boo01.value,1 putslot boo01.value,~ putslot int01.value,123,04/10/1998 14:00:00 putslot -cMSP-1.West-Plant,int01.value,123,04/10/1998 14:00:00 putslot str01.value,"hello" putslot ana01.value,*ana02.value Configuring the same slot of multiple agents If necessary, create the required Agentgroup or simply use the pre-defined Agentgroups for the defined Agent types. text: Read Only Scanning Strategy Top Read Only Scanning Strategy This scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). configuration is the normal mode of operation for read only scanning. Where users should not modify the values of tags within the Agent Server manually otherwise the value of these tags in the Agent Server will be out of sync with their process values i.e. their values in the front end device (PLC). For details of all the scanning strategies offered, see Scanning Strategies or for further details on the effect of combining the available global and tag-specific scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . Required global scanning settings: MonitorStatus can be set, in which case any values which have been manually modified in the Agent Server, will be overwritten with the process value, on the next read. Where both the Agent Server and the front-end device (PLC) can manipulate the values of the tags at will, where the value of the tag is set by whoever changes the value last. Real-time Catch-up Top Real-time catch-up Certain agent types on a cluster server require synchronisation of internal data structures with their Master partner. This process is called real-time catch-up. When a cluster partner starts up and it's Master server is available, this synchronisation takes place while the standby server is loading up. Note: Real-time catch-up is not associated with shadowing and datalog catch-up. The following agent types support real-time catch-up: Analog , Digital , Counter , Expression , IOT , MaxDemand , PID , Scheduler and Statistical . How the Real-time catch-up process works The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers. The process occurs during the start up of a standby agent server, if a master agent server is already running. If this is the case, then every agent that is loaded from the WGP file and also supports real-time catch-up will request the current state of the agent from the master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each ag

master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each agent subscribes to other agents when required by expression agents. It is during this phase that the agent will synchronise itself, using real-time catch-up with the same agent in the master agent server. On completion of phase 2 above the agent server then enters the ready state. As an illustration of real-time catch-up: Let’s assume we have an analog agent called TANKLEVEL. The saved value of TANKLEVEL in the WGP file is very likely to be an old value (for example, 25%) that was relevant at the time the WGP file was last saved. The current real-time value in the process is very likely to be different (let’s say 55%) from the saved value of 25%. The TANKLEVEL agent in the newly started standby agent server will then synchronise its slot values with those of the master during the agent initialization phase. Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value . Take note of following In scenarios where Adroit installations only save their WGP files after a configuration change, i

ialization phase. Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value . Take note of following In scenarios where Adroit installations only save their WGP files after a configuration change, it is important to realise that: Adroit does not automatically save WGP files on shutdown of the agent server unless it is specifically configured to do so. It is then very likely that the WGP files contain old saved values which makes the requirement for real-time catch-up a very important process. Installations where a cluster is setup to extend the configuration on the standby server should execute the following procedure: Let’s call the maser server AS1 and the standby server AS2. Save the WGP file on the standby server AS2. Switch the standby AS2 to master, resulting in AS1 becoming the standby. Stop the standby agent server which is now AS1. Copy the WGP file from standby AS2 to master AS1. Restart the standby server AS1. Optionally, once AS1 is back up and running correctly, switch AS1 back to master if this is the preferred master agent server. When the synchronisation has completed, the agent server values contained in the newly copied WGP file may still be a few minutes old an

Recipe Agent Overview Top Recipe Agent Description A recipe is a statement of the ingredients and procedures necessary for the making or compounding of some preparation or formulation. It defines how the control system is to process its raw materials to make the desired product and byproducts. In Adroit , this is achieved by the Recipe agent which provides the means for automatically downloading information to process variables. These variables allow a plant to produce the final product. Mundane tasks can be automated saving time and removing the element of human error. In common with modern industry practice (SP88), the recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for

efined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. For example, the Master Recipe could describe a Fruit Juice mixing plant. Several Control recipes would provide the data to manufacture various flavors and mixtures of fruit juice such as Orange, Mango, Pineapple, Mango and Orange, Pineapple and Orange etc. The Adroit recipe system allows: Each Control recipe to be assigned a batch identification. Accumulation of batch histories through event logging. Downloading of process variables that are of type Boolean, Integer, Real or String. The sequence of execution to be delayed by a specified amount of time, to be paused until a desired condition in the plant is met, or to be redirected to another step. Master recipes and Control recipes to be imported or exported to files using the comma separated variable (CSV) format, for ease of viewing and editing by 3rd party products (e.g. Excel). For details of the formats of this CSV files, see Agent List CSV File Format . Perform a selective import of each alarm agent, only importing the AGNTLST file. Note: If you import a list of alarm types list into an existing Alarm agent, it is recommended that this Alarm agent is deleted and then re-created to quickly clear its list of already configured alarms, as these may conflict with the new alarm types. text: Replication Top Replication While catch-up deals with the requirement for a new server being added to the cluster to be a mirror image at the current point in time, replication is concerned with how changes that occur as a result of external influences on the cluster are dealt with. For instance, external changes affecting the cluster members can occur from a Adroit client application or from Agent Server scan inputs. Client changes are typically a result of changing a set point from within a UI. All these sources of change are replicated to all Agent Servers in the cluster in order to maintain the mirror image state of the clustered servers. Two instances of configuring replication within a cluster are: Client Runtime Transaction Shadowing : All transactions initiated by a client on a server are shadowed to the other server in the cluster to provide total data replication. Parallel scanning : Each cluster server is configured to replicate the scanning tasks to provide scan task replication, that is, each server performs scanning as if it were a normal server. This is an alternative to automatically shadowing the scanned data. -->

Note: Project names must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. Click the Project Options button, and ensure that Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server is checked. The checkbox Explicit Additional Server Connections should remain unchecked initially. Ensure that each computer within the same project has a unique name for its local Agent Server. (This message is also displayed when more than one Agent Server is started on a computer.) If duplicate agent names exist in the Agent Servers, the one on the local Agent Server will be used. Routing to Audio Devices Top Routing to Audio Devices Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented. The priority of a Beeper agent determines the interval between beeping i.e. a high priority will beep faster than a lower priority Beeper agent. If the start slot of a MultiMedia agent is used, this will activate the configured multi-media file. These files may be any Windows compatible multi-media standard such as .WAV, .AVI, .MID and .RMI. Alternatively, integer slots of any other agent type may be used to keep a count of active and unacknowledged alarms. To route the alarm to an audio device . To remove a current audio device . -->

Running the Main Subroutine Top Running the Main Subroutine The Script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine. This main subroutine can be executed in one of four different ways, namely: On demand, by manually poking ( putslotting ) a one into the runNow slot. While the main subroutine is running any new request for it to run will be ignored. To stop the main subroutine from running, poke a zero into the runNow slot. This method will cause the script to be recompiled, as it needs to be re-initialised after termination. By scheduling , which is based on a simple schedule; e.g. execute every hour starting from midnight on the 1 st of January. By triggering , which is based on a list of tags. Each trigger has an identification number that corresponds to its position in the list of triggers. The first tag in the list has an identification number equal to one, etc. Reordering this list will change the trigger identification numbers. To determine from within your script the value of a trigger or the tag that triggered the script, use the system object denoted by Adroit . By using a combination of scheduling and triggering . For instance, using scheduling on condition th

value of a trigger or the tag that triggered the script, use the system object denoted by Adroit . By using a combination of scheduling and triggering . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the script, e.g. run every five seconds but only if a tag in the trigger list has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple executions. -->

Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Top Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Each WanClient is able to determine how the scan bad status of all the tags that it communicates is set within its local Agent Server. This is a global setting, in that it applies to ALL the tag values that are communicated by this WanClient, irrespective of the number of WanServers that these values are communicated to and / or from. This is configured within the Tag bad philosophy group of the WanClient Configurator dialog, which is launched by selecting Open Configurator from the File menu. Note: Although these are actually ‘scan bad’ indication methodologies, whenever the ‘scan bad’ status bit is set for a tag, this will result in this tag being marked ‘bad’ i.e. its ‘bad’ status bit will also be set. Therefore the terms ‘scan bad’ and ‘tag bad’ can be used synonymously. The following four events can be used to determine how the scan bad status of these tags are set within the Agent Server that is on the WanClient computer: On comms start: This event occurs when the WanClient begins communicating the tag values to and / or from the WanClients specified within its tag link database. On comms fail: This event

ent computer: On comms start: This event occurs when the WanClient begins communicating the tag values to and / or from the WanClients specified within its tag link database. On comms fail: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is halted unexpectedly. On comms stop: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is stopped. On client shutdown: This event occurs when the WanClient application itself is exited i.e. the WanClient.exe is shut down. . For each of these four events, one of the following scan bad indication methodologies can be selected: Do nothing: This leaves the current status of the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags unchanged. Mark bad: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to ON. Mark healthy: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to OFF. text: Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Top Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Scan point licenses or 'scan points' are just one of the components of an Adroit license. These are consumed when information is being manipulated in some way. Their typical usage is when communicating (scanning) a value to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other consumers of scan point licenses, as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot) using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface ( MISSRVR ) or the Adroit ActiveX component will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot)

hat changes the value of an agent.slot) using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface ( MISSRVR ) or the Adroit ActiveX component will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked". Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips Top Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips A significant change or noise filter can be specified in the Deadband field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . Any change in value less than this deadband limit will not be used to update this tag’s value. For details on scanning tags, see How to scan a tag or Scanning tags for general scanning information. The purpose of applying a deadband is to reduce the amount of internal updating of this value within the Adroit database (such as its related alarming, client UI updates and datalogging) in order to conserve PC resources. Note: This does not affect the usage of the commmunication channel itself, since it is performed after the data has arrived. Please consider the following recommendations when configuring this deadband: Ensure that the deadband is specified in the same units as the slot of the agent being communicated. The deadband operates best when used to filter out noise or minor variations in value from an integer or analog value that y

is specified in the same units as the slot of the agent being communicated. The deadband operates best when used to filter out noise or minor variations in value from an integer or analog value that you do not need to see in Adroit . For instance, when using a 12 bit A/D input with 1 bit noise, then use a dead-band of 2. Also when measuring a level on a vessel or item that changes due to vibration, waves or instability, then specify a deadband only slightly greater than the amount of variance. Do not use a deadband when scanning slots containing state information, as you may lose significant bits of information when decoding to binary format. -->

text: Scanning Interval Configuration Tips Top Scanning Interval Configuration Tips A scanning interval can be specified in the Scan rate (ms) field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . This is used to specify the time, in milliseconds, which will elapse before this value is communicated to or from this device. For details on scanning tags, see How to scan a tag or Scanning tags for general scanning information. Note: This field should ONLY be specified when configuring POLLED devices, since event-based or TELEMETRY devices do not use setting when communicating. Please consider the following recommendations when configuring this scanning interval: It is good practice to make your scan-interval longer, for polled drivers, because this minimises the queuing of tasks to be performed by the driver. Scan-tasks are created by Adroit (not the driver) whenever the scan-interval expires. Once a scan task has been created it is given to the driver, where it joins the queue of existing tasks. Hence when scan-times are too short, the queue o

he driver) whenever the scan-interval expires. Once a scan task has been created it is given to the driver, where it joins the queue of existing tasks. Hence when scan-times are too short, the queue of existing scan-tasks to performed by the driver increases, which cause configuration-tasks, such as the adding or removal of scan-points or the starting/stopping of the devices, to arrive at the back of this same queue. If the scan-intervals are configured to be longer, then the queue of scan-tasks is reduced, so that the configuration-tasks can be dealt with sooner. Note: The length of the task queue also affects control actions or writes, to the device, which are usually not prioritised to the front of the queue. By slowing the scanning sufficiently, pauses can be created in which nothing is happening, which can be filled by a fast-scanning task. However there is a limit to the number of fast scanning tasks that can be accommodated i.e. if a large amount of fast scanning is required then more sluggish scanning is required too. Therefore, as scan tasks are added, the scanning intervals need to be constantly adjusted and increased to cater for the increased traffic. For details on gro

n more sluggish scanning is required too. Therefore, as scan tasks are added, the scanning intervals need to be constantly adjusted and increased to cater for the increased traffic. For details on grouping scanned data together with similar scanning intervals, see Scanning Optimization . Drivers interlock all communications on a communication resource (e.g. COM1) so that it is not possible for the driver to do 2 polls at the same time on a port, but is possible to do 2 polls at the same time on 2 different ports. Note: In this example RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) could also mean any other front-end device, such as a PLC. This means that the request to a RTU #1 has to complete before the request for data from RTU #2 starts. But if RTU #1 responds very slowly, the driver may timeout before this response has been given and so will query RTU #2 for a response but receive the response from RTU #1 instead. Hence the driver loses synchronization as a result of this confusing traffic. Although this problem can be prevented by making the scan-times longer, it would be better to make the timeouts longer to accommodate any late responses, since then no performance is lost when the RTU responds

his problem can be prevented by making the scan-times longer, it would be better to make the timeouts longer to accommodate any late responses, since then no performance is lost when the RTU responds within the required time. -->

Scanning Optimization Top Scanning Optimization The optimization of scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). typically involves grouping data correctly within front-end devices, so as to prevent fragmentation of the data that usually creates a bottleneck for communication performance. Usually I/Os acquired from the plant are not needed by the SCADA, but are intermingled with the SCADA I/O. Therefore, it is recommended to allocate separate memory space in the controller for SCADA tags and the internal I/O. Although determining how much memory to reserve is never easy, it is recommended to plan correctly in this area. Certain front-end devices, such as Siemens controllers, make this process easier by using addressable data blocks or files that can grow in size. By scanning tags, whose slots belong to the same data type, which has contiguous addresses in the front-end device, will ensure that this device will require the least number of transactions to communicate its tags. For details, see Contiguous Scanning . Note: The reason for this is that a separate Scan agent is generally created by this device's Device agent, for

t number of transactions to communicate its tags. For details, see Contiguous Scanning . Note: The reason for this is that a separate Scan agent is generally created by this device's Device agent, for a block of manageable contiguous addresses, the size of which is dependent upon the protocol being used to transfer this data to and from Adroit . When grouping data, ensure that the various data types are separated, such as Analogs and Digitals, examples of such groups are: Digital Inputs, Analog Inputs, Digital Outputs, Analog SPs etc. It is also recommended to further differentiate data with respect to their required scan rate. Typically Analog values for I/O, such as temperatures can be grouped together as these values generally change very slowly. Although, Digital data must always be scanned quite fast, it is possible to differentiate between feedback and event digitals that must be polled very fast and digitals that indicate situations that need not be acted on right away, such as a high level indicator that takes 15 minutes to overflow. Note: When scanning tags, remember that it is the data type of the SLOT that is being scanned that determines which group it should be scanned

a high level indicator that takes 15 minutes to overflow. Note: When scanning tags, remember that it is the data type of the SLOT that is being scanned that determines which group it should be scanned to and not its AGENT name. For details of optimizing the scanning for an Analog agent, see Analog Scanning Optimization Example . The following examples illustrates how various types of data types could be grouped: Note: Scan times of less than 1000 ms should only be used if the driver can poll fast enough. Using faster scan times may adversely affect communications error recovery and the sending of controls to the front-end device. A further tip to optimise scanning in Adroit: Save the WGP and then restart the Agent Server to potentially reduce the number of required Scan agents. Reason: It is only when saving the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file that the Adroit scanning sub-system sorts the scan list into the optimal order, but this .WGP file is only read again when the Agent Server is restarted. Example: After successively importing and deleting scanned items a system required 69 Scan agents. By simply saving the WGP file and restarting the Agent Server, without doing anything els

restarted. Example: After successively importing and deleting scanned items a system required 69 Scan agents. By simply saving the WGP file and restarting the Agent Server, without doing anything else, Adroit only required 30 Scan agents! -->

Scanning Overview Top Scanning Overview Scanning in Adroit refers to the sending of or the communication of values between Adroit tags (agent.slot) and the front-end devices in the field, such as a PLC a Programmable Logic Controller or programmable controller is a digital computer used for the automation of industrial processes. , RTU an Remote Terminal Unit is a device installed at a remote location that collects data and transmits this data back to a central station, or master. etc. Since each front-end device can use a different protocol a set of rules or conventions governing the exchange of information between a computer and a front-end device. or language for communication, Adroit has developed a driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. for each of these different protocols, which allow Adroit to communicate to these front-end devices by adding and configuring a for each. For further details, see Understanding Protocols and Protocol Drivers . Once installed, a protocol driver provides the protocol or language to communicate to front-end devices that use this protocol. However, it is necessary to

erstanding Protocols and Protocol Drivers . Once installed, a protocol driver provides the protocol or language to communicate to front-end devices that use this protocol. However, it is necessary to add a device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. for each front-end device through which the communication actually occurs. Each device is essentially a logical connection to the front-end device that it is communicating to. For further details, see About Protocol Drivers . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . In other words, while the installed protocol driver is the language that needs to be communicated, the devices are the actual translators that use this language to communicate between the front-end devices and Adroit . Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ Top Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ This topics provides answers to commonly experienced problems/issues associated with scanning: Q: When the Agent Server is started, 3 beeps are heard and the Agent Server disappears. Why does this happen? A: The 3 beeps are produced when a driver is NOT loaded by the Agent Server, which can occur because of the following reasons: the driver has not been configured and therefore cannot load properly the port is already in use or does not exist some other resource has run out. Look for the devices in the Adroit Setup drivers tab, and check the amount of free disk space. Make sure you do not have a folder in your installation directory with the same name as the device. Q: When writing to a register, the value does not change, why? A: This can be due to writing to an input; a driver automatically disallows writing values to inputs, since they are most likely not supported in that protocol. In the Modbus driver, for instance you cannot write to digital input 1XXXXX registers, nor to the analog input 3XXXX registers. A driver in most cases does not generate an error/alarm, but simply fails the transaction. This is noticeable b

cannot write to digital input 1XXXXX registers, nor to the analog input 3XXXX registers. A driver in most cases does not generate an error/alarm, but simply fails the transaction. This is noticeable by the tag greying out in the mimic, and then becoming healthy on the next scan. Note: Whenever you perform a write using any polled (not telemetry) driver, Adroit automatically queues that item/task for reading afterwards Q: The driver software does not run, and I do not get any messages explaining what is wrong. Where do I look now? A: The first place to look in event of an error is the Windows event log. Look at the last few entries in the Application and System event logs for more details on a problem. Often a problem is the result of an error reported a little further back in the log. Q: An error message appears about a buffer overrun in the protocol driver monitor just before the comms dies. What does this mean? A: Buffer overruns and underruns are caused when the buffer on the serial card overflows. This is because character reception and transmission relies on the CPU emptying the buffer as the computer receives characters in the line. If the computer is busy with some other tas

card overflows. This is because character reception and transmission relies on the CPU emptying the buffer as the computer receives characters in the line. If the computer is busy with some other task (which happens all the time in windows), the buffer is not serviced often enough. The solution is to use a card with a buffered UART (FIFO buffer). This provides a 16-byte buffer as opposed to the 1-byte buffer common in older cards. Q: I have a serial card with a Buffered UART of FIFO but I still get overruns, why? A: The serial card driver for Windows may not have detected the FIFO. Use the Ports applet in Control Panel to enable the use of the FIFO. Delete the affected ports, and re-boot. The operating system will auto-detect the FIFO on the port and add it in. If it is not added in, you may edit the port settings and go to the advanced dialog which allows changing IRQ’s etc. Check the box at the bottom of the dialog, in order to enable the FIFO. Q: I get error messages such as parity error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the b

error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the baud-rate on both devices. Q: The (any serial) driver is not running. When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears. Although no driver or hardware configuration was changed, there is no longer any communication. A: Make sure the mouse is plugged into the correct port. If the mouse is on the port the driver would use, the mouse will work but the Adroit driver will not. To correct this problem, either swap the mouse back and re-boot, or re-configure the driver to use the free port, and re-start Adroit . Q: Why does scanning not work for certain Analog agents? A: Please ensure that you scan the raw value slot and NOT the Engineering value as this can cause scanning to fail because the scanned value is out of range. Q: When I access a device agent, all I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning conf

ll I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning configuration is not loaded. This occurs for intermittent Windows/PC resource/device unavailability/conflict at the time of Agent Server startup. The Agent Server needs to be restarted to gain access to these resources or to sort out a resource conflict; for example, your RAS connection (or other software) is still active which is using the same COM port as your device configuration. Q: When I install a protocol driver, it is copied without errors but does not appear in the "Available protocol drivers" list. A: A number of our Adroit drivers rely on 3rd party components being installed, if they are not, then you get the above symptoms. This is because the driver available list in setup uses the driver, which also uses the missing 3rd party component. Examples are: Allen Bradley RSLINX, Eagle, Lonworks, Modbus plus (+), Siemens H1, Siemens L2 and Siemens S7 Functions among others. In such cases, the required hardware and accompanying software must be installed (preferably before the driver)

Scanning Values Top Scanning Values How to Scan a Tag : how to communicate a process value in Adroit to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . Scanning values simply means communicating values, typically to and from front-end devices, such as a PLC a Programmable Logic Controller or programmable controller is a digital computer used for the automation of industrial processes. or RTU an Remote Terminal Unit is a device installed at a remote location that collects data and transmits this data back to a central station, or master. . Since in Adroit terminology a value (slot) is the same as a tag , ‘to communicate a value’ is the same as saying ‘to scan a tag’ or ‘adding a scanned point’, which typically requires a scan point license. For further details, see Scan Points . In addition to communicating or scanning a single tag, it is also possible to: Scan multiple tags simultaneously i.e. to scan multiple agents of the same type, using the most recently specified scanning configuration. For details, see Template Scanning . Scan in bulk i.e. to import many scanned points to a Device agent. For details, see Bulk Scanning o

type, using the most recently specified scanning configuration. For details, see Template Scanning . Scan in bulk i.e. to import many scanned points to a Device agent. To the simulation driver : This is an emulation of a Siemens S5 PLC, mainly provided for testing and demonstration. To another tag : This simply copies the value of one agent’s slot into the value of another agent’s slot and is known as @scanning. e protocol used. Rate: Scan period, in milliseconds. Deadband: Scanning deadband, in scanned units. OutputEnable: 1, if scanned point must be an output, otherwise 0. Scheduling and Triggering Scripts Top Scheduling and Triggering Scripts This enables the remote execution of the main subroutine by the Script agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling can be configured: Triggering only: This is used when the execution of the script is only required after a particular condition, defined within the script, has been met by one or more of the tags within Adroit . This requires checking Run when one of the following tags change and then configuring one or more triggers . Scheduling only: This is used when the execution of the script is required at a set time period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the configuring the scheduling . Ensure that both the, only if one of the following tags change and Run when one of the following tags change options, are unchecked. Triggering and Scheduling: In this case the script is executed when its scheduled to and when a value of the one of the triggers change. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, Run when one of the following tags change option, should be

nd when a value of the one of the triggers change. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, Run when one of the following tags change option, should be checked. Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the script is only executed when it is scheduled to, if a value of the one of the triggers also change. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple executions. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, only if one of the following tags change option, should be checked. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! -->
