Script Procedures Top Script Procedures When a Has script engine Custom agent is derived the following empty procedures are created, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent: OnCompiled() Code that is executed every time the Agent Server detects a change in the script code. This procedure can be used to initialise any global variables. OnLoadComplete() Code that is executed once an agent has been loaded from the WGP file. This procedure can contain code to initialise slot values. OnChange(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a slot value is changed. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the slot and value thereof being changed, e.g. setting status bit slots. OnUpdate(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a Tagname type slot receives a subscription update. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the subscription received. OnBackground() Code that is executed every second in the background. This procedure should contain time-dependant and/or simulation code. -->

Searching the help for topics Searching the Help for Topics The Search tab, on the left hand side of the help viewer, is a good way to find a topic title if you know it, as this looks through the online help to find topics that match the specified word(s) and/or phrase(s). Tip: Use this if you know the EXACT PHRASE you are looking for. Otherwise this may return a long list of irrelevant topics, in which case use the Index tab instead. To search the help for topics: Click the Search tab. Type the search query that you want to locate in one or more help topics into the edit box or click the list button and select a previously entered search query from this list box. Basic searches: Guidelines or tips for creating the search query. Searches are not case-sensitive, so you can type your search in either uppercase or lowercase characters. You may search for any combination of letters (a-z) and/or numbers (0-9). Punctuation marks such as the period ("."), colon (":"), semicolon (";"), comma (","), and hyphen ("-") are ignored during a search. Group the elements of your search using double quotes or parentheses into phrases, where necessary e.g. (TermA TermB) or “TermA TermB”. Note1: The d

","), and hyphen ("-") are ignored during a search. Group the elements of your search using double quotes or parentheses into phrases, where necessary e.g. (TermA TermB) or “TermA TermB”. Note1: The default operation between terms is AND, so unless you specifically group terms into phrases then all instances of each individual word will be searched for. Note2: You cannot search for quotation marks. Note3: If you are searching for a file name with an extension, you should group the entire string in double quotes, ("file name.ext"). Advanced searches: Additional items that can be added to your search query to help you narrow your searches for more precise results. Wildcard expressions: These can be used as placeholders for one or more characters, within your search query. Use a question mark (“?”) as a single-character placeholder e.g. 90?10, will return 90a10, 90610 etc. Use an asterisk (“*”) as a multiple character placeholder e.g. water*, will return "WATER", "waterfall", "waterproof" etc. Note: These wildcard operators cannot be the only character in a term. Boolean operators: These can be used to create specific relationships between the phrases or words in your search query. Te

etc. Note: These wildcard operators cannot be the only character in a term. Boolean operators: These can be used to create specific relationships between the phrases or words in your search query. TermA AND TermB: This will return topics that both contain TermA and TermB. TermA OR TermB: This will return topics that either contain TermA or TermB. TermA NOT TermB: This will return topics that contain TermA but not TermB. TermA NEAR TermB: This will return topics that contain TermA within eight words of TermB. Note1: If no Boolean operator is specified, AND is used i.e. TermA TermB = TermA AND TermB. Note2: The |, &, and ! characters do not work as Boolean operators (you must use OR, AND, and NOT). Nested expressions: These allow you to create complex search queries. Use parentheses to nest expressions within a query. The expressions in parentheses are evaluated before the rest of the query. If a query does not contain a nested expression, it is evaluated from left to right. Examples: TermA NOT TermB OR TermC will locate topics, which contain TermA without TermB or topics containing TermC. TermA NOT (TermB OR TermC) will locate topics, which contain TermA without either TermB or Ter

ermA NOT TermB OR TermC will locate topics, which contain TermA without TermB or topics containing TermC. TermA NOT (TermB OR TermC) will locate topics, which contain TermA without either TermB or TermC. Note: You cannot nest expressions more than five levels deep. Note: If you are performing an advanced search and using one or more Boolean operators, click the button to select the required operators from the list. If necessary, ensure that the required search settings have been set before the search is performed: To only search topic titles and not their contents, ensure the Search titles only checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. To find words similar to your search term, ensure the Match similar words checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. To narrow your search, ensure the Search previous results checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. To highlight all instances of search terms that are found in topic files, click the Options toolbar button and select Search Highlight On. Note: To turn off this highlighting of words, select this menu item again and then perform the search again. Click List Topics , select the topic you want, and then click

select Search Highlight On. Note: To turn off this highlighting of words, select this menu item again and then perform the search again. Click List Topics , select the topic you want, and then click Display . To sort the list of topics, alphanumerically that have been found by this search, click the required column heading: Title: The names of the located help topics. Location: The name of the help file in which these topics have been located. Rank: The lower the number, the greater the number of occurrences of the required words and/or phrases.

Secondary Port Disabled Top Secondary Port Disabled A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the driver fails, and the scanning resumes immediately. -->

Secondary Port Enabled Top Secondary Port Enabled Adroit drivers can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3-step process: Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. Timeout Phase : the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary port if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternat

munications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternate Secondary Port Enabled scenario where the same PC port / resource is used but with different PLC ports / resources. -->

(each of which is an OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. ) from a single device on the network. Sending SMS Messages Top Sending SMS Messages SMS messages will only be sent to the specified phone number of the recipient of this Command agent via the specified GSM_SMS device. For details, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number and Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Note: If necessary, sent SMS messages can also be sent via another Command agent to another recipient, if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . SMS messages can be sent by means of the following methods: Note1: If the Require recipient response option is enabled, all sent messages will be prefixed by an asterisk "*" to indicate to the recipient that he/she needs to return the message to the Command agent. For details, see Monitoring Message Response . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Manually: By typing the required message in the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent d

updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Manually: By typing the required message in the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Tip1: It is also possible to expose the required message processing and/or sending slot and send messages to it directly by using a mimic, for instance, by associating a Data Entry Operator Action Behaviour to it. For details on these slots, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . Tip2: In addition to simple text it is also possible to place commands into these slots so that they can be performed before the message is sent. For details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Programmatically: By using another agent to create the message dynamically and then passing it into the required message processing and/or sending slot of the required Command agent. Automatically: The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. This message can either be sent when triggered by ano

is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. This message can either be sent when triggered by another Adroit tag or when the change in its value exceeds the specified deadband. For details, see Automatic Sending of Values . Note: Pseudonyms and macros are generally used to simply the creation of SMS messages that are RECEIVED by the Command agent. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . Tip: The lastMsgSentTime slot displays the time of the last message sent. -->

Server ActiveX Property Top Server ActiveX Property Connection Functionality . Property Server : string This property specifies the Agent Server that the ActiveX object will connect to. Servers Top Servers The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. Therefore, the WanClient creates and maintains a tag link database that stores a list of WanServer(s), that this WanClient is required to connect to, and a list of the tags whose values are communicated to each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers. Servers contain the settings required by the WanClient to communication to the required remote WanServer applications. Servers can be configured, as follows: To add a new server . To edit an existing server . To delete an existing server . To recover a formerly deleted server . To manually edit servers – this may be necessary when adding a large number of servers at once. -->
Servers ActiveX Property Top Servers ActiveX Property Connection Functionality . Property Servers : array of string; This property contains a list of all Agent Servers found on the network. -->

ServerStatus ActiveX Property Top ServerStatus ActiveX Property Connection Functionality . Property ServerStatus : long; This property contains a bit mask of the status and mode of the connected Agent Server. See the ConnectionUpdate event description for an explanation of the mask. -->

ServiceCleanShutdown Top ServiceCleanShutdown WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". To cause the Agent Server service to attempt a clean shutdown to ensure that the OPC client drivers disconnect from their OPC Servers, add the following value and set it to 1: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup (REG_)DWORD ServiceCleanShutdown = 1, the default value is 0. The OPC client drivers need to disconnect from their OPC Servers so that these OPC Servers can clean up their resources and shutdown if necessary. -->

SET Command Usage Restriction Top SET Command Usage Restriction Once SET commands are enabled for a Command agent , additional restrictions can be imposed on these commands to further ensure that they are not misused to create a serious security and/or operational risk. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or Additional SET Command Restrictions . One of the additional restrictions is to force the Command agent to only perform SET commands that use pseudonyms or macros to control or limit which tags can have their values modified i.e. tags can no longer be typed in by the user issuing the SET command. In this way it is possible to limit the possible misuse, malicious and otherwise that could be achieved. For details of the various usage formats of this command, see SET Commands . Note: In addition to being a further security precaution, this also simplifies the process of setting process values. To further restrict the usage of SET commands: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default s

For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands and Allow ‘Set’ commands checkboxes are checked to allow this Command agent to perform SET commands. Under the Extended ‘Set’ Configuration group, check the Only ‘Set’ by pseudonym checkbox, the default is unchecked. Note: Once this checkbox is checked, the SetByPseudos specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this added restriction that apply to all of its SET commands. For details, see Specific Status Bits . -->

SET Commands Top SET Commands Function: To modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server. Note1: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a serious security and operational risk through the remote modification of process and control values. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: Due to the seriousness of the potential security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict the usage of this command. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . Note3: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. The decision of which of the following command formats to use, is usually a tradeoff between the prior configuration in the Command agent and the required amount of typing, when specifying the SMS command itself: Note1: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Note2: When using this command, it is the responsibility of the user to specify a value of the correct slot type for the tag (a

se-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Note2: When using this command, it is the responsibility of the user to specify a value of the correct slot type for the tag (agent.slot) that is being modified. Basic command syntax: SET, tagName, value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed and value is the required value for this tag. For instance: set,dig_01.value,1 This is the simplest format of this command, which requires the least prior configuration in the Command agent, it is able to modify the value of any tag, however it does require the most typing when specifying the command. Note: If the Only ‘Set’ by pseudonym setting has been enabled, then this command can ONLY be performed using pseudonyms or macros and NOT by typing in the name of required tag directly. For details, see SET Command Usage Restriction . Pseudonym usage: SET, pseudonym, value In this case, a pseudonym or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the required tag (agent.slot) and value is the required value for this referenced tag. For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command ca

r the required tag (agent.slot) and value is the required value for this referenced tag. For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command can be specified as: set,dig01v,1 Although pseudonyms save on the typing when specifying the command, ONLY the tags that have defined pseudonyms for this Command agent can be used. For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms . Macro usage: macro In this case, a macro or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the entire SET command. For instance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1ON’ is created to represent ‘set,dig_01.value,1’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1ON". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command names, they require the most pre-configuration in this Command agent and are therefore most restrictive. For details on creating and using macros, see Creating Macros . -->

Datum +/- Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum forwards or backwards in time at a specified interval. Datum - Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum backwards in time at a specified interval. Interval - for DataLog agent Length and Time configuration. Time - for EventOutput agent Time Printing setting. nection string. data RAWBYTES Encoded data about the current shift for internal use by Adroit agents. day REAL The day value for the current shift – overnight shifts will have previous day’s number from midnight until end of shift info STRING Current shift information string in the format e.g. 2010/03/17 Shift 2, 08:00 hours from 10:00 to 18:00 number INTEGER The current shift number pattern LIST A list of time shift patterns where each entry contains the following parameters: SpecialDate – a string value in the format yyyy/mm/dd that denotes a specific unique date. SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver Top SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver The Adroit simulation protocol is a software only emulation of a Siemens S5 PLC, and is provided solely for the purposes of testing and demonstration. This is particularly useful when a PLC and communications hardware is for some reason unavailable. It uses the Siemens S5 addressing scheme, which can be written to and read from. However, there is the limitation whereby only tags of the same type (Boolean, Integer, Real, String) can be mapped to the same address, otherwise the simulator will assign separate memory locations for each tag. Siemens S5 PLC data address types supported by the simulator are: For example, if you map a Digital tag to DB10:DW2.2, you may not assume that mapping an Analog tag to DB10:DW2 will actually map to the same simulated PLC address, even though the address points to the same place in the simulated PLC. Note: The Protocol Driver Monitor cannot be used on this driver. Groups of selected tags can be configured in one step, across Data Block boundaries. For example, if you scan DB4:255 the next address will now be DB5:0 and not remain at DB4:255. The default address

Groups of selected tags can be configured in one step, across Data Block boundaries. For example, if you scan DB4:255 the next address will now be DB5:0 and not remain at DB4:255. The default address is DB2:0. DB0 and DB1 are reserved for system use. Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values: To simulate a dynamic situation, the values in memory are automatically incremented, for every scan, by the DB number. The formula is: newvalue = oldvalue + DBnumber In other words, DB 0 will NEVER increment, and if DB100:DW### is scanned, the value will be incremented by 100 each scan. For Digital tags, the value will TOGGLE. -->

Slot Status Words Top Slot Status Words In addition to an overall agent status word, which shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent. This is an advanced feature that can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. The bit allocations and meanings for the slot status words are exactly the same as they are for the overall agent status. For details, see Agent Status and Slot Status . Note: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . These slot statuses may be accessed by appending the relevant status slotname after the agent and slot, e.g. ANA01.status.statusBit00. SNMP Community Strings Top SNMP Community Strings SNMP Community strings are like a user name or password that provide specific access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. ( OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. values) of a device. If the community string is correct, the device responds with the requested information. Otherwise the device simply discards the request and does not respond. The following three types of community strings determine the management commands that can be used, all of which are supported by Adroit: SNMP Read-only community string – this only allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from the managed device. Note: By convention, most equipment ships from the factory with a read-only community string set to "public". SNMP Read-Write community string – this allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from and modified within the managed device. SNMP Trap community string – this allow

ity string set to "public". SNMP Read-Write community string – this allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from and modified within the managed device. SNMP Trap community string – this allows SNMP Traps to be sent from a managed device. Traps are configured on a device to report when an error or specific event occurs. For instance, a common trap is the ‘Authentication Failure’ trap, that is sent when an incorrect community string is sent to a device. Note: Up to 16 community strings can be defined per device. Tip: Each device in a network can have its own unique set of community strings, although it may simplify network management if every device uses the same set of community strings. -->

SNMP Managed Objects Top SNMP Managed Objects Network devices that are managed by SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. expose their management data as managed objects. These managed objects might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and so on, that directly relate to the current operation of the device. EVERY managed object (value) is uniquely described and organised hierarchically in an international database, known as the SNMP Management Information Base (MIB), by means of an associated Object Identifier (OID). This OID not only uniquely describes it in the MIB but also describes the exact location of this object within the tree-like structure of the MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. database too. For details on their naming convention, see SNMP Object Identifiers . Each SNMP agent DO NOT confuse this with an Adroit agent, this is simply software running on a device that allows it to be managed by SNMP. is responsible for maintaining its own virtual MIB, which ONL

ach SNMP agent DO NOT confuse this with an Adroit agent, this is simply software running on a device that allows it to be managed by SNMP. is responsible for maintaining its own virtual MIB, which ONLY contains the managed objects supported by its device. This virtual MIB is read by an SNMP manager a program that is responsible for managing and monitoring SNMP devices, such as the Adroit SNMPManager agent. to obtain a list of this device’s managed objects, so that it can know which values to get and/or to set. Note1: SNMP allows the extension of these standard objects (as defined in the international MIB) with objects that are specific to a particular agent through the use of private MIBs. Note2: SNMP also provides a limited security system, known as SNMP Community Strings, which control the access to these objects. For details, see SNMP Community Strings . -->

SNMP Object Identifiers Top OID Naming Formats SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. (values) have an associated Object Identifier (OID), which describes the exact location of this object within the tree-like structure of the MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. of its device. Note: The MIB maintained by a device is a virtual subset of the international MIB database, which uniquely describes EVERY SNMP object. There are also two formats of these OID names: The literal name, in which the name of each branch, within the international MIB tree, is specified and separated by means of periods e.g. iso.org.dod.internet.mgmt.mib.system.sysUpTime The numeric name, where each branch name is replaced with its unique numeric position, within the international MIB tree, instead e.g. 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3 . Each SNMPMgr agent is able to retrieve and/or write to any number of SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. from a single device. text: Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent The Timer agent is able to perform one of three commonly used timing operations. The following status bits can determine, whether the configured timer is running or has expired: statusBit16 Running On if the timer is enabled i.e. the timer is operating. statusBit17 Expired On when the timer has terminated, which is timing operation-specific, as follows: The pulse width time expires, when configured as an on timer. For details, see Configuring On Timers . The delay time expires, when configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this agent, since these are sometimes independent elements i.e. the timer is not necessarily off when its value is FALSE. For details of the timing operations performed by this agent, see Timer agent . -->

text: Specifying Additional Callers Top Specifying Additional Callers Once a Command agent has been linked to a device, it is possible to specify one or more additional cell phone numbers that are able to send SMS messages to it, in addition to the configured recipient phone number. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device or Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . However it is ONLY when the Command agent has been enabled to perform commands that commands received from these phone numbers will be performed. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . WARNING! Once the Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by each unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and these additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. There are two methods by which these additional callers can be specified: Anonymous access: This requires the least configuration, although it provides unrestricted access in that anyone who phones the recipient will be able to send commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Anonymo

ires the least configuration, although it provides unrestricted access in that anyone who phones the recipient will be able to send commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Anonymous Caller Access . PLEASE NOTE: In this case EVERY unique caller who phones the recipient and issues a command to the Command agent will consume a scan point license, which will not be released until the Agent Server is shutdown. Authorised access: This requires the cell phone numbers of all the callers who are allowed to issue commands to this Command agent to be added to the Cmd phone numbers list. However, only these additional callers are able to ‘command’ this agent and hence will consume scan licenses. For details, see Configuring Authorised Caller Access . Note: This list can hold a maximum of 10 numbers. Tip: Since these commands are able to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server, it is recommended to BOTH specify the authorised phone numbers AND to limit these command-able phone numbers for security reasons. -->

In other words this dialog allows you to select the reason and its sub-reason that caused the incident to occur and/or to specify any other textual description or note concerning this incident. Tip: The ReasonsRequired status bit of the AlarmManagement agent is enabled when there are incidents that require reasons and/or notes (this can take up to 30 seconds to reflect the current status). Note: The dialog status is now sensitive to the Alarm Management agent name so that the correct set of outstanding reasons and notes are displayed in a proxy server environment, where multiple AlarmManagement agents may exist. Depending upon the configuration of the incident either the reason and/or note may be mandatory displays the current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled and as yet unspecified. To specify a reason: this requires you to select a reason AND a sub-reason that best describes the cause of this incident. Sel

s required and/or Notes required settings enabled and as yet unspecified. To specify a reason: this requires you to select a reason AND a sub-reason that best describes the cause of this incident. Select the most applicable reason for this incident from the Reasons list of the Incident reasons and notes dialog. Select the most applicable sub-reason (or cause) of this incident from the Sub-reasons list. Click the OK button. This logs the specified reason to the database of this AlarmManagement agent. To specify a note: this note should typically include some explanatory detail concerning the cause and action taken concerning this incident, especially if this is not adequately explained by the selected reason or sub-reason. If necessary, you can also launch the Incident reasons and notes dialog from a button or another picture element on a Classic UI mimic, see Customizing the launching of the View Reasons Dialog . -->

For this reason it is necessary to specify exactly which commands each Command agent are able to perform. For details on allowing a command agent to perform commands, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . To select which commands a Command agent is able to perform: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands checkbox is checked. Check or clear, the checkboxes next to the available commands, listed beneath each of the following checkboxes, as required: Note: For details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Allow ‘Get’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to retrieve the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the GetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also

Allow ‘Get’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to retrieve the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the GetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see GET Commands or Specific Status Bits . Note: This command does not pose a security risk since process values are only received. Allow ‘Set’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the SetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see SET Commands . WARNING! Since this command can cause a serious security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict its usage. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . Allow ‘Ack’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to globally and/or locally acknowledge alarms that have been reported by an agent within the Agent Server. The AckCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see ACK Commands . Note: This command DOES pose a security risk since alarms can be acknowledg

. The AckCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see ACK Commands . Note: This command DOES pose a security risk since alarms can be acknowledged remotely. -->

text: Start Communications Top Start Communications Either if the Start Comms item in the File menu is selected after the WanClient is launched or if the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, this will initiate the following sequence of events: A check is made to ensure that there is an Agent Server that is currently running on the local computer. If this fails, this error is reported in the WanClient message window and an appropriate warning message is displayed. The main database is loaded The main database is opened. If the main database does not contain any configured servers then this error is reported in the WanClient message window. WanClient then connects to the local Agent Server The database is then closed WanClient then begins the process of connecting to the configured servers by PINGing them. When a WanServer responds to the PING, the WanClient will send it its list of tags that it needs to subscribe to and the required polling periods of each tag. The WanClient will then request from the connected WanServers their changed data. Note: As soon as an error is reported, this communication process terminates. When the WanClient starts up, control tags ar

anClient will then request from the connected WanServers their changed data. Note: As soon as an error is reported, this communication process terminates. When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. -->

Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations Top Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations IMPORTANT: It is compulsory that Adroit Distributed systems are time synchronised , since clustering and other important aspects of Adroit are compromised by an unsynchronised system. This can be accomplished by ensuring that the W32Time service is enabled and working. If so, Active Directory domain member computers will automatically synchronise with the domain controller, however, Workgroup computers must ensure that they are synchronised to the same source. Also ensure that the country selection in the Regional Settings in the Control Panel is the same on all the computers. CAUTION: If the system clock is set back, the mimics, alarming and datalogging may appear to cease working and look as if the system has frozen. This is because Adroit will discard any time stamped data that is older than that currently held in the User Interface; since it always displays or records the latest events it receives. When the system clock reaches the time it was set back, the mimics, alarms and datalogging will come alive again. -->

Tag Groups Top Tag Groups The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. These tags are organised using one or more groups, which primarily manage their required communication settings. Although there are other criteria that can be used when organizing tags into groups. For details, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . While the groups provide the tag-specific communication settings, servers provide the group-specific communication settings to access the required WanServers. Therefore groups are server-specific i.e. they can only be configured after the required server(s) have been configured. For details, see Configuring Servers . Tag Groups can be configured, as follows: To configure a new tag group . To edit an existing tag group . To delete an existing tag group . To recover a formerly deleted tag group . To manually edit tag groups – this may be necessary when adding a large number of tag groups at once. -->

Tag Links Top Tag Links The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. A tag link or tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server, which together provide the communication settings, required by the WanClient to connect to the necessary WanServers. For details, see Servers or Tag Groups . Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. Tag Links can be configured, as follows: To configure a new tag link . To edit an existing tag link . To delete an existing tag link . Note: Any link that is deleted is permanently removed from the database and cannot be recovered later. To manually edit tag links – this may be necessary when adding a large number of tag links to one or more groups at once. -->

Tag to Field Mapping Buttons Top Tag to Field Mapping Buttons To add a new tag-to-field mapping simply click the button. To remove a tag-to-field mapping, click the button. To send the timestamp of this transaction to the database, click Transaction Time button, either after adding another tag-to field mapping or selecting any cell of the mapping to be used for recording the time of the transaction. This button will automatically replace the Tag field with ‘ Transaction Time ’, which will generate the time and date of the transaction in a format recognised by all databases. Note2: If an alternate time and date format is required, make use of the date/time field specifiers , but if this format is not recognised by the database then the entire transaction will fail. Tag-specific Scanning Settings Top Tag-specific Scanning Settings These settings are the scanning-specific Control bits , which are usually configured in the required agent's header . These settings apply to all the scanned slots of the agent for which they are configured. Note1: Changes made to these settings ONLY take effect when the device(s) used to scan the slots of the configured agent(s) is restarted. Note2: By this usage "scan" implies "reading", hence "scanOutput" implies "writing’. Output Enable: If this bit is set, it will enable the agent to update the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanOutputEnable or statusBit09. Scan Inhibit: If this bit is set, it will stop the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from updating a PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanInhibit or statusBit08. Output Initialise: If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Slot name: statusScanInitialise or statusBit11. -->

Tags within Selected Scan Jobs Top Tags within Selected Scan Jobs The Scanning Monitor utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server, so this information can be used to manually fine-tune the scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance. For details, see Monitoring Scanning in Adroit . The list at the bottom of this utility, displays the tags (scan points) grouped within the selected scan job or jobs within the scan job list, directly above this list. For details, see Scan Jobs within Selected Devices . Note: Scan jobs are automatically created by Adroit to group the scanned tags together in such a way as to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. For details on how to assist with this process, see Scanning Optimization Tips . This list, consists of the following columns: Tag: This identifies the name of tag (agent.slot) or scan point contained within the selected scan job(s) in the scan job list. The other columns indicate the following attributes of this scan point: Device address: This is the address of the front-end device to which or from which the value of this tag will be written or read. This addres

umns indicate the following attributes of this scan point: Device address: This is the address of the front-end device to which or from which the value of this tag will be written or read. This address is device-specific. Job offset: This indicates the offset of the item within its scan job. Bit offset: This is a legacy value, which generally shows a value of zero. Deadband: This indicates the specified deadband value for the tag Output enabled: This is 1 when the tag is output enabled, which allows this tag to write new values to the front-end device. The Accumulator Agent Top The Accumulator agent The Accumulator Agent gets its name from the type of process values that it monitors and operates in three ways: It retrieves an input value that normally accumulates over time and is always increasing in value. It uses this value to calculate the difference, or its change in value, between successive events or over a specific time or interval. Finally, it calculates the total for a period based on a predefined trigger or time interval. Operation When the agent is first enabled, it works as follows: If the intervalMode slot property is set to 4, a new period will commence immediately. If the intervalMode slot property is set to 3, the period will commence immediately but will end at the next synchronised period. At the end of every period, the value is saved as lastValue and the new value is calculated as inputValue minus startValue . If a SQL Server connection is configured, a new record is added to the history table (see History below) containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum

containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum required configuration for the Accumulator agent: Define an inputTag OR scan the inputValue and then enable the agent. Define a triggerTag and triggerMode OR a method of driving the trigger slot. Trigger event When a trigger event occurs: The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period. This results in a value which represents “the total production for the last hour or shift or day and so-on” . It then calculates the rate of change in value, which is the differential value for the current period divided by the interval of this period (value per hour) . Alarming You can also configure alarm limits for both the differential value and rate of change in value for the current period, which will monitor the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarme

the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarmed. History To maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals, you should connect the Accumulator agent to a SQL Server database: Each record captures the start and end times of the period, the start and end values and the differential value for the period. To provide automatic management of this data, then a housekeeping period can be defined to ensure that it keeps the most relevant or most recent records only. If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table is created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period Further Information For further details, read the following topics: Configuring Accumulator Agents - How to configure some or all of the functionality for an Accumulator agent. text: The AgentGroup Agent Top The AgentGroup Agent Agents that are considered to have something in common can be combined into groups by means of AgentGroup agents. For instance, all agents belonging to the north side of a process plant could be grouped in the NORTH_PLANT agent group. Agent groups may, and usually do, have overlapping memberships (i.e. an agent is allowed to belong to more than one group). For details, see Grouping Agents Together . Normal mode, the AgentGroup agent simply acts as a container for the agents grouped with it, and does not modify its status if any of its group member’s status changes. Fan in status bits mode, the AgentGroup agent will set its status bits in accordance with the status bits of its members. Only one member agent needs to set a given status bit for it to be "fanned in" to the AgentGroup’s status bit. Bulk editing of agent type mode, this is only possible if all the agents contained by the AgentGroup are of the same type, any changes made to an AgentGroup agent’s control status bits will "fan-out" to the same control bits belonging to the members of the group. The AlarmManagement Agent Top The AlarmManagement Agent Alarm Management is an important aspect of process control required to counteract inefficient alarming. Alarm management allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. In this case fewer alarms are more effective as the human mind can only focus on a few things at a time. For details, see About Alarm Management . The AlarmManagement agent logs all incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). and their details, including their time of occurrence, their time of acknowledgement and the time at which they were cleared to a database. This repository of incidents allows you to: generate statistics from the data produced by the alarming system. This allows you to have efficient and meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. measure KPIs to improve your alarming configurat

The Alias Agent Top The Alias Agent An alias is an assumed or "false" name of another agent. By containing a reference to the agent it is aliasing, the Alias agent appears to have the same Behaviour and state information of the agent it is referencing, differing only in its identity. Aliases can be very useful when attaching Behaviours to picture elements, which are to be repeatedly reused for different scenarios, such as recipes, particularly if the source agent is unknown. By simply reconfiguring the Alias agent to reference the desired agent for each scenario, the need to re-edit all the Behaviours on each picture element is eliminated. For example, a rectangular picture element with fill Behaviour supplied by tag ALI01 can be switched from REC01 to REC02 by simply re-editing the Alias agent or by dynamically changing the contents of the Alias agent’s tagname slot from REC01 to REC02 using the Operator Action, Data Set Behaviour. To access the slots of the Alias agent directly (as opposed to the slots of the agent it is aliasing), preface it with a % symbol to override its de-referencing. These scaling parameters are typically only specified, when a front-end device contains this value. The Analog agent provides support for up to 51 bit numbers, in that the new maximum range is 2,000,000,000,000,000 for unsigned numbers or -1,000,000,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000,000,000 for signed numbers. Note: To reduce the loss of accuracy in scaling caused by IEEE conversion issues, the Analog agent bypasses the scaling calculation, when the scaling is 1:1. Monitoring its value against one or more of the following value-specific alarm limits: low-low, low, high, high-high and/or rate of change. Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bits, which can be alarmed. Specifying the engineering units used to measure this value. Monitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a status bit, which can be alarmed. The ARec Agent Top The ARec Agent The ARec agent or "Associated digital Record" agent, is a fancy version of the Multistate agent that enables the configuration of up to 255 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. These 32 bits can be mapped to individual digital tags or the complete 32 bit value can be scanned from an external value. Each state can be configured to test a mask of the bits for ON, OFF or DON'T CARE conditions and can also be tested for timeouts and can be used to set status bits. In addition, each state, or timed out state, can be configured to set or clear one or more of the 32 input bits, allowing this agent to be used as a sequence controller. It is also possible to configure the AREC agent as a numerical sequence , to display text, similar to the StringList agent, except that the AREC supports up to 255 sequence steps and enables these steps to set its status bits. To edit or configure an AREC agent . Configure a Truth Table . Configure the I/O Bits . Configure the States . Configuration a Numerical Sequence . Configure the Sequence Steps . The Audit Agent Top The Audit Agent This agent supplements the auditing or logging of the Agent Server sessions and selected activities performed during these sessions to an OLE DB database. Use the Audit agent to specify one or more tags that you want to monitor for ANY change in value. When a value changes, for any reason, the agent logs this change of value to the audit database. In other words, EVERY value change for EVERY specified tag is logged, regardless of whether Adroit or a PLC or something else causes this change in value. For this reason, it is essential that you ONLY specify the process tags whose EVERY change in value is important to the running of the process . Typically you will audit set points or alarm levels, but not temperature or level values. In other words, do not specify process tags whose values that are required to change frequently as part of the normal operation, as these will simply flood your database with unnecessary records. Tip: If you want to analyse your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your

your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your Agent Server auditing and tag auditing, where Agent Server auditing includes any activities on the Agent Server, while the tag auditing is concerned specifically with data logged by any Audit agents. Each changed value is logged to the Activity table of the audit database, which records the following: The action i.e. Tag value change The process tag that is changed i.e. agentName.slotName The change in value i.e. oldValue to newValue Information common to all the other records, such as the date and time of this action, the Agent Server computer and the currently logged on username. text: The Basics of the OLE Server Interface Top The Basics of the OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The Adroit OLE server objects leverage OLE infrastructure. This may seem daunting to an end user, but the use of OLE actually makes an end user’s life easier. When talking about objects, a whole litany of terminology tends to arise. In OLE, the coarse grained entities are typically referred to as objects and containers. The words of the great OLE architect, Tony Williams, define these best. He says: "There are things, and there are places to put things". The "things" are the objects. The "places" are containers. In our case, the "things" or objects are local or remote Agent Server(s), and the "places" or containers are shrink wrapped or custom applications, written using Visual Basic™, Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, or any other OLE-aware application development platform. WOSA/XRT forces us to address another piece of terminology: OLE Automation. Extending Tony’s quote, we can say: "There are things, places to put them, and ways to talk to them". The way we talk to a thing (object) is OLE Automation. OLE Automation is simply a way for software, structured as an OLE object, to expose internal functi

text: The Beeper Agent Top The Beeper Agent The Beeper agent provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker and is usually controlled by an Alarm agent. The beeping sound is started when the value in the start slot is set to an integer greater than zero. The pitch or tone of the beeping sound depends on the contents of the start slot, and will become higher as it is incremented. The Alarm agent puts a value equal to the number of current unacknowledged alarms into this slot, to indicate that more than one agent is in alarm at the same time. Note: The pitch increases each time a new alarm is signaled, and decreases when an alarm is acknowledged. When the start slot is set to zero, or the reset slot is pulsed, the beeping sound will stop. The beeping sounds will become more urgent (i.e. interval between beeps will decrease) if the Beeper agent’s priority is increased from 0 to 4. This is a useful feature if you wish to route high priority alarms with high priority settings to one Beeper agent and low priority alarms with low priority settings to another Beeper agent. Normally, the contents of the start slot will not be saved to the loadfile (WGP file, by clicking the Save t

ne Beeper agent and low priority alarms with low priority settings to another Beeper agent. Normally, the contents of the start slot will not be saved to the loadfile (WGP file, by clicking the Save toolbar button or File menu item when the Configurator window is selected or when the Agent Server is Shutdown (if the SaveonExit advanced option is enabled). To save the contents of this slot, check the Store values when saving checkbox, which sets the dataPersist slot to 1. Beeper Agent - Slot Details . Beeper Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Command Agent Top The Command Agent The Command agent can send and receive SMS messages, by using a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver to bypass the scanning subsystem with its imposed scanning limitation of 79 character strings, so that the full 160-character SMS message length can be used. Its name is derived from its ability to also receive commands within these textual messages, which can manage Adroit remotely. Note: The sole function of this new GSM_SMS driver is to send and receive SMS messages to and from a SMS GSM modem. For details, see About the GSM_SMS driver . For details, concerning the configuration and use of this agent, see Configuring Command Agents . This agent, unlike the Notify agent, provides the following functionality: Note: If necessary, this agent can be used to SMS alarms received by the Notify agent instead. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . The ability to BOTH send and receive SMS messages of up to the full 160 character SMS message limit, instead of being restricted to only 79 characters. Send SMS messages to a single recipient, manually, programmatically or automatically to remotely monitor the status of important process

sage limit, instead of being restricted to only 79 characters. Send SMS messages to a single recipient, manually, programmatically or automatically to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For further details, see Sending SMS Messages . Sent SMS messages can also be monitored for auditing purposes. If they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period they can also be sent to another recipient via another Command agent, such as a colleague or even escalated up the management chain, if necessary. Receive SMS messages from the one or more cell phones and, if necessary, perform commands to remotely supervise and control your process and configure Adroit , for instance, by acknowledging alarms or fetching or setting process values etc. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Received or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . PLEASE NOTE: Once the Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers tha

icenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. Pseudonyms can also be used when specifying commands, to simplify the process of specifying commands by providing shorter aliases for the names of commonly referenced tag (agent.slot) names. For instance any cell entries that are displayed in blue, in the grid, can be both edited or replaced . The first untitled field numbers the information items in the grid. Item: This field specifies the configuration item, which is being displayed. Setting: This field specifies the current configuration of the specified item. The following list describes what the listed Configuration Items refer to: Server type: This field, specifies the current type of Agent Server that is running on the selected computer, as follows: Type 0 - Cluster Server: In this case master or standby mode assignment is necessary and duplicate databases need to maintained on each. eated if remote duplicate tags are found. Type 2 - Stand-alone server: In this case Proxy agents are not created if remote duplicate tags are found. The latitude (lat_DD) and longitude (lng_DD) slots can be set permanently as a record of an asset in a permanent position. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to

ompacted at the next Agent Server startup. The DbAccess Agent Top The DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle, by using OLE DB technology, supported by Microsoft. OLE DB connectivity means that Adroit can connect to any OLE DB provider, unlike ODBC that was only created to provide access to relational databases. The DbAccess Agent allows Adroit to share its information with 3rd party applications that use databases to store information. These 3rd party applications may be responsible for optimised control, reporting, MES, ERP or many other enterprise solutions. As each DbAccess agent is responsible for a transaction on a row in a database, it allows the user to specify how and where he wants the data to be stored which is ideal for reporting. Note: If a connection fails, due to network problems etc. the DbAccess agent will recover and continue transacting. The DbAccess agent allows the following transactions to be performed: new rows can be added to an existing table; existing rows can be updated with current information; specific rows or the entire table can be deleted and data can be retrieved from the table inserted into

w rows can be added to an existing table; existing rows can be updated with current information; specific rows or the entire table can be deleted and data can be retrieved from the table inserted into tags inside the Agent Server. These transactions can be done on demand, they can be scheduled and (or) they can be triggered. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. The DbAccess agent is ideally used in applications where data inside the Agent Server is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job) for reporting reasons. It is not suited for fast logging of data. Usage Guidelines . Basic Principles . Configuring the DbAccess Agent . Connection string Tag to database table field mapping . Field Format Specifiers . This agent also provides: a Logging method list box to select the required methods for specifying when and how the listed tags are logged. a String logging checkbox (the BOOLEAN strLog slot), which when enabled logs the tag values as Strings and not numeric values; this also allows you to log other string slots (this will log the first 79 characters). a Housekeeping section to specify how long, in days, that you want to store your logged tags. n days, that you want to store your logged tags. This depends upon the storage capacity you have available for your database and how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. The DBQuery Agent Top The DBQuery Agent The DBQuery agent provides a robust and efficient methodology for asynchronously executing OLE DB transactions. The agent was created to supersede the DBAccess agent and consequently provides more powerful control by giving you direct access to the query to be executed. The agent is designed to perform SELECT transactions on a database easily and can be configured to perform any other SQL Query transaction using the custom query option. The agent can also be configured to run manually, triggered by a tag or run periodically. The agent can also be configured to execute stored procedures. Configuration Configuring the DBQuery agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below. The agent dialog provides the ability to set several options: (See the Configuration slots option for more information.) Enable or disable the functionality of this particular agent. Disable transactions executed on the standby server. Select the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the requi

the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the required tag list. Enter the required Table name . Enter the WHERE clause containing tag names within an angled bracket (< >) pair. The agent automatically substitutes these tags into values first and then performs the following example SELECT statement transaction: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) Enter a custom query. Let’s have a look at a few Custom Query examples. If a SELECT query returns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown below: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC Because Adroit only uses the first record returned, the example custom query could effectively be changed to: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in th

: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in the tag list will be ignored because you would add this information to the custom query. Custom SELECT queries will substitute the ‘Tagname’ entries in the tag list with values returned from the custom query, therefore it is important to ensure that the custom SELECT query requests the data in the order required by order of the ‘Tagname’ entries. Other Custom Query examples For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume failure with the above query. Delete records The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019. The query disregards the contents of the tag list in the dialog. DELETE FROM MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1,

MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (1, 1, 123, 456 ,678, 901) or INSERT INTO MyTable (dt, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (<systeminfo.currenttime>, 1, 1, <f1.value>,<f2.value>,<f3.value>,<f4.value>) Execute Query Automatically The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes SELECT date,timestart,timeend FROM shift_adv_sh1 WHERE idx=<f1.value> Running Stored Procedures The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameters as may be required by the stored procedure EXEC spCheckRecords 1,5 For all SELECT queries or stored procedures which return data, these results will be substituted into the tags as specified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following:

cified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following: Simply apply the index number to use e.g. 0, 1 or 2. or Leave the field name empty for the tag entry, The agent will then attempt to use the row number (beginning with 0) of the tag entry as the field name. Agent Slots DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds ma

The Device Agent Top The Device Agent Device agents are used to manage the Adroit -specific communication settings of one or more tags (agent.slot) for a device that has already been added to an installed protocol driver. This device is typically a logical connection to a front-end device, with which it communicates. For further details concerning the role this agent plays in communicating values, see the Scanning Overview . For this reason, Device agents cannot simply be added to the Agent Server like other agents. Instead its associated ‘device’ must first be added to an installed protocol driver. For details, see About Protocol Drivers . Then it is only when this device, which appears in the Device list in the Tag scanning configuration dialog, is selected when scanning a tag (agent.slot), for the first time, that a Device agent with the same name is added to the Agent Server. For details, see Scanning Adroit tags . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. Fo

ub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . The purpose of a Device agent is simply to manage the Adroit tags that have been scanned to it and their communication to and from its associated front-end device, as follows: The Device agent automatically creates Scan agents, which generally contain a manageable amount of tags that are scanned to contiguous addresses. Each Scan agent manages the scanning configuration of their assigned Adroit tags, such as their poll rate, deadband, timestamps etc. For details, see Configuring Device Agents . Note1: The Device agent also removes these Scan agents when Adroit tags are unscanned from it. Note2: Since Scan agents are created dynamically, it is not recommended to use their slots in other agents, such as Expression agents, since their names are not fixed. The DumpConfig Agent Top The DumpConfig agent The DumpConfig agent is used for reporting purposes only and is a special report that exists in the Adroit Pack of our Adroit Report Suite. The sole function of this agent is to periodically record a snapshot (or a dump, or a record) of the current configuration of certain agent types. The snapshot record is saved to specific tables in an OLE DB database that will allow reports to be generated. An example of its use is to report on agents in the context of their configuration at the time of the report, or it may be used to audit changes made to specific agents. text: The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Top Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Note: Asynchronous or non-polling exception-based (telemetry) drivers are particularly affected by shadowed cluster servers. When a second cluster partner, is started, it will start in standby mode and then any Classic UIs configured to attach to this newly started server will display any tags that are linked to "telemetry" device(s) as being "greyed-out" or marked bad. This is by design, since Adroit has no way of knowing what which of these tags are healthy at startup because of the unsolicited nature of these telemetry drivers. Therefore Adroit errs on the side of caution and greys out all the tags, this also protects the shadow system from mismatched databases in the cluster. Note: Normally, this should only be a problem on the UI of an unmanned cluster node, which is configured to connect locally, since all other remote UIs should be tracking the master. When the clustered servers are both online and the standby is "bad" because it has been started up later than the master, try one of the following: Stop and restart the affected devices on the master server. Swap master an

The EventLogging Agent Top The EventLogging Agent The logging of events in Adroit is managed by the EventLogging agent, which is provided as a destination for one or more alarm routes. This agent is able to log events to the following locations: to the Applications event log on any Windows computer on the network. to an OLE DB compatible database, such as MS Access or MS SQL. Note: Events logged to this database CANNOT be viewed in the Event Log Viewer window. Typically, events include undesirable states, process values and the malfunction of control devices. Logged events are used to analyse process conditions over a specified period. Some of the types of events that can be logged by Adroit include: incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). : agents going into alarm, being acknowledged and cleared change monitoring events : when the values of Analog or Digital agents change that are configured for change monitoring control events: any operator control action that is configured to log events,

The Expression Agent Top The Expression Agent The Expression agent can create powerful user-defined calculations. It functions by gathering data from other agents, or from the plant directly by scanning into slots V01 to V20, and performs a user defined mathematical transformation to calculate an output value. This result can be fed into a front-end device on the plant, or to a picture in the Classic User Interface for display, or sent to another agent. Note1: The Expression agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configuration. Data Acquisition . Display Options . Evaluation Options . Calculations . Examples . Agent Slot Details . Database File Format . text: The Frame Agent Top The Frame Agent A Frame agent can store 32 character strings (in slots V01 to V32 ), each string having a length of up to 79 characters (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). These character strings are indexed (from 1 to 32) and the current string being pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. By suitable indexing, the text string in the value slot can be made to change in a predetermined manner. For example, the Frame agent FRA01 has the four character strings cold , cool , warm and hot edited into its slots v01, v02, v03 and v04. If the value in FRA01.index slot is 4, then the character string hot will be duplicated in the FRA01.value slot. In this way, by subscribing to another agent’s integer slot type, the Frame agent can translate the subscribed value into an appropriate meaningful text message using its indexing Behaviour. The ICMP Agent Top The ICMP or PING Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. This round trip time is the time that it takes to send an ICMP message to the remote IP address and to receive its reply. How to use the ICMP or PING agent to ensure the availability of a networked device Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent : this describes the status bits of this agent that can be used for diagnosing the existence of the specified remote device on the network.
