The IOT Agent Top The IOT agent The term Internet of Things (IOT) is an abstract concept that refers to an ever-growing network of physical objects that use an Internet Protocol (IP) address for Internet communication between these objects and other Internet-enabled devices and systems. This implies connecting any device with an interface to the Internet and also possibly to each other. IOT is expected to offer advanced connectivity of devices, systems, and services that goes beyond machine-to-machine (M2M) communications and covers a variety of protocols, domains, and applications. The interconnection of these embedded devices (including smart objects), is expected to support automation in many technological fields. Creating a specific IOT Agent As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP. All that is required is to first copy the default Adroit IOT agent x_iot.dll to a new file called t_2KVAPump.dll in the Adroit system folder, which is typically found at C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . The newly copied agent type is then available to Adroit. A newly created IOT agent can represent any object containing multiple properties or slots. Currently, the

Currently, the IOT agent does not support real-time catch-up . Management slots By default, The IOT agent in itself does not contain any useful slots that are usable for end-user process purposes. It does, however, contain four management slots that may be used to build up the structure of the IOT agent after it has been created. Select the Agent Specific Slots option below to view more information. The xmlSlots slot When this agent is created, it only contains the management slots, one being the xmlSlots slot which is used to create and configure the user-defined slots. This agent does not have any default status slots. The expression engine is similar to the expression engine used by UDP-Based Protocol (UDT) agents for manipulating status slot values (See the “ Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions ” topic). The Marshal Agent Top The Marshal Agent The Marshal agent is designed to replace the popular marshalling function of the Multistate agent, by gathering discreet binary data from its 16 bit rawvalue or value slot. By giving each of the individual bits the full functionality of a digital agent, the Marshal agent exceeds the former capabilities of a marshalled mode Multistate Agent. These bits can then be alarmed, pulsed, named, and the 1 and 0 states of each bit can be named (on/off, open/closed etc). Tip: You can implement and use the MarshalAlarmMode registry value, to specify the type of information reported in the description field for Marshal agent alarms. Only the ON state is reflected in the status bit header slots of the agent and therefore the alarming subsystem has been extended to allow the alarming of status bits that are ON or OFF. The rawvalue and value relationship can also be reversed i.e. mirrored. To address the individual properties of each bit in the Marshal agent, e.g. from a mimic, used the following convention: MarshalAgentName.BitName.slot , e.g. MSH1.Switch.Value - will address the Value slot of the Switch bit inside the MSH1 Marshal agent. The MaxDemand Agent Top The MaxDemand Agent What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? . The MaxDemand agent predicts the maximum kVA demand for the current block period the interval over which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand, which is typically 30 minutes. so you can create alarms if the predicted consumption exceeds a predefined limit. This enables you to control the electricity consumption during each block period and prevent your actual “maximum demand limit” from being exceeded. For details on how to use this agent to monitor your maximum demand, see Maximum Demand Quick Start . Usually, control entails turning off machines which do not affect the main production process or which are not essential. While the primary aim of this agent is to monitor your power usage, it can also automate the control of your electricity consumption. In other words you can use its MaxDemand status slot in a script or expression agent to perform the necessary remedial actions. The MaxDemand agent can also calculate your instantaneous power factor, which also has the potential to save you money. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent sup

actions. The MaxDemand agent can also calculate your instantaneous power factor, which also has the potential to save you money. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue monitoring your maximum demand. Related topics: Configuring the MaxDemand agent : To explain the various configuration options. Specific Status Bits : To describe how you can use the provided status bits of this agent. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. This agent also provides the following additional slots: kVAOptimal , mdOverUnder and timeToMD . See MaxDemand Agent - Slot Details . -->

The OEE Agent Top The OEE Agent What is OEE? Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) is a measurement of how effectively a single piece of equipment, or a group of equipment, and even how an entire factory is being utilised. OEE is percentage determined by the cumulative impact of the following three factors: Availability : is the percentage of the actual running time of the monitored equipment and/or factory. So this factor is decreased by the activities that cause unplanned downtime. Performance : is the percentage of how often the monitored equipment and/or factory performs at optimum speed. So this factor is decreased by the all the factors preventing the equipment and/or factory from running at optimal speed. Quality : is the percentage of good quality items produced by the monitored equipment and/or factory. So this factor is decreased by the amount of produced waste or bad quality and scrapped items. OEE% = Availability% x Performance% x Quality% This OEE percentage takes into account all losses in downtime, speed and quality and can therefore be used for analysis and benchmarking. Why use the OEE agent? The OEE agent can : EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment

ount all losses in downtime, speed and quality and can therefore be used for analysis and benchmarking. Why use the OEE agent? The OEE agent can : EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant. Since targeting the three key OEE factors simultaneously, can effect significant improvements in production. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate OEE OR measure a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . In other words, individual OEE agents can be applied to any component or part of a process for which a variable denoting a measurement of output is available, as follows: Note: The number of OEE agents that you can add to your Agent Server is determined by the OEE Count parameter of your Adroit license. KPIs are typically the measurement of some production value over time OR one production value against (divided by) another production value. Therefore the OEE agent can measure TWO variables: the FIRST variable (the REAL input1 slot) the SECOND variable (the REAL input2 slot), used as a DIVISOR of the first (input1/input2). Note: If the SECOND variable is not spec

an measure TWO variables: the FIRST variable (the REAL input1 slot) the SECOND variable (the REAL input2 slot), used as a DIVISOR of the first (input1/input2). Note: If the SECOND variable is not specified, then the FIRST variable is simply divided by time. In this way it is possible to measure production figures, such as ton/hr, kWh/ton, total produced, actual run-hours, etc. The measured KPI can either compare actual performance with benchmark figures or compare shift performances or today’s performance with the previous day or the previous day's shifts. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI This agent supports real-time catch-up on a standby clustered Agent Server from a master server and Agent Server session persistence via a work file in the project work folder, typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. The PerfMon Agent Top The PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent is used to monitor Windows Performance counters, which belong to performance objects such as the Agent Server, Processor, Memory, and others. These counters facilitate the monitoring of the computers performance and assist in detecting performance bottlenecks that could adversely affect the functioning of Adroit . The values of these counters are updated every second and can also be assigned to other tags, such as Analog agents, which can then be appropriately alarmed. Up to 16 performance counters can be monitored per agent. The following performance counters are added, by default, to first PerfMon agent created: CPU load i.e. \\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time Agent Server CPU load i.e. \\Process(as)\\% Processor Time Total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes Agent Server memory usage i.e. \\Process(as)\\Private Bytes and \\Process(as)\\Virtual Bytes Agent Server put slots i.e. \\Agent Server(name (project))\\PutSlots Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, bec

s Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc To edit or configure a PerfMon agent . To Add a Performance Counter to the Grid . PerfMon Agent - Slot Details . PerfMon Agent - Database File Format . -->

The PID Agent Top The PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent. These values can then be scanned to the outside world, via their raw slots. This provides great savings in the overall number of agents required in the configuration of a project that contains PID controllers. Configurable high and low operation limits are provided for the SP (set-point) and CV (control variable) slots, which will prevent these values from being set to potentially harmful values, when they are being manually configured. This agent also triggers alarm conditions based on configurable alarm limits that are indicated by the specific status bits . Added support for realtime catch-up To edit or configure a PID agent . The Primitive Agents Top The Primitive Agents The primitive agent types Boolean, Integer, Real and String are the simplest building blocks. Instances of these primitive agent types are used simply to hold a single value in the value slot. They do not contain any other slots or additional functionality such as inversion, pulsing, linearisation, etc, as found in the Digital, Analog and other agent types. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! These agents should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. A Boolean agent will hold a Boolean value (0 or 1) An Integer agent will hold an integer number -2147483648 to +2147483647 (32 bits) Note: The specific status bits of the Integer agent will be set if its value is between 0 and 15. A Real agent will hold a double precision floating point number (64 bits) A String agent will hold a 79 character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). Due to the increasing need of customers for the Agent Server to support strings longer than 79 characters, the String agent now has a new slot called valueex that is able to

ro terminator character). Due to the increasing need of customers for the Agent Server to support strings longer than 79 characters, the String agent now has a new slot called valueex that is able to contain these longer strings. Usage examples for these longer strings include queries that are created dynamically and long descriptions. WARNING! This new "valueex" slot is NOT supported by the scanning subsystem because the scanning subsystem cannot handle strings larger than 80 characters in length. Note: This new valueex slot is now identical to the String slot type of Custom agents, which have always supported strings that are greater than 79 characters. The legacy "value" slot of the String agent will still remain and contain the first 79 characters of the "valueex" slot. Therefore the "valueex" slot will always be equal to the "value" slot its string length is less than 79 characters (excluding the zero terminator). Note: When editing the String agent, only the "valueex" slot can be configured, although the content of the "value" slot is also displayed. -->

The Script Agent Top The Script Agent The Script agent provides a way for the user to execute complicated tasks such as batching, reporting or complex mathematical operations through a Visual basic script or Java script. IMPORTANT: If your Agent Server is running as a service and you create a script that needs access to protected network resources or that launch other Windows programs or perform any other function that requires a logged on user. Then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to perform these functions. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: This agent does not replace the expression agent , as the expression agent can execute simple calculations far more efficiently and faster than the Script agent. Each Script agent can be configured to have an associated list of module files that contain user-defined variables, functions and subroutines. The Script agent allows the user to interact with the Agent Server , in order to access and manipulate data within the Agent Server. A script is compiled after the Agent Server has started

ubroutines. The Script agent allows the user to interact with the Agent Server , in order to access and manipulate data within the Agent Server. A script is compiled after the Agent Server has started up or whenever the script agent is modified from within the Agent Configurator. The script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine, in one of four different ways. For details, see Running the Main Subroutine . PLEASE NOTE: There is no way for the Agent Server to protect itself from badly written or buggy scripts and Adroit Technologies does not take responsibility for badly written or buggy scripts written by users. Users also have the ability to launch other applications, or manipulate other applications via OLE automation, for example to configure reports in Microsoft Excel or Microsoft Word. The Script agent may also be used as an alternative to using the Recipe agent and it can be used to perform simple scheduled tasks. Note1: If you are using scripts to obtain datetime tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. text: The Shift Agent Top The Shift Agent Various agents in Adroit , such as OEE, require knowing the current shift number. Instead of configuring the shift pattern information into each instance of these agents, you can instead configure these shift patterns globally, in a Shift agent, for use by any interested agents. The value slot of the Shift agent should also be scanned, output enabled, to any PLCs that perform any shift end functions, such as resetting shift count accumulators. Tip: Multiple shift agents can define different shift patterns that may occur within a plant. The Shift agent continually monitors the current time and checks it against the configured shift pattern to determine the current shift number. If NO matching shift pattern is found, the shift value is set to 0. Configured shift patterns are selected using the following order of preference: In other words if one or more shift patterns have the current time configured, then the configuration of the shift pattern determines which is selected, in the following order: Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. nes which is selected, in the following order: Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. Annually recurring holidays on a given day of the month, such as Christmas 25 Dec. The Statistical Agent Top The Statistical Agent Statistical Process Control and Acceptance Sampling are methods used to detect significant changes in the manufacturing process and to monitor the quality of manufactured items being produced in batches. The problem is to decide whether a batch should be accepted or rejected on the basis of a sample, which is randomly or otherwise, drawn from the batch. There are many ways to make a sample - whether at timed intervals or on triggered events. The Statistical agent provides the basic functionality for a user to build a statistical process control strategy using its built in data collection method and by linking the agent to other Adroit agents. Note1: The Statistical agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: Use agent persistence files to prevent Statistical agents from losing their statistical data, instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . PLEASE NOTE: When exporting Statistical agents, ensure that the Floating average enabled checkbox is UNCHECKED, then save the WGP file and export. After importing, re-enable this checkbox for the applicable Statistical agents. Th

tatistical agents, ensure that the Floating average enabled checkbox is UNCHECKED, then save the WGP file and export. After importing, re-enable this checkbox for the applicable Statistical agents. There is a Statistical agent Wizard to demonstrate its operation, which can be found in the Wizards folder under the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \Wizards. The Tag-link Database Top The Tag-link Database Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database. This database stores a list of WanServer(s) and tags whose values are to be fetched or sent to or from each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers and these database files are stored in the database-folder . The tag link database is typically (initially) created using the WanClient Configurator, which can be launched from the Open Configurator item of the WanClient File menu and is used to stores the following items: The communication settings of each remote (Wan)Server whose Agent Server contains tags that either need to be fetched or sent. The tag groups , these tag groups classify tag-links in terms of the type of communication that is required and are server-specific. For details on possible criteria to use for creating tag groups, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . The tag-links , specify the required local and the remote tag name, whose values are ‘linked’ and are tag group-specific. The local tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanClient computer, and typically received its value from the remote tag name UNLESS it is wi

ose values are ‘linked’ and are tag group-specific. The local tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanClient computer, and typically received its value from the remote tag name UNLESS it is within a control group, in which case it can set the value of the remote tag. The remote tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanServer computer, and typically supplies the value for the remote tag. Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. The name of the file that stores the tag-link database for each WanServer is user-defined, typically when adding or editing the communication details of a WanServer. This file can be edited manually, in Excel or any other CSV file editor, for bulk configuration purposes. The onus is then upon the user to ensure that all the values entered into these files are correct. For details, see bulk configuration of tag groups and bulk configuration of tag links . -->

The Timer Agent Top The Timer Agent The Timer agent can perform several commonly used timing operations. This agent provides a Boolean value slot as an output, which is enabled (set to TRUE) and disabled (set to FALSE) by the agent, depending upon its current mode of operation. This slot can therefore be used as an enabling or disabling or scheduling tag for other agents. Note: Although the Timer agent does not provide a cold-start value, it does support real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server, which means that if the master Agent Server fails, the timing operation will seamlessly continue. This agent can perform one of following three timing operations or modes: Example: to illustrate the action of the three timing operations. This is a trend of the value and start slots of three Timer agents, to indicate their timing actions. In this example: each Timer agent is named after its configured timing operation for the purposes of easy identification ONLY, you can name your Timer agents anything you like. all the delays and pulse widths are 3 seconds long. On timer: This mode can be used for the timing of specific events. The value slot is only enabled for the speci

your Timer agents anything you like. all the delays and pulse widths are 3 seconds long. On timer: This mode can be used for the timing of specific events. The value slot is only enabled for the specified period (pulse width). For details, see Configuring On Timers . Note: This, in effect, provides the same functionality as a pulsed digital. On delay timer: This mode can be used for the filtering out of specific events. The value slot is only enabled after the required period of delay has elapsed. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . Pulse generator: This mode can be used for generating free running square waves. The value slot is enabled for the duration of the required pulse width and then disabled for the required period of delay. The period of the generated pulse is the sum of the delay and pulse width times. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: All the timing operations, with the exception of the Pulse generator , can be automatically reset. The status bits of this agent can show when the timer is running or has expired. For details, see Specific Status Bits . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this

its of this agent can show when the timer is running or has expired. For details, see Specific Status Bits . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this agent, since these are sometimes independent elements i.e. the timer is not necessarily off when its value is FALSE. Time Stamping Top Time Stamping Adroit achieves its accuracy by time stamping data at the point of creation whenever possible. Scanned values get their timestamp from the data packet returned by the front-end device, if the protocol driver is exception based and implements a time-stamping protocol. A time stamp may also be created in an agent when a user enters a value manually. The time is taken from the systemInformation agent, which in turns gets it from the system clock. The name of the operation which causes this is the putslot method, which as well as updating the value in the target slot (e.g. value ), also updates the agentTimeStamp slot. When the agent subsequently sends a subscription update to another agent, or picture element Behaviour, the same timestamp value is passed on. For example, if the Alarm agent receives a subscription update, it will route the timestamp it gets to whichever printers, event logs, alarm lists and beeper agents it has been configured with. Timestamps will propagate into the user interface, into mimics and ultimately into picture elements containing associated Behaviours. For this reason, it should be clear that tampering with the system clock i

ps will propagate into the user interface, into mimics and ultimately into picture elements containing associated Behaviours. For this reason, it should be clear that tampering with the system clock is NOT advised. In particular, setting the clock backwards (say from 10:00 to 09:00) will have the effect of freezing all mimic updates, datalogging and existing alarms, for a period of 1 hour, until the timestamping mechanism "catches up" with the new time. Note: Sites using the SystemInformation time for calculations should be especially careful. -->

Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster Top Time Synchronization It is essential that both the cluster Agent Servers and their clients have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively. This is ALSO critical in a distributed Adroit installation (where there are multiple user interfaces and/or Agent Servers on different computers) that the system times of all of the computers are synchronised to a common source. Adroit will behave unpredictably on a system which system time is not synchronised with the computer it’s connecting to. Time synchronization is typically managed by the Windows Time service that is installed by the default installation of Windows XP and later operating systems. The following are symptoms of unsynchronised times: The User Interface does not seem to be updating with the most recent information. The Trend displays odd Behaviour: either the data seems to be inserted into the middle of the trend, or a strange unexplainable sudden change in the values being trended when pressing F5 to refresh the trend. The data logs of the two unsynchronised Agent Servers in a cluster seem to get corrupted (as a result of the data being inserted into the

This corruption is most notable in a trend. Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds. To indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. This feature does NOT affect Adroit clients (UIs) that connect to a remote Agent Server. Timer Agent - Slot Details Top Timer Agent - Slot Details The Timer Agent performs several commonly used timing operations, which previously could only be inefficiently accomplished by using expressions, recipes and scripts. This agent is located in the following file: T_TIMER.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function autoReset BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this will automatically reset the start slot, 100 milliseconds after the timer has expired. Not used if the freeRun slot is enabled. delayTime INTEGER The delay time (in ms) i.e. the time before the pulse (value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Timers . freeRun BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this enables the "pulse generator" mode of operation. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . granularity INTEGER The granularity (in ms) determines how often the Timer agent monitors the time after the timer has started. If less than the duration of the timer, then the timeleft slot indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds, before this timer expires. The default value of 0, forces the granularity period to equal the required duration of t

of the timer, then the timeleft slot indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds, before this timer expires. The default value of 0, forces the granularity period to equal the required duration of the timer, so that this timeleft slot is never calculated. WARNING! The smaller the specified granularity, the greater the amount of work the Agent Server is required to perform in updating its clients with the timeleft slot value. Note: Although this granularity value is has a minimum of 100 ms, a minimum of 1000 ms is recommended as a "safe" value. inputTag TAGNAME This can automatically start the timer by subscribing to another tag in the Agent Server. Note1: If this tag is numeric, then the start slot is enabled (set to TRUE) when it’s value is non-zero. Note2: If this tag is a string, then the start slot is enabled when this string is not empty. pulseWidth INTEGER The pulse width (in ms) OR the time at which the pulse ( value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on delay timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . start BOOLEAN Starts and stops the timer. Note: When this slot is set to FALSE, the value slot is also set to FAL

o if an "on delay timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . start BOOLEAN Starts and stops the timer. Note: When this slot is set to FALSE, the value slot is also set to FALSE and the currently configured timer expires. timeLeft INTEGER If the granularity slot is set at 100 milliseconds or greater and is less than the required duration of the timer, then this slot displays the amount of time left in the timing cycle in milliseconds. value BOOLEAN The output of the timer. Note: This slot can be used to enable, disable or schedule other agents. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 Running On if the timer is enabled i.e. the timer is operating. status bit 17 Expired On when the timer has terminated, the event which causes this to occur is timing operation-specific, as follows: The pulse width time expires, when configured as an on timer. For details, see Configuring On Timers . The delay time expires, when configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Methods

configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the agent database file (.WGP), see: Timer Agent - Database File Format . -->

Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance Top Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance Title 21 CFR Part 11 (21 CFR 11) of the Code of Federal Regulations deals with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES). This defines the criteria and circumstances under which electronic records and electronic signatures are considered to be trustworthy, reliable and equivalent to paper records by the FDA. In short, for those records that remain subject to part 11, need to adhere to the following requirements: the validation of computerised systems computer-generated time-stamped audit trails to ensure the trustworthiness and reliability of the records the need to provide investigators with reasonable and useful access to records during an inspection Furthermore, 21 CFR 11 also requires that the following controls and requirements be implemented: limiting system access to authorised individuals use of operational system checks use of authority checks use of device checks determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks establishment of

ty checks use of device checks determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks establishment of and adherence to written policies that hold individuals accountable for actions initiated under their electronic signatures appropriate controls over systems documentation -->

PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". If the following settings are correct the system will automatically log you on the next time that you boot. If the changes are bad, a message box will notify you, closing the box will invoke the standard logon procedure. From the Start menu, select Run …, type in REGEDIT and click OK Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\WindowsNT\Current

ou, closing the box will invoke the standard logon procedure. From the Start menu, select Run …, type in REGEDIT and click OK Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\WindowsNT\CurrentVersion\WinLogon . Select Add Value from the REGEDT32 Edit menu and enter the name of AutoAdminLogon with a data type of REG_SZ and a string value "1". Select Add Value again and enter the name DefaultPassword with a data type of REG_SZ and a string that is the password for your computer. All of the data between the two specified times in the datalogs on one of the cluster partners is mirrored across to the datalog agents on the other cluster partner. Since this may vary between device types, the user should ascertain the correct front-end device span is used for each value. Note: Once these limits are set these values cannot be manually set above and below these limits. The inner (H or L) and outer (HH or LL) High and Low alarm limits for the PV can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. Note: When the Cascade checkbox is ticked, the SP is controlled by the output (PV) of another PID agent, therefore the SP edit box is greyed out. text: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging Top To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging The user has no direct control over the speed at which the raw data log file will grow. Therefore, it is important to calculate the maximum space each agent may occupy, before the data log file wraps around and overwrites itself from the beginning. This figure can be compared to the actual free disk space available on the host computer. Two files are involved in storing historical data: the raw data log file (.LGD) and its index file (.LGI) which uses comparatively little space. Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . The amount of disk space reserved for data logging is a function of the rate at which the tag is being logged i.e. the time between each sample and the total logging period specified for each tag, summed for all the tags being logged. Each log record takes 20 b

metadata.title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging

text: ion of the rate at which the tag is being logged i.e. the time between each sample and the total logging period specified for each tag, summed for all the tags being logged. Each log record takes 20 bytes therefore it would be expected that the following formulae would be used to calculate the maximum raw disk space that may be used for each .LGD file: Raw Buffer size (bytes) = 20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate) Raw File size (bytes) = Sum of all Raw Buffer sizes Example of raw disk space calculations . However, the original design of datalogging made the assumption that the data would only change 5 times slower than the rate actually configured and therefore Adroit is designed to only reserve 20% of the space calculated above. Hence the following formulae must be used to accurately calculate the actual disk space that will be used for each .LGD file: PLEASE NOTE: Adroit ’s proprietary logging uses an in-built logging factor, which reduces the specified logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Actual Buffer size (bytes) = [20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate)]/

metadata.title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging

text: clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Actual Buffer size (bytes) = [20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate)]/5 Actual File size (bytes) = Sum of all Buffer sizes While the above design assumption can be considered true for faster logging rates such as 1 second, this is definitely not the case for slower rates such as 1 minute or 1 hour where the values (especially analog values) will have definitely changed. In the latter Adroit will only have capacity to log for 1/5th of the configured period necessitating the user to over specify his logging period by a factor of 5. Note: It is possible to override this 20% data log capacity or the "divide by 5" storage factor, by setting the LogCompressionFactor registry setting. Each Datalog agent has a maximum of 53 million records, which can provide at least 30 days of logging at a log rate of 50 milliseconds! For instance: if the log rate is 100 ms, 10 values are logged per second, 36000 values/hour, 864000 values/day, so the total logging length of this datalog file = 53000000/864000 = 61.34 days. Instead of using one log file for all agents, you can

metadata.title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging

text: ues are logged per second, 36000 values/hour, 864000 values/day, so the total logging length of this datalog file = 53000000/864000 = 61.34 days. Instead of using one log file for all agents, you can create different log files for agents (values) that require different logging speeds. For example, DAY.LGD, WEEK.LGD, MONTH.LGD and YEAR.LGD. Note: Adroit allows a slot of an agent to be datalogged once only. If multiple logfiles need to be created from, for example, an ANA01.value, then this can be done by using an intermediate agent such as an Expression agent called EXP01. Insert the ANA01.value into the Expression Agent’s slots v01, v02 and v03, and configure EXP01 for data logging, such that: ANA01.value is logged at 1 second intervals for 5 days into logfile DAY.LGD EXP01.v01 is logged at 15 second intervals for 7 days into logfile WEEK.LGD EXP01.v02 is logged at 120 second intervals for 31 days into logfile MONTH.LGD EXP01.v03 is logged at 8 hour intervals for 365 days into logfile YEAR.LGD -->

To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Top To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Typically the Agent Server is configured to run as a Service during the install, although you can do this after the install if necessary by using the following command line switches that the Agent Server process (as.exe) provides: Press the Windows key + R shortcut to open the Run dialog. Type in as.exe followed by following commands and press ENTER: /install /u:"[Domain\]Username" /p:"Password" /quiet This command will install the Agent Server as a service. The /u: and /p: parameters specify the credentials of the user account that the Agent Server service will run as, ensure that you specify a user that has the rights / permissions to access the network resources (printers, SQL Express, network shares) that the Agent Server requires access to. IMPORTANT: The username MUST NOT be "Administrator", the built-in Windows Administrator account, since UAC is automatically disabled whenever this built-in Administrator account is used, which causes a myriad of problems to occur. Note: The [Domain\] portion of the username ONLY applies if the specified user is on a domain. The /q

text: To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure Top To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure The following steps can be taken: Use only NTFS instead of FAT or FAT32 file partitions2. Remove "flush lazily" setting on Adroit Logging. The adverse side effect of this is that duty cycle on disk will be much more intense, as every change will be flushed right through to disk. In consequence disk may need replacing after several months/years (who knows). In addition system throughput may be reduced. Make sure a battery-backed UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is installed so that power is never removed from the server in an uncontrolled fashion. This option allows "flush lazily" to be enabled. Note: This option provides the only cast iron guarantee, but most sites find option 1 sufficient. -->

metadata.title: To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure

In the Add tag edit box, if required, modify the currently selected agent and slot combination. In the

metadata.title: To Modify the Scanning Configuration of Scanned Tags

text: canned tag list, below this Device list box, click on the scanned tag that needs to be modified. In the Add tag edit box, if required, modify the currently selected agent and slot combination. In the Device address edit box, if required, modify the protocol driver specific address in this Device to which the value of this tag will be stored. In the Scan rate (ms) edit box, if required, modify the scanning interval or period in milliseconds between attempts to poll this item. Note: This will only apply to polled devices; telemetry devices will ignore this parameter. In the Deadband edit box, if required, modify the limit that the change in the scanned value must exceed before the agent’s slot is updated. This Deadband is in the same units as the tag that is being scanned. For performance reasons, it is advisable to give a non-zero Deadband for Analog or Integer values in order to filter out noise or minor variations in value, since applying a Deadband reduces the number of changes to the database thus improving performance. Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents Top Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents The DbAccess agent can perform the following transactions: Insert row: Use this transaction to insert a new record of tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s into a table, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is not required for this transaction, as the new record is inserted at the end of the existing records in the table. Note: If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then when a cluster is accessing the same database, this setting prevents both nodes (Agent Servers) in a cluster from executing the transaction thereby causing double entries for "Insert" transactions. Update row: Use this transaction to update a row in a table with new tag/s, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is required for this transaction to take place. Delete row: Use this transaction to delete one or many rows from a table in a database. This is the only transaction that does not require a tag-to-field mapping. IMPORTANT: If the row identification field is left empty , then all of the rows in the table are removed and the entire table

his is the only transaction that does not require a tag-to-field mapping. IMPORTANT: If the row identification field is left empty , then all of the rows in the table are removed and the entire table is deleted . Retrieve row: Use this transaction to update tag/s with value/s from a row of a table in a database, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. The DbAccess Agent has to know in what format date/time information is kept in the database to perform a successful translation. Note: This agent also supports the retrieval of time-stamped values from SQL into Adroit Filetime slot values. If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then the master Agent Server will perform the Retrieve transaction and shadow the result to the standby Agent Server tags. If this option is NOT enabled and client runtime transaction shadowing is also enabled, then any Retrieve transactions performed by this DbAccess agent will be performed by both cluster nodes (Agent Servers). For details on enabling client runtime transaction shadowing, see Cluster Server Options . -->

TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem Top TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. But, if the retry also fails then either Adroit has a bug or has been incorrectly configured. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: Backup your database (WGP file) Unscan all the tags to that PLC. Save and restart the Agent Server. Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each. Watch for errors, typically by using the Datascope screen of the Driver Monitor. When the problem occurs, you have the error somewhere in your last group of tags. Check that the scan-points, within the group that have just been added have actual addresses in the PLC. Sometimes due to a driver bug, if you read the last register/value in a memory block, the driver tries to read the (invalid) one after it. Verify that is not happening. Note: The above steps only apply if the problem is observed on the datascope as being repeatable, i.e. the

ory block, the driver tries to read the (invalid) one after it. Verify that is not happening. Note: The above steps only apply if the problem is observed on the datascope as being repeatable, i.e. the same driver request causing the same error. -->

Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers Top Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers Networking and security issues most often prevent Adroit clusters from working. Networking: Use the PING command to determine if your clustered Agent Server computers are networked correctly. For instance, in the command prompt, type the following: ping –l 64000 –t partnerServerComputerName If you have a low success rate (many packets being lost or a high round trip time), then your network is the problem, which requires input and action from your I.T. department. Security: Try to copy a file from the one agent server machine, across the network, to the other agent server machine. You should be able to achieve this without being prompted for authentication. If this fails, then your Windows security is not identical on the two machines and needs to be investigated. Other common problems: Different versions of the product on the two machines. To check this, open the Adroit File Version Information utility and ensure that the file versions of the installed files are identical on both computers. Firewalls blocking communication between the clustered Agent Server computers. To test this, isolate the syst

and ensure that the file versions of the installed files are identical on both computers. Firewalls blocking communication between the clustered Agent Server computers. To test this, isolate the system, then switch off the firewalls on both Agent Server computers. If communication is suddenly possible, you need to add the Agent Server process to the allowed programs on both firewalls. Inadequate licensing. Open the Adroit HASP License Reader and verify. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . For more details on clustering Adroit Agent Servers, see Active Clusters Foundation . -->

Troubleshooting Continuous Writing Top Troubleshooting Continuous Writing The Scanning Monitor utility is designed to assist experienced users in fine-tuning the Adroit scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance, by providing an intuitive report-like view of advanced diagnostic information. This utility is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. For details, see Using the Scanning Monitor . However, if after making changes to the scan rates configured for a polled device, you find no perceivable difference, then you may have a stuck continuous output. Since Adroit only sends controls or writes on change, it is possible that a rapidly changing output driven by some logic inside Adroit (example: systeminformation.second) can generate lots of control actions to a PLC. This flood of outputs will seriously affect all polling and is known as a stuck continuous output. Furthermore, since such a problem tag has to be an output, it will have the Output Enable status bit enabled, making it easier to find. To use the Scanning Monitor to locate a stuck continuous output: Launch the Scanning Monitor and connected it to the required Agent Server Select the require

tus bit enabled, making it easier to find. To use the Scanning Monitor to locate a stuck continuous output: Launch the Scanning Monitor and connected it to the required Agent Server Select the required device from topmost Device List . Select each entry in the middle Scan Job List , This will display the scanned tags within each of these jobs in the bottom Tag List . Observe the Output enable column of this tag list and investigate each of the tags that have this bit set within this device to locate the culprit. The tag configuration that causes these continuous outputs is often created quickly to test something and then forgotten about and not removed. Another common cause is when Adroit is used to time synchronise a PLC using a one-second interval, however, this is better achieved by using a 24-hourly digital pulse. -->

Trust Relationships Top Trust Relationships Trust Relationships in Windows specify the domains that this domain trusts, and the domains that are allowed to trust this domain. A trust relationship is a link between two domains, where one domain honors the users of another domain, trusting that other domain to authenticate the logons of its own users. When trust relationships are properly established between the domains of a network, they allow a user to have only one user account in one domain, yet to access the entire network. All the computers on the network can recognise the user account, requiring a user to log on and provide a password only once to access any computer on the network. Trust relationships move the convenience of centralised administration from the domain level to the network level. -->

Type List CSV File Format Top Type List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. The rows in this CSV file are sorted alphabetically and the alarm type name is used as an index, so that the first alarm type name has an index of 0. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: Alarm type: The name for this alarm type, which MUST NOT be duplicated per agent-type. Agent type: The type of agent that this alarm type applies to. Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. This is the sum of all the bit-positions, which are calculated as 2 n , where n is a position from 16 through 31 of the agent status bit as the built-in status bits occupy the positions from 0 to 15. Value : If applicable, this contains the slot value that is shown with the alarm. For instance for Marshal agents this could be dig##.textValue. Alarm off-states: 0 is the normal alarming of bits in the mask, while 1 is the alarm off state. -->

UDT Agent Type Designer Top UDT Agent Type Designer Certain new PLCs optimise their communication performance by consolidating multiple data values into a single User-Defined Type (UDT). Adroit provides the UDT Agent Type Designer to support this new functionality. This utility creates agent types (templates) that duplicate the structure of any UDTs used by your PLCs, by adding properties (basic data types) to them and if necessary to configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. Note : This only supports UDTs that are composed of data types that can be represented by Boolean, Integer, Real, Datetime, String (80 characters or less) and VarString values. Array data types are NOT supported. Since each defined UDT is a separate Adroit agent type, you can add more than one of each UDT to your Adroit installation, as is necessary. Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features Top Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features NASA stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. While many of these improvements are “under-the-hood”, this document aims to describe the new features that these NASA drivers provide and how they can benefit you. Note: The NASA driver DLLs are differentiated from the legacy drivers by being prefixed by a “d_” e.g. d_opcua_cl. Optimised scan tasks Typically when scanning process values to and from Adroit, the legacy drivers would create separate scan jobs for different: Agent types, such as: Analog, Digital, Integer, String, Marshal and Multistate and their Data type formats, such as: longs, words and dwords. This would therefore increase the total number of scan jobs and therefore the overhead required to communicate your process values. For this reason, less than optimum scan rates were typically attained. With NASA drivers, both different Agent types and dat

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: obs and therefore the overhead required to communicate your process values. For this reason, less than optimum scan rates were typically attained. With NASA drivers, both different Agent types and data type formats can co-exist within a single scan job, which ensures that the minimum number of separate transactions transmit the data to and from the front-end devices. This means that you will achieve improved throughput as the communication overhead is kept to an absolute minimum. Improved multi-channel performance Previously, only specific legacy drivers supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio. All NASA drivers provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. When enabled, NASA drivers can support up to 8 channels, which are utilised as-needed to service the required transactions to achieve parallel communication on a single device. Dynamic configuration Legacy drivers would only attempt to reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded. NASA drivers also reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry when the de

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: rom the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded. NASA drivers also reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry when the device is started and/or stopped to make it possible for online or runtime changes to running devices without needing to restart the Agent Server in order for these changes to take effect. Examples of possible runtime changes are adding additional debug information to the Datascope or to correct configuration errors like IP address typos etc. Improved Performance Monitoring NASA drivers provide support for up to 16 new counters that are common amongst all NASA drivers to facilitate their improved debugging and analysis. Demand Scanning Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: and scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spide

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: t demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning t

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY b

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: ed in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the r

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: ubscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server. -->

User Rights Policy Top User Rights Policy The Windows User Rights policy manages the rights granted to groups and user accounts. A right authorises a user to perform certain actions on the system. A user who logs on to an account to which the appropriate rights have been granted can carry out the corresponding actions. When a user does not have appropriate rights, Windows blocks attempts to carry out those actions. Rights apply to the system as a whole and are different from permissions, which apply to specific objects. The rights granted to a group are provided to the members of that group. In most situations, the easiest way to provide rights to a user is to add that user’s account to one of the built-in groups that already possesses the needed rights, rather than by administrating the User Rights policy. -->

text: Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits Top Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits The Analog agent provides extensive monitoring and alarming of its engineering value (the value slot), by providing low-low, low, high, high-high and/or rate of change alarm limits, which when reached set the relevant specific status bit, which can be alarmed. You can use these alarm limits and their deadbands, where applicable to monitor a process value, as follows: Using alarm limits and their deadbands: The Low (the lo slot) and High (the hi slot) inner alarm limits are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. The Low-low (the loLo slot) and High-high (the hiHi slot) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm

red. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm will become inactive (be cleared) once the process value goes past the limit AND through its deadband, if configured. Click here for an illustration: Using the Rate of Change alarm limit: The Rate of Change status bit is set when the difference between any two consecutive engineering values in ONE second exceeds the defined Rate-of-Change limit. Click here for an illustration: In other words, if this is set to 100, the default value, then if the engineering value (the value slot) of this Analog agent changes from 1 to 101 in 1 second then the Rate of Change status bit is set. But if the engineering value takes 2 seconds to change from 1 to 101 then the effective rate of change is (100/2 =) 50 so the Rate of Change status bit is NOT set. This rate of change measurement is independent of the condition of the low-low, low, high and high-high limits. The value change could be the result of a scan (from the front-end device), operator action or an output from another agent. -->

s / commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . ' define the slot index numbers starting at 0 in the same order as defined in adrcusdes Const idx_Start = 0 Const idx_Stop = 1 Const idx_Value = 2 Const idx_Tripped = 3 Const idx_Speed = 4 Const idx_Temperature = 5 Const idx_HighTemperature = 6 ' define the status bit index numbers starting at 16 in the same order as defined in adrcusdes Const idx_TempHiStatus = 16 Const idx_TripStatus = 17 ' define the constant for three seconds Const ThreeSeconds = 0.00003472 ' 1 second = 1 day / (24 hours * 60 minutes * 60 seconds) StartTime = 0 StopTime = 0 Sub OnCompiled() 'global initialisation - called for each agent at startup and whenever this file is saved 'while AS is running ' DriveXYZ has nothing to do End Sub Sub OnLoadComplete() 'agent initialisation - called for each agent at when agent has been loaded from WGP file or 'newly created ' DriveXYZ - make sure that the start and stop controls are OFF Custom

Sub OnLoadComplete() 'agent initialisation - called for each agent at when agent has been loaded from WGP file or 'newly created ' DriveXYZ - make sure that the start and stop controls are OFF Custom.SetSlot idx_Start, 0 Custom.SetSlot idx_Stop, 0 End Sub Sub OnChange(slotid, value) 'agent slot changed - called whenever a putslot has been done into one of this agents slots 'DriveXYZ - do not allow the drive to start if the temperature is too high if (slotid = idx_Start) AND (value = 1) then if (Custom.GetSlot(idx_Temperature) >= Custom.GetSlot(idx_HighTemperature)) then Custom.SetSlot idx_Start, 0 end if end if 'DriveXYZ - if the drive has tripped, set the trip status bit if slotid = idx_Tripped then Custom.SetStatus idx_TripStatus, value = 1 'DriveXYZ - if the temperature is higher than the configured high temperature value, set the 'high temperature status bit if slotid = idx_Temperature then Custom.SetStatus idx_TempHiStatus, value >= Custom.GetSlot(idx_HighTemperature) end if if slotid = idx_HighTemperature then Custom.SetStatus idx_TempHiStatus, Custom.GetSlot(idx_Temperature) >= value end if 'DriveXYZ - if the start slot is on, save the current start time if (slotid = idx_St

lotid = idx_HighTemperature then Custom.SetStatus idx_TempHiStatus, Custom.GetSlot(idx_Temperature) >= value end if 'DriveXYZ - if the start slot is on, save the current start time if (slotid = idx_Start) AND (Value = 1) then StartTime = Now 'DriveXYZ - if the stop slot is on, save the current stop time if (slotid = idx_Stop) AND (Value = 1) then StopTime = Now End Sub Sub OnUpdate(slotid, value) 'agent slot changed - called whenever a tagname type slot receives an update ' DriveXYZ has nothing to do End Sub Sub OnBackground() 'agent background management - called every second 'DriveXYZ - pulse the start and stop slots if (StartTime > 0) AND (Now - StartTime > ThreeSeconds) then Custom.SetSlot idx_Start, 0 StartTime = 0 end if if (StopTime > 0) AND (Now - StopTime > ThreeSeconds) then Custom.SetSlot idx_Stop, 0 StopTime = 0 end if End Sub -->

Versioning WGP Files Top Versioning WGP Files Adroit WGP files from version 6, contain versioning information to provide an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes and to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. Note: In addition to this version information, Adroit WGP files can ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Adroit WGP file structure has been modified to contain this versioning information, as follows: Line 1: This remains unchanged and contains the number of agents stored in the WGP file: SYS=#, where # is the number of agents currently added to this Agent Server. Line 2: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains the version of Adroit : AVER=XYZ, where X is the major version number, Y is the minor version number and Z is the update number, therefore for Adroit 7.0.0, this number will be 700. Note: Th

contains the version of Adroit : AVER=XYZ, where X is the major version number, Y is the minor version number and Z is the update number, therefore for Adroit 7.0.0, this number will be 700. Note: This is especially important for forward compatibility. Line 3: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains a sequential version number: FVER=1 Note: This version number will increment EACH time the WGP file is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Line 4: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains an optional version description for the WGP file, describing the changes made to it since its previous save: DVER= Adroit default configuration. The manner in which this description is specified, depends upon how this WGP file is being saved, as follows: The WGP file is being automatically saved: In this case, the new wgpdescription String slot of the System Information agent, can be used to programmatically provide the required version description instead. WanClient Configurator Top WanClient Configurator Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database that is stored in the database folder . This database stores a list of WanServer(s) and tags whose values are to be fetched or sent to or from each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers. This tag link data is created using the WanClient Configurator, which can be launched from the Open Configurator item of the WanClient File menu, as follows: Configure Servers : This specifies the communication settings of each WanServer and hence the Agent Server resident on this computer. Configure Tag Groups : To assist in the communication of the necessary tag values, the tags are organised into one or more tag groups, which specify the communication settings of any tag that is added to them and are server-specific. For details on possible criteria to use for creating tag groups, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . Configure Tag Links : A tag link or tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server. Note: The data type of the local and the

tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server. Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. However, the WanClient Configurator, is also able to perform the following global communication configuration, which apply to all the WanServers that are being communicated to: Scan bad philosophy configuration : This governs how this WanClient will set its local Agent Server tag bad information, for the tags, whose values it communicates. Agent Server Cluster-specific configuration : This performs cluster-specific configuration, when using a WanClient is used to communicate tag values from a pair of clustered servers. -->

WanClient Contents Top About WanClient Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. Therefore, the WanClient creates and maintains a tag link database that stores a list of WanServer(s), that this WanClient is required to connect to, and a list of the tags whose values are communicated to each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers. Note: This tag link database can be created and maintained using the WanClient Configurator . For details of the post-installation configuration actions that may be required for the WanClient, see Post Installation Configuration or for details on how this and other Wanlink components can be launched, see Launching components . When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty

re assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. The File Menu The View Menu The Diagnostics Menu The Help Menu Quick Start : procedure to access data from an Agent Server over a WAN. Wanlink Components Top Wanlink Components Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). For further details, see General Description . Wanlink is essentially comprised of the following two components: WanServer , which allows Adroit tags (agent.slot) within the Agent Server that is also running on the same computer, to be communicated to one or more remote WanClients, which are typically situated across a WAN (wide area network). This can also be installed to run as a Service within Windows, by using the WanServer Service Setup application, which ensures that the WanServer does not shutdown when the current user logs off. WanClient , which communicates to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of specific local Adroit tags from or to their Agent Servers. These WanServers typically reside on remote computers and are connected by a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN). Note: These components are separate applications, which can be launched separately.
