Wanlink Quickstart Top Wanlink Quickstart Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). For further details, see General Description . In order to gain access to a local Agent Server from a remote Agent Server across a WAN (Wide Area Network) ensure that the following steps are followed: Note1: For ease of explanation the local Agent Server will be known as LOCAL and the remote Agent Server, will be known as REMOTE. Note2: This will assume that the FULL Adroit installation has been installed and that the Agent Servers have already been started on both computers. On the LOCAL computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Server and select it from the list to run the WanServer. On the REMOTE computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Client and select it from the list to run the WanClient. Note: If the Agent Server is not started, then the WanClient application will wait for it and attach to it when it is opened. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, open t

un the WanClient. Note: If the Agent Server is not started, then the WanClient application will wait for it and attach to it when it is opened. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, open the File menu and select the Open Configurator command. In the Configurator dialog do the following: Click the Add Server button to configure the connection settings required to reach the LOCAL computer. (Add as many servers as there are Agent Servers that require data from this computer’s Agent Server.) Click the Add Group button to configure a tag group , for the Select ed Server , that may only contain a subset of the total required Adroit tags, depending upon the requirements of the tags it is to contain e.g. the group type determines if the Adroit tags will be able to be modified by the other Agent Server or not. (Add as many groups as are needed to cater for the Adroit tags that are to be referred to by the selected server i.e. the current Select Server entry.) Click the New Link button to configure a tag link in which an Adroit tag on this computer’s Agent Server (REMOTE in this case) is linked to which Adroit tag on the Agent Server of the computer on the other side of the WAN (

on to configure a tag link in which an Adroit tag on this computer’s Agent Server (REMOTE in this case) is linked to which Adroit tag on the Agent Server of the computer on the other side of the WAN (LOCAL in this case). This link is added to the Select ed Group and also determines the method by which the data between these two Adroit tags is transferred. (Add all the linked tags that meet the criteria of the currently selected group i.e. the current Select Group entry.) Once all the tags have been added to their relevant groups and all the groups have been added to necessary servers, then click OK. Note: This is a once-only configuration, the next time that the WanClient is opened; this step can be skipped, unless alterations or additions need to be made to the configured tag mappings. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, after tag mappings have been configured, open the File menu and click on the Repack command and then open the File menu and click on the Reload command, to avoid stopping and restarting the WanClient. The LOCAL Agent Server will now have access to all the configured tags on the REMOTE Agent Server. Note1: It is possible to configure the WanServer app

to avoid stopping and restarting the WanClient. The LOCAL Agent Server will now have access to all the configured tags on the REMOTE Agent Server. Note1: It is possible to configure the WanServer application to run as a service on the LOCAL computer, so that it start automatically whenever the Agent Server starts up. The WanClient application does not have this facility, as it must be run from within windows. Note2: If the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, then it will automatically start communications. Tip1: Both the WanClient (if using the "/start" command-line parameter) and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Tip2: It is possible to start the WanClient application from an Adroit mimic by using an Execute Command Behaviour, in this case, specify "/start" after wanclient.exe in the "Application name:" field. This will saves the operator from opening WanClient manually each time and because the "/start" command-line parameter is used, will automatically start communicating. -->

What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Top What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Both this amount and the cost of providing this power are agreed between you and your electricity provider, with the condition that if you exceed this amount then you will pay heavy penalties. Your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand in “block” periods (in South Africa these are every 30 minutes) during these peak times. Your monthly electricity bill uses the highest recorded block kVA usage as the kVA for the whole month. In other words, at the end of the billing month you pay the penalty resulting from the largest divergence from your maximum demand for a block period, for the ENTIRE month. For instance, if you exceed your maximum demand in t

metadata.title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?

text: d of the billing month you pay the penalty resulting from the largest divergence from your maximum demand for a block period, for the ENTIRE month. For instance, if you exceed your maximum demand in the first block period of the month, you will pay this penalty for the entire month, even if you turn off your plant at this point! Needless to say, the cost penalties for the excess power are very high and this is why power management is so important. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage. However, it is recommended to automate this monitoring, such as by using an MaxDemand agent, because one mistake can easily exceed your maximum demand limit for the current billing period. For details on how to monitor your maximum demand, see Maximum Demand Quick Start . -->

text: What you can do with agents Top What you can do with agents Adroit is a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. product and as such is primarily concerned with process values, since these are essentially used to supervise and control processes. Like all programs, Adroit has its own terminology or jargon and in this case its jargon applies to how it refers to these process values. For details, see Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values . Adroit is built on a client-server architecture, where the server or Agent Server, is the database that contains the values and the client or User Interface (that is only one of many possible clients) provides the capability of configuring, displaying and manipulating the values. For further details, see About Agent Servers . Adroit provides the following process value (agent-specific) operations: Create the necessary agents to both store your process variables and perform more advanced calculations and manipulations of this data. Communication of process values, this is the primary function of any SCADA, in that it allows you to bring in values from your process, via front-end devices in the field. This allows the process to be supervised, by reading the values and controlled, by writing them back to the field. For details, see Communicating Values . Alarming of values, when values transgress configurable operational limits, an alarm can be created to notify the operator or engineer of this transgression using a variety of methods. IMPORTANT: Existing Adroit and MAPS users require NEW licenses for Adroit 10 or MAPS 4, since the entire licensing mechanism has changed! PLEASE NOTE: Purple HASPs are not supported (they lack the necessary space required by this licensing mechanism). Only the Agent Server and/or SmartUI Server, requires a licence - all the other applications, such as the Designer or Operator etc. do not. text: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility Top Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility The Adtech Licensing Utility allows you to get, view and/or update your Adroit 10 or MAPS 4 product license. Working with the Agent Server Monitor Top Working with the Agent Server Monitor The Agent Server Monitor utility is typically provided for advanced users to diagnose or troubleshoot the Agent Server and its client connections. The information retrieved from the Agent Server is classified into the following tabs: General : this tab shows certain key pieces of information pertaining to the running state of the Agent Server. These include information such as: The number of available channels. The state of the internal subscription buffer. Various memory allocations. Tip: Depending on the installed version this can also displays the loading status of the WGP file, so that it is possible to view this even when running the Agent Server as a service. Channels : this tab shows the state of the Agent Servers communication channels. This includes which channels are currently connected to by a client as well as the state of health of each channel. Tip: This tab is particularly useful in understanding problems to do with remote client connections and quickly shows if the number of allowed channels is insufficient to service the required client connections. This includes values such as CPU usage, memory consumption etc. This information is shown for a user defined time frame and allows analysis of these values over time. Eventlog : this tab shows the data contained in the Windows Application event log pertaining to the Agent Server (similar to the data displayed in the Adroit event viewer). Working with the Health Monitor Service Top Working with the Health Monitor Service The common Health Monitor Service (HealthMonitorService.exe) is installed by all Adroit Technologies applications and it runs in the background and cannot be interacted with directly. Its function is to monitor various significant values of the system (computer) on which these Adroit Technologies applications are running, since these both directly and indirectly affect their performance (their health), such as the CPU load monitoring. This Health Monitor Service creates a Windows EventLog called “HealthMonitorService”, where it logs any related messages. What does it do? At start-up the service attempts to determine which network cards have Power Saving Enabled. At start-up the service will attempt to determine the UAC status of the currently logged on user. The Service will periodically attempt to check the following computer information (every 10 minutes): Total instantaneous CPU Usage as a % Total and available Memory (Physical & Virtual) Drive Information for all drives (Total size and available space) The Service will periodically check specific processes (every 30 seconds) The default processe

metadata.title: Working with the Health Monitor Service

text: d available Memory (Physical & Virtual) Drive Information for all drives (Total size and available space) The Service will periodically check specific processes (every 30 seconds) The default processes are "as.exe", "VIP Designer.exe", "VIP Operator.exe", "VIPServer.exe", "VIPService.exe". However you can add additional processes too - see below for details. The following CPU usages are checked for each process: If the CPU % is higher than 50% of 1 CPU Core it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. If the Memory (Private Bytes) is more than 80% of 1146880000 bytes it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. When a Process has been flagged for higher resolution monitoring, then it is checked every 10 seconds: If the process is still above the thresholds, an event entry is written to the Eventlog indicating the Process ID, Name, Description, Running Time, CPU Usage, Private Bytes & Virtual Bytes. If/when the process has dropped below the thresholds, it will be removed from the higher resolution monitoring. How to add additional processes to be monitored If necessary, you can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service. The configuration file r

metadata.title: Working with the Health Monitor Service

text: the higher resolution monitoring. How to add additional processes to be monitored If necessary, you can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service. The configuration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml Example Configuration Entry to add the Notepad.exe process to the list of monitored processes, add the following to the end of this file, above the </NewDataSet> line: <Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables> How to adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes If necessary, you can adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes to customise them for your typical system performance. The configuration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonit

metadata.title: Working with the Health Monitor Service

text: nfiguration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml In this file, each specified executable allows you to specify the following thresholds, which specify the normal usage values, which if they are consistently exceeded indicates that there may be a problem and hence the Health Monitor Service will log messages in these instances: CPUCoreThresholdPercent : This specifies the maximum percentage of the CPU that this process executable should consistently use in normal operation, above which the Health Monitor Service will provide alerts. PrivateBytesLimit : Private Bytes refer to the amount of memory that the process executable has asked for and is a reasonable approximation of the amount of memory the executable is using. This specifies the maximum amount of memory that this executable should normally use. PrivateBytesThresholdPercent : This specifies the percentage of the specified PrivateBytesLimit that this application executable should normally use above which the Health Monitor Service will provide alerts. -->

text: Working with the SimCSV driver Top Working with the SimCSV driver The SimCSV driver is not a true driver in the sense that it does not communicate to a front-end device; instead, it allows a user to define the required timestamped sequence of integer, real or Boolean values to simulate the scanning or logging of a real-time process value. If necessary, you can also: adjust the time intervals between successive values and/or specify historical values too and, if need be, specify the required quality or status (bad / good) of this value too. The SimCSV driver simply reads in a .CSV file that specifies which of its addresses should be changed in value at whatever time and/or whatever status (quality) should be applied to change in value in order to define the required sequence. Therefore, this driver can be very helpful when testing or demonstrating other agents like the Analog or DBLog agent, that require real world scanning and/or logging of real-time process values. CSV File Structure Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive. The following first three entries are required, but the others entrie

Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive. The following first three entries are required, but the others entries can be omitted: Seq T+x : this specifies how long after the .CSV file was initially loaded (or reloaded) to change the specified address to the specified value. So a value of 0 performs this change in value as soon as the .CSV file is loaded. But any positive value specifies the number of seconds to wait after the .CSV file loads before the specified address is changed to the specified value. IMPORTANT: If this time offset is configured then the order in which the values of the specified addresses are changed are NOT determined by the sequence of rows in the .CSV file, but by the specified time offsets instead! Address : the address (and therefore the applicable data type) to which the specified value will be written. Value : the required value to write to the Address at the specified time. For instance: 0 , DW0 , 1 In this case as soon as the .CSV file is loaded a value of 1 is written to the DW0 address (which is presumably being scanned to an Integer or Real tag). Since when no ti

me. For instance: 0 , DW0 , 1 In this case as soon as the .CSV file is loaded a value of 1 is written to the DW0 address (which is presumably being scanned to an Integer or Real tag). Since when no time is specified then the time of Now is assumed and when no status is provided then a status (quality) of good is assumed. Applicable Addresses Scan an Integer to one of these INDEX addresses either to read the value of the associated internal variable or to perform the associated action at runtime: Integer Address Function Description IN0 (last callback) The time that the last address changed in value. IN1 (Time since start) The time that has elapsed since the .CSV file started. IN2 (Reload csv) Action: reloads the .CSV file of this driver. IN3 (Execute csv) Action: starts processing the .CSV file of this driver. IN4 (Reload and execute) Action: reloads and processes the .CSV file. IN5 (Iteration count) The number of times that the .CSV file has reiterated. Use the following applicable addresses to write a value to an Integer, Real (Analog) or Boolean (Digital) tag: Address Type prefix Min Range Max Range BOOLEAN Tag INTEGER Tag REAL Tag STRING Tag Dataword DW 0 9 - DW0-9 DW0-9 - Data

dresses to write a value to an Integer, Real (Analog) or Boolean (Digital) tag: Address Type prefix Min Range Max Range BOOLEAN Tag INTEGER Tag REAL Tag STRING Tag Dataword DW 0 9 - DW0-9 DW0-9 - Databit DI 0 15 DI0-15 - - - Note: This driver does NOT support the writing of values to String tags. Skipping Optional Parameters If you want to skip one of the optional entries then include the comma and a space as the driver does a fixed lookup. For instance to only specifying the Status, specify TWO successive commas and spaces first: 5 , DW0 , 5 , , ,I Optional Parameters Time offset from seq The sequence time offset can be either a float or an integer value relative to the sequence, meaning that if the sequence is active the time (NOW) is used and the offset, if any, is appended to the active time. This offset can be either positive (future or forward in time) or negative (historical or back in time). For instance: 0,dw0,123 ……………… omitted 0,dw0,123,1 ……………. Time 0 + 1 0,dw0,123,-4 ……………. Time 0 - 4 Instead of the specifying the required number of seconds that are either added or subtracted from the start time when the .CSV file is loaded you can also specify the required timestamp u

. Time 0 - 4 Instead of the specifying the required number of seconds that are either added or subtracted from the start time when the .CSV file is loaded you can also specify the required timestamp using an IEEE754 float string or an OLEDT using the system locale settings. For instance: 0,dw0,123,29/09/2018 12:33:23 …… a specific datetime Fixed Timestamp This column allows you to specify the required timestamp of this change in value that uses the locale settings of the computer on which this is run. For instance: 4 , DW0 , 4 , , 1993/01/01 12:33:24 Status (Quality) The status (quality) that the system will apply to this update, which may or may not override the specified timestamp, as follows: [] – Good … Driver will send a {NOW} or {SPECIFIED} timestamp [I , i] – Item bad … Driver will send a {-2} timestamp just for this item [J , j] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [K , k] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} [D , d] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [E , e] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked

2} timestamp with this event… {new method} [D , d] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [E , e] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time, it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now! Special Lines Comments: Lines can be commented out using “//” For instance: //This is a comment Reiteration command The :reiterate command can be specified in the last line of the .CSV file to cause this file to loop around back to the top. For instance: :reiterate Tip: In this case you can query the IN5 address to determine how many times the .CSV file has been repeated. Usage Examples: The following provides a number of CSV rows followed by an explanation of what this means: 0 , DW0 , 123.45 , 0 , I At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW0 with 123.45 with a timestamp of now (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2). IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same t

ow (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2). IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time; it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now! 0 , DW1 , 0 , , 1973/12/3 12:33:45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW1 with 0 with a timestamp of 1973/12/3 12:33:45. 0 , DW2 , 45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW2 with 45 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 1 , DW0 , 123.46 , 1 At start time = T+1, which is now, update DW0 with 123.56 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 2 , DW0 , 123.46 , , , J At start time = T+2, which is now, update DW0 with 123.46 with a timestamp of now (same as index) but the whole job will be marked bad {old method – returning failed (timestamp not overwritten)}. How to use the SimCSV driver Create the required CSV file (see above for detailed instructions). For instance, you can copy the following lines as-is into a text editor and save it as your CSV file in an accessible folder, in this case it was saved as the following .CSV file: D:\test.csv: Simple CSV: Due to the numerous methods provided by the SimCSV dri

text editor and save it as your CSV file in an accessible folder, in this case it was saved as the following .CSV file: D:\test.csv: Simple CSV: Due to the numerous methods provided by the SimCSV driver to create a sequence of timed events, the following lines simulate an Integer value changing between 1 and 10 for a total of 16 seconds: 0 , DW0 , 1 2 , DW0 , 9 4 , DW0 , 2 6 , DW0 , 3 8 , DW0 , 7 10 , DW0 , 5 12 , DW0 , 6 14 , DW0 , 8 16 , DW0 , 2 Advanced CSV: The following lines demonstrate the usage of much of the functionality provided by SimCSV driver and is provided so that you can play around with these various settings, as needed: Note: This how to guide assumes that the .CSV file contains this content. 0 , DW0 , 1 , 0 0 , DW0 , 7 , 1 1 , DW0 , 2 , 40 3 , DW0 , 3 , 1.2 4 , DW0 , 4 , , 1993/01/01 12:33:24 5 , DW0 , 5 , , ,I 6 , DW0 , 6 , , ,I Add a device for the SimCSV driver. For instance in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor, right click the CSV Simulation Driver and select Add device and provide the required 8 character name, in this case MY_SCSV: IMPORTANT: In this case, the status of the device is unhealthy because the test.csv file contains BAD scan j

iver and select Add device and provide the required 8 character name, in this case MY_SCSV: IMPORTANT: In this case, the status of the device is unhealthy because the test.csv file contains BAD scan jobs and that is why its icon is red. Configure this device to specify the required .CSV file: For instance in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor , right click the device, in this case MY_SCSV and select Configure . In the device configuration dialog, browse in the required .CSV file that you have created into the Select csv file field, in this case D:\test.csv. Note: The Device ID simply allows you to run multiple CSV files and to scan additional agents (for instance once all of its available addresses are used). Create and start a Device agent for this device in Adroit . In this case, an Analog agent called MY_ANA was added and scanned to the DW0 address of the MY_SCSV device (that was specified in its test.csv file). Note: When the MY_SCSV device is selected from the Device drop-down list of the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog you are asked it you want to automatically create it, in which case select Yes and then you also need to select the Started radio button to s

ce drop-down list of the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog you are asked it you want to automatically create it, in which case select Yes and then you also need to select the Started radio button to start this device. After specifying the required address for this Analog agent, in this case DW0 then click the Scan button. This will ensure that the value of this Analog agent will be set to the specified values once the simulation begins. Open the Datascope for this device to ensure that there are no communication errors. For instance, in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor , right click the device, in this case MY_SCSV and select Diagnostics , which displays the following dialog: In this case, type a 1 into this window to display the DataScope (in ASCII mode) so you can assess current communication status for this device, which in this case displays the following: This indicates that the specified .CSV file has been successfully loaded (that there were no errors detected when processing all the lines). However this .CSV file needs to be explicitly executed in order to begin the required simulation. IMPORTANT: The .CSV is NOT automatically executed, the device needs to

when processing all the lines). However this .CSV file needs to be explicitly executed in order to begin the required simulation. IMPORTANT: The .CSV is NOT automatically executed, the device needs to be manually configured to do so to start the specified simulation. This is by design, to provide you with total control over when you want your simulation to begin. Start the simulation, by adding an Integer tag and scanning it to the applicable INDEX for this driver as an Output enabled value (check the Output enabled checkbox in the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog BEFORE clicking the Scan button). In this case an Integer tag called START_CSV was created and scanned to the IN4 address (this index address both reloads and processes the .CSV file). Tip: If you forget to check the Output enabled checkbox in the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog BEFORE clicking the Scan button, then click the Unscan button, check this checkbox and then click the Scan button. Edit the value of this Integer agent and set it to a value of 1. In this case, edit the START_CSV Integer agent and change its Value field to 1 and click the OK button. When viewing the Datascope for this driver (which should still

agent and set it to a value of 1. In this case, edit the START_CSV Integer agent and change its Value field to 1 and click the OK button. When viewing the Datascope for this driver (which should still be open) you should see the following: Note: The reason this .CSV file was loaded twice was because in this case IN4 was used which both reloads and executes the .CSV file. Tip: If you want this simulation to automatically repeat the lines of the .CSV then add the :reiterate command to the last line of the .CSV file. -->

Working with the WGP Inspector Top Working with the WGP Inspector This utility inspects the structure of your existing Agent database (.WGP) files. The following functions are provided: Open file… : Loads a new WGP file. Find text… : This provides standard “Find text” functionality, use F3 to “Find Next”. Find O/P enabled : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being "Output Enabled" and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Enabled (STS=) and individual slots (SSTx=). Find O/P initialised : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being “Output Initialise” and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Initialised (STS=) and their individual slots (SSTx=). Datalog file size… : Calculates the total amount of disk space required by LGD and LGI files. HMI compatible? : Click this button to test whether the loaded WGP file is HMI mode compatible (which is if it ONLY contains the agent types supported by HMI mode) and displays the result of this test in a message box. The Errors section, contains the following settings and checks for locating errors in the currently loaded Agent database (.WGP) file: If the Silent mode option is not check

his test in a message box. The Errors section, contains the following settings and checks for locating errors in the currently loaded Agent database (.WGP) file: If the Silent mode option is not checked a message box is displayed for each error that is found. If the Include default logfiles option is checked, this includes datalogs that log to the default log file. Find errors : Finds references to non existent agents/tags in alarm, datalog, device, eventlogging, expression and statistical agents; empty lines; illegal tag names; references to non existent tags; dead datalog agents (tag does not exist or datalog of a datalog). The results of this check are saved in the file “[wgpname].wgpinspectorerrors.csv”. Find dead : Finds boolean, integer, real, analog, digital and multistate agents that are not referred to by the device and/or expression agents. Usage by other agents is not yet supported. Note: Counters and Statistical agents are not checked. The results of this check are saved in the file “wgpname dead.csv”. -->

Write Only Scanning Strategy Top Write Only Scanning Strategy This scanning configuration, should ONLY be used for write only scanning, but is NOT recommended since it does NOT guarantee than the value of the scanned tag will be in sync with its value in the front-end device (PLC). The reason for the existence of this strategy is to stop writes being permanently sent to the process and thereby consuming scanning bandwidth. For details of all the scanning strategies offered, see Scanning Strategies or for further details on the effect of combining the available global and tag-specific scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . Required global scanning settings: ForceOutputs = 0 SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan should NOT be set to 1, if it is see below as to its effect. Required tag-specific scanning settings: Output Enable = 1 Scan Inhibit = 1 Operation of strategy: When the Agent Server is started, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). Note: If SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1, then when the Agent Server is started, The Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the fro

he front-end devices (PLCs). Note: If SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1, then when the Agent Server is started, The Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). When a device stops or starts, the Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs) – this is unhealthy. When the communications have been restored after a device has failed, the Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs) – this is unhealthy. If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed in the Agent Server, this value is written to the front-end device (PLC). If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed externally, the Agent Server does NOT receive this value from the front-end device (PLC) – this is unhealthy. -->

WriteThreadStacksize Top WriteThreadStacksize WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". To change the stack space available for tag write-threads (this only affects output enabled tag writes to front-end devices), add the following registry key and value and set this value to amount of space required (in kilobytes): HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Scanning (REG_)DWORD WriteThreadStacksize = the required amount of space (in kilobytes), this value is 256 KB by default. WARNING This option is not generally required and should ONLY be changed at the direction of the Support Desk. -->

Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry Top Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry After the list of scheduled entries have been modified, such as a new entry has been added or the details of an existing entry have been changed, it is necessary to write this information to the registry. In this way it is not necessary for the Scheduler to remain running in order to schedule the specified entries. This list of entries are written to the registry when the Scheduler is terminated, as follows: either right click on the Scheduler icon, in the tray bar, and select Terminate or by open the Scheduler window and click the Terminate button. Note: Logging off Windows also terminates the Scheduler application. -->
